# Part I: The World

## Chapter 1: Overview of Tirvandor™


### 1.1 World Summary


Tirvandor™ is a world divided---two great continents separated by the
Sundering Sea™, each representing fundamentally different philosophies
of civilization and magic. In the west lies Thaldros™, a militaristic
empire built on order, central authority, and feudal tradition. In the
east sprawls Aethoria™, a confederation of free cities and ancient
forests where independence, democratic ideals, and harmony with nature
reign supreme.

Between these continental powers stretch the Contested Lands---war-torn
frontiers where neither power holds sway, and adventurers find both
opportunity and danger in equal measure. The current year is 1247 CR
(Common Reckoning), with Year 0 marking the catastrophic Worldrend™ that
tore the continents apart and reshaped civilization itself.

The world's total estimated population stands at two to three million
sentient beings spread across all settlements and nomadic groups. The
climate ranges from temperate to subtropical across most inhabited
regions, with significant magical saturation in natural areas and
moderate levels in settled regions.

\column

### 1.2 Fundamental Nature


Tirvandor is defined by several essential characteristics that shape all
aspects of life within its borders.

**Grounded Realism:** While magic exists and profoundly shapes the
world, Tirvandor emphasizes realistic consequences, political
complexity, and morally gray choices. Heroes are not always virtuous,
villains may possess legitimate grievances, and every decision carries
weight that echoes through time.

**Natural Magic:** Magic flows through ley lines---ancient channels of
power that crisscross the world like invisible rivers beneath the earth.
Where these lines intersect, they create nodes of particular power.
Spellcasters who understand these currents can amplify their abilities,
though the lines also create areas of wild magic and unpredictable
effects that have shaped civilization's development.

**Political Intrigue:** The great powers of Tirvandor---kingdoms, noble
houses, merchant guilds, and secret societies---all pursue their own
agendas with ruthless determination. Webs of alliance and betrayal
connect every center of power, and the actions of individuals can
reshape the political landscape of nations.

**Historical Depth:** Tirvandor possesses a rich history spanning over
sixteen thousand years, from the Age of Myth through the devastating
Worldrend to the present day. Ancient ruins dot the landscape, lost
civilizations whisper secrets through crumbling stones, and lingering
curses tie the present to the deep past in ways both subtle and
profound.

## Chapter 2: Geography


### 2.1 The Sundering Sea


The vast ocean that separates the two continents of Tirvandor serves as
both highway and barrier between worlds. Ancient mariners claim it was
created in a cataclysm millennia ago when the continents were torn apart
by warring primordial forces---an event now known as the Worldrend. The
waters run deep, prone to violent storms, and unpredictable in ways that
command respect from sailors and fear from the superstitious.

**The Deep Trenches** plunge to unknown depths where strange magical
currents flow, creating conditions unlike anything found elsewhere in
Tirvandor's waters. Sailors who claim to have glimpsed these abyssal
chasms speak of lights that should not exist and shadows that move
against the current.

**The Storm Belts** are semi-predictable regions of violent weather that
shift with the seasons. Experienced navigators chart their movements
carefully, for those caught unprepared within a Storm Belt rarely return
to tell of it.

**The Singing Waters** occupy certain areas where the waves produce
haunting melodies, said by some to be the songs of drowned civilizations
calling to those above. Whether this phenomenon is magical residue from
the Worldrend or something older remains a matter of scholarly debate.

**The Trade Winds** provide reliable currents that have enabled commerce
between the continents for centuries. These predictable channels of
favorable sailing represent the lifeblood of intercontinental trade and
have shaped the development of port cities on both shores.

\column

{{margin-top:350px}}

### 2.2 The Island Chains


Between and around the two great continents lie numerous islands and
archipelagos. These scattered lands serve as stepping stones for trade,
havens for pirates and outcasts, and homes to unique cultures that blend
influences from both Thaldros and Aethoria. The total number of islands
is estimated at over one hundred, though fewer than twenty support
permanent settlements.

#### The Splintered Isles (Western Islands)


Located off the western coast of Thaldros, these islands bear the brunt
of storms coming off the Sundering Sea. Despite harsh conditions, they
possess significant strategic value for both trade and military
purposes.

**Stormwatch Isle** is home to the Stormwatchers, weather-mages who have
dedicated their lives to predicting storms and warning ships of
approaching danger. Their forecasts are considered invaluable by any
captain crossing the Sundering Sea.

**Saltmere** is a tropical island renowned for its extensive salt flats
and thriving pearl diving industry. The wealth extracted from its waters
has made it a prize worth fighting over throughout history.

**Western Haven** has earned its reputation as a pirate haven and
smuggler's port, where those who operate outside the law find
sanctuary---for the right price.

#### The Drifting Chain (Central Archipelago)


The islands between Thaldros and Aethoria are crucial for maritime trade
and have developed their own distinct culture---a unique blend of
eastern and western influences that belongs wholly to neither continent.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page

**Isla Myrthen** hosts **Port Myrthen**, the largest settlement in the
archipelago with a population approaching nine thousand souls. This
cosmopolitan trading port serves as neutral ground where goods from both
continents exchange hands freely. Known for its relaxed attitude toward
laws and deliberately neutral political stance, Port Myrthen is home to
the Merchant's Guild headquarters and operates under a "no questions
asked" policy that attracts both legitimate traders and those with
goods to hide.

The Drifting Chain also includes **Midway**, a village serving as the
halfway point for continental crossings; **Coral Bay**, a pearl diving
community; and **Trader's Rest**, a resupply station for ships making
the long voyage between continents. Several smaller islets serve
primarily as navigation markers for vessels threading through the
archipelago.

#### The Shattered Arc (Eastern Islands)


Located near Aethoria's fractured coast, these islands share the
mystical character of the eastern continent. Many are sacred sites or
home to isolated communities seeking spiritual enlightenment.

**Thornhaven** is a mysterious island shrouded in perpetual mist, home
to a reclusive order of monks who study the boundary between life and
death. Its population of approximately eighteen hundred souls lives in
contemplative isolation.

**Emerald Isle** is a lush tropical paradise considered a sacred druidic
site, where the boundaries between the material world and realms of
nature spirits grow thin.

**Serpent's Tooth** is a rocky island that serves primarily as a
lighthouse and naval outpost, guiding ships through the treacherous
waters of the eastern approaches.

#### The Northern Islands


**Frostwatch** and its surrounding settlements provide harbor services
in the harsh northern seas. Primarily inhabited by humans and half-orcs,
these communities survive through fishing, seal hunting, and their
strategic naval positioning along northern trade routes.

#### The Southern Islands


Scattered tropical islands south of both continents remain largely
unmapped and unexplored. Persistent rumors speak of lost civilizations,
hidden treasures, and dangerous creatures lurking in these warm waters,
though few expeditions return with concrete evidence.

### 2.3 Thaldros (Western Continent)


The Western Continent, called Thaldros by its inhabitants, is a land of
dramatic contrasts---snow-capped mountains give way to arid deserts,
which transition into temperate woodlands. The continent bears scars of
ancient conflicts, with ruins dotting the landscape and ley lines
running through its heart like veins of magical power.

**Capital:** Kaer Thandros (Population approximately 45,000)

**Major Cities:** Ironhold, Silverpine, Goldreach, Crossvale, Sundara,
Ashgate

**Total Settlements:** Approximately 120 towns, villages, and hamlets

#### The Frostmarches (Far North)


The frozen northern reaches of Thaldros represent the edge of habitable
land, where winter reigns for nine months of the year. Ice fields,
tundra, and frozen coastline dominate a landscape of harsh beauty. The
aurora borealis dances in winter skies, and locals claim they can hear
voices in the lights---the souls of great warriors, they say, singing
from beyond.

The climate is arctic to sub-arctic, with extreme cold that tests the
limits of survival. Blizzards sweep across the land without warning, and
the dangers include not only the weather but frost giants, ice demons,
and the rare but terrifying white dragon. Yet the Frostmarches offer
valuable resources: furs, walrus ivory, ice crystals with magical
properties, and whale oil for lamps and heating.

The population remains very sparse---only the hardiest humans and
goliaths make their homes here. The people of the Frostmarches are
survivors above all else. They hunt seals, fish through ice holes, and
trade furs and ivory with southern merchants. Communities are tight-knit
because survival depends on cooperation. Hospitality is considered
sacred; turning away a traveler in winter is viewed as tantamount to
murder.

**Major Settlements** include Frostholm (a town of 2,500 for ice fishing
and seal hunting), Northwatch (a mountain pass guard post of 2,200 that
warns of giant incursions), and Iceridge (a high-altitude mining town of
1,800 known for ice crystals with magical properties).

#### The Ironspine Holds (Mountains)


A formidable mountain range dominates the northern reaches of Thaldros.
The Ironspine Mountains are rich in mineral wealth but deadly in their
beauty. Ancient dwarven settlements tunnel deep into these peaks, though
many have been abandoned for centuries, their halls echoing with
memories of former glory. The mountains are home to rare magical ore
veins that glow faintly at night, drawing miners and treasure-seekers
despite the dangers.

The climate is alpine with harsh winters and brief summers. Avalanches,
wyverns, frost giants, extreme cold, and cave-ins all threaten those who
venture into these heights. Yet the resources justify the risk: iron,
silver, mythril ore, rare gemstones, and crystal formations of
extraordinary purity.

Dwarven culture dominates the Ironspine. Clan loyalty supersedes all
other bonds, and craftsmanship is considered the highest calling. The
great halls of the dwarven holds are wonders of engineering---cities
carved from living stone where the sound of hammers on anvils never
ceases. Non-dwarves are tolerated in

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page
trading posts but rarely welcomed deeper into the mountain kingdoms.

**Major Settlements** include Kaer Thandros itself, the great mountain
fortress-city built into living rock that serves as both capital of
Thaldros and center of metalcraft and rune work; Ironhold (population
8,000), a heavily fortified town guarding the Northern Pass; Deepforge
(population 3,500), a deep mining town with volcanic forges primarily
inhabited by dwarves; and Stonehaven (population 2,800), a quarry town
with ancient ruins nearby.

**Notable Locations** include the Crown Forge in Kaer Thandros, capable
of creating permanent magical items; the Echo Halls, an abandoned dwarf
hold with strange acoustic anomalies; and the Crystal Caverns below
Crystalmine, where crystal golems guard treasures untouched for
centuries.

#### The Shattered Shore (Northeast Coast)


The northeastern coast is a jagged, broken shoreline of cliffs, rocky
beaches, and hidden coves. Constant winds from the Sundering Sea create
dramatic waves that crash against the rocks with thunderous force.
Numerous shipwrecks dot the coastline, providing salvage opportunities
for the daring and cautionary tales for the wise.

The climate is temperate coastal with frequent storms. The dangers
include not only the treacherous waters but sahuagin raids from the deep
and ghost ships that appear without warning on moonless nights. The
sparse population consists primarily of fishing communities and sailor
outposts, people who have learned to read the moods of the sea and
respect its power.

#### The Silverwood (Central Forest)


The Silverwood is an ancient forest of silver birch and oak trees, where
dappled sunlight creates ever-shifting patterns on the forest floor.
Unlike the wild forests of Aethoria, the Silverwood has been carefully
managed for generations---thinned, cultivated, and respected by those
who live within and around it. It is a place of beauty and tranquility,
though old magic still runs deep beneath the roots.

The climate is temperate with four distinct seasons. Bandits, fey
creatures, occasional monsters, and the legendary wild hunts pose
threats to travelers, but the forest provides abundant resources: timber
(especially the prized silver birch), wild herbs, mushrooms, and
venison.

The people of the Silverwood value balance between civilization and
nature. Woodcutters follow strict codes about which trees may be
harvested. Hunters observe seasons and quotas. Druids maintain sacred
groves, and their counsel is sought in matters affecting the forest. It
is a place where progress and preservation have found uneasy but
functional harmony.

**Major Settlements** include Silverpine (population 32,000), a
prosperous city built among ancient silver birch groves known for its
Magical Academy and artisan guilds; Oakenheart (population 3,200), a
forest town renowned for woodworking with a druid circle nearby; and
Willowbrook (population 2,600), a riverside town featuring waterwheel
mills and paper production.

**Notable Locations** include the Silverpine Magical Academy, famous
across both continents for both magical and mundane learning; and the
Old Oak Circle, an ancient druid site marked by standing stones.

#### The Heartlands (Central Plains)


The Heartlands are the agricultural engine of Thaldros---endless fields
of grain, pastures dotted with livestock, and prosperous farming
communities connected by well-maintained roads. This is the most
"civilized" part of the continent, crisscrossed by trade routes and
dotted with market towns where the rhythms of planting and harvest
dictate the pace of life.

The climate is temperate and ideal for agriculture. While bandits lurk
along lesser roads, occasional monster incursions threaten outlying
farms, and feudal disputes sometimes turn violent, the dangers here are
manageable compared to the frontier regions. The resources are the
foundation of Thaldrosian prosperity: grain, livestock, wool, leather,
and processed food that feeds the entire continent.

Heartland culture represents "normal" medieval life---feudal
structure, seasonal rhythms dictated by farming, strong community bonds,
and traditional values. People here are pragmatic and hardworking,
somewhat provincial in outlook. They view mountain-dwellers as eccentric
and desert-folk as exotic. Magic is tolerated but viewed with suspicion
by the common folk.

**Major Settlements** include Crossvale (population 18,000), located at
the junction of five major roads with a massive market district and
heavy fortifications; Riverdale (population 4,200), an agricultural hub
for grain processing and river trade; Grainhaven (population 3,800),
surrounded by wheat fields stretching to every horizon; Millford
(population 2,900), producing flour for the entire region; Fairhaven
(population 3,400), hosting a quarterly fair that draws crowds from
across Thaldros; and Highfield (population 2,700), an elevated plateau
town known for sheep herding.

**Notable Locations** include Crossvale Market Square, the largest
market in the region where everything can be bought or sold; and the
Standing Stones, an ancient monument of unknown origin where strange
lights appear during solstices.

#### The Goldcoast (Western Shore)

The western coast of Thaldros is blessed with natural harbors, sandy
beaches, and a climate moderated by ocean currents. This is where
Thaldros meets the Sundering Sea, making it the gateway for trade
between continents. Coastal towns have grown wealthy from maritime
commerce, and the smell of salt and opportunity hangs perpetually in the
air.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page

The climate is temperate coastal with mild winters. Pirates, storms, and
sea monsters pose threats to shipping, but the rewards of trade make the
risks worthwhile. The resources here are the goods of commerce itself:
trade goods from across the world, ships, and fish.

Coastal culture is more cosmopolitan than inland Thaldros. Sailors bring
news and exotic goods from distant lands, and the population includes
immigrants from across Tirvandor. Locals are traders and
sailors---practical, shrewd, and deeply superstitious about the sea.
Social mobility is higher here than elsewhere; wealth matters more than
birth, and a clever merchant can rise higher than a minor noble.

**Major Settlements** include Goldreach (population 28,000), the largest
port on western Thaldros and primary gateway for ocean trade, featuring
the famous Golden Harbor district and the Lighthouse of Eternal Flame;
Saltmere (population 2,400), known for salt harvesting and fish
preservation; Harborview (population 2,800), specializing in
shipbuilding and naval supplies; and Westport (population 1,500), an
unofficial smuggler haven.

#### The Sundaran Expanse (Desert)


The southern reaches of Thaldros transform into a vast desert---the
Sundaran Expanse. Golden sand dunes stretch to the horizon, broken by
rocky outcroppings and the occasional life-giving oasis. Beneath the
sand lie the ruins of ancient civilizations that flourished before
climate shifts turned fertile land to barren waste.

The climate is arid with extreme temperature swings between scorching
days and freezing nights. Sandstorms, giant scorpions, sand elementals,
dehydration, and the dangers of buried ruins all threaten travelers. Yet
the desert offers its own treasures: exotic spices, rare herbs, ancient
artifacts, and desert glass formed by lightning strikes on sand.

Desert people are divided between nomadic tribes who move with the
seasons and permanent oasis dwellers who tend the precious water
sources. Nomads are skilled navigators, using stars and subtle landscape
features to cross trackless dunes. They are hospitable to travelers who
approach correctly but wary of those who show disrespect. Oasis
settlements serve as cosmopolitan trading posts where cultures mix and
ancient traditions persist.

**Major Settlements** include Sundara (population 18,000), the jewel of
the desert built around the Great Oasis and serving as a center for
exotic goods trade with a famous glass bazaar; Sandstone (population
2,600), a caravan stop built entirely from local sandstone; Oasis Rest
(population 2,100), a vital water source along trade routes; Southwatch
(population 1,700), a border fortress and desert trade checkpoint; and
Borderkeep (population 1,200), the southernmost fortification.

**Notable Locations** include the Great Oasis, the largest water source
in the desert whose mysterious well never runs dry; the Whispering
Dunes, where voices speak in the wind; and the Glass Valley, an entire
valley floor of fused glass from some ancient cataclysm.

#### The Ashfall Barrens (Volcanic Southeast)


The southeastern region of Thaldros is a land of fire and ash---a
volcanic wasteland where the earth seethes with heat and the ground
itself cannot be trusted. Active and dormant volcanoes dot the
landscape, and rivers of lava create temporary lakes of molten rock that
reshape the terrain without warning.

The climate is volcanic and unpredictable, with toxic gases that can
kill without warning. Volcanic eruptions, lava flows, fire elementals,
and poisonous fumes all threaten those who venture here. Yet the region
offers unique resources: obsidian, volcanic glass, metals found nowhere
else, sulfur, and fire gems that burn with eternal flame.

Those who live in the Ashfall Barrens have adapted to conditions that
would kill outsiders. They build with black stone that resists heat,
channel volcanic warmth for forging, and know which warning signs
precede eruptions. They are tough, practical people who view their harsh
homeland as a crucible that burns away weakness.

**Major Settlements** include Ashgate (population 12,000), built on the
edge of the volcanic region with black stone architecture and a famous
hot springs district; Cinderfall (population 2,300), built on an old
lava flow and known for obsidian mining; Emberforge (population 2,800),
a smithing town that uses volcanic heat for legendary metalwork;
Eastmarch (population 2,500), an eastern frontier town engaged in
volcanic glass trade; Ashford (population 2,200), a crossroads in the
volcanic region; and Flamekeep (population 1,900), a fire temple complex
where an eternal flame burns without fuel.

**Notable Locations** include the Eternal Forge in Emberforge, which
uses volcanic heat for legendary smithing; the Black Spire, an
impossibly smooth obsidian formation that defies explanation; and
Hellmouth Crater, the largest active volcano in the region.

#### The Reaching Claws (Eastern Badlands)


A transitional badlands region between the Heartlands and Ashfall
Barrens, the Reaching Claws takes its name from the claw-like formations
of volcanic rock that reach across the landscape. This is dangerous
frontier country full of opportunity and peril in equal measure.

The climate is varied but generally dry and rocky. Monsters roam freely,
bandits prey on travelers, and geological instability makes even the
ground treacherous. Yet the region offers monster parts for alchemists
and wizards, volcanic minerals, and salvage from those who came before
and failed.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page

Frontier mentality dominates here. People who settle in the Reaching
Claws are refugees, outcasts, adventurers, or those seeking fresh starts
where their past cannot follow. Law is what each community decides it
is. Everyone is armed, everyone is cautious, and everyone helps during
monster attacks---because monsters are common enough that cooperation is
survival.

### 2.4 Thaldros Climate Patterns


Thaldros experiences distinct seasonal changes across its varied
terrain. The Ironspine Mountains create a rain shadow effect that
contributes significantly to the Sundaran Expanse's
aridity---moisture-laden clouds from the sea drop their rain on the
western slopes, leaving little for the lands beyond.

The Heartlands receive moderate rainfall year-round, supporting the
agricultural productivity that feeds the continent. The Goldcoast enjoys
mild winters moderated by ocean currents, while the Frostmarches endure
nine months of winter with only brief, cool summers.

The Ashfall Barrens create their own weather patterns, with heat rising
from volcanic vents affecting air currents for miles around. The
Silverwood's ancient trees moderate temperature extremes, creating a
stable microclimate that has persisted for centuries.

### 2.5 Aethoria (Eastern Continent)


The Eastern Continent, known as Aethoria, is a land of deep magic and
ancient growth. Where Thaldros is marked by human ambition and dramatic
geography, Aethoria is characterized by primordial forests, mysterious
swamps, and a profound connection to the natural world. The very air
feels thicker here, saturated with magical energy that has shaped
evolution and culture alike.

**Capital:** Aethermere (Population approximately 38,000)

**Major Cities:** Starfall, Crystalbrook, Wildgrove, Marshaven,
Thornhaven

**Total Settlements:** Approximately 84 towns, villages, and hamlets

#### The Starwood (Northwest)


Ancient forests of tremendous age where massive star-trees grow so tall
their canopies seem to touch the heavens. The wood glows faintly at
night, and celestial events have unusual effects here---meteor showers
are brighter, eclipses last longer, and the stars themselves seem closer
than they should be. The elves claim this is because the trees
themselves are blessed by celestial forces.

The climate is that of a temperate rainforest, often misty and cool.
Ancient guardians patrol the forest depths, fey courts hold power in
hidden glades, and disorienting magic can turn travelers in circles for
days. The resources include starwood timber prized across both
continents, astral herbs with powerful magical properties, and star iron
from fallen meteors.

The Starwood is primarily elven territory, inhabited by wood elves and
moon elves whose culture predates human civilization on Aethoria. They
live in harmony with the forest, building homes among the branches and
on the forest floor. Outsiders are viewed with suspicion unless they
show proper respect for nature. Decisions are made by consensus in elven
councils, druids advise on matters affecting the natural world, and age
grants authority---for elves can live over seven hundred years.

**Major Settlements** include Starfall (population 6,500), an
observatory city built in a meteor impact clearing where frequent meteor
falls provide materials for cosmic magic; Moonwatch (population 4,200),
an elven settlement home to moon druids who study the celestial cycles;
and Shimmerleaf (population 2,800), a fey-touched village where the
boundary between worlds grows thin.

**Notable Locations** include Starfall City, where cosmic magic
concentration affects reality itself; and the Moon Well, a sacred pool
that reflects the moon perfectly even in daylight and grants visions to
those who drink from it.

#### The Crystalvale (North-Central)


A network of pristine lakes and rivers with crystalline waters forms the
largest freshwater lake system on Aethoria. The water here is so pure it
can be used for scrying without magical enhancement. Underground springs
feed the surface water, creating a network of waterways that sparkle
like gems under sunlight.

The climate is temperate with abundant rainfall. Lake monsters lurk in
the depths, water elementals guard certain springs, and flash floods can
catch the unwary. The resources include freshwater fish, scrying-quality
water prized by diviners, and water crystals that form naturally in
underground caves.

The Crystalvale is cosmopolitan by Aethorian standards. Humans, elves,
halflings, and others coexist peacefully, united by their reverence for
water. Water is central to life here---religiously, economically, and
socially. Water mages practice their craft openly, and scrying services
are a major export. People are generally friendly, educated, and
sophisticated, governed by elected councils and powerful scrying guilds.

**Major Settlements** include Crystalbrook (population 12,000), a trade
hub on the Great Crystal Lake with crystal towers that reflect sunlight
for miles and underground crystal caves; and Clearwater (population
3,800), known for fishing, boat-building, and bottled water trade.

**Notable Locations** include the Crystal Caves, a natural cavern system
with magically resonant formations; and the Mirror Lake, perfectly still
waters used for prophetic scrying that occasionally shows parallel
timelines.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page

#### The Fractured Coast (Northwest Shore)


The western shore of Aethoria is a broken coastline of islands, coves,
and hidden bays---a maze of small islands, hidden coves, and treacherous
reefs where thick fog is common and navigation treacherous. The region
bears the scars of the Worldrend most clearly. This "fractured" nature
makes it perfect for those seeking to hide, and pirates, smugglers, and
outcasts have operated here for centuries.

The climate is coastal temperate and frequently foggy. Pirates and
coastal raiders threaten shipping, storms arise without warning, and
ghost ships appear on moonless nights. The resources include fish,
salvage from countless wrecks, and sea-spray crystals that form on
certain rocks.

Communities here are insular and independent. Each island has its own
culture, often distrusting even nearby islands. Piracy and smuggling are
open secrets---most coastal towns have "arrangements" with
freebooters. Life is hard, and loyalty is to family and crew, not
distant governments.

**Major Settlements** include Haven's Rest (population 5,500), a port
city that serves as the gateway to the fractured coast.

#### The Emerald Deeps (Central-West)


The heart of Aethoria's ancient rainforests, the Emerald Deeps are
primordial woods so old and dense that entire ecosystems exist in the
canopy, with creatures born, living, and dying without ever touching the
ground. The trees grow to impossible heights, their canopies forming
multiple layers. The forest floor is dim even at noon, filled with
ferns, fungi, and undergrowth. The magic here is old, deep, and
sometimes hostile to civilization.

The climate is tropical rainforest with year-round humidity. Dire
predators hunt through the undergrowth, territorial fey defend their
domains, disorientation magic turns travelers in circles, and wild magic
can produce unpredictable effects. The resources are correspondingly
valuable: rare herbs, sacred woods, magical plants, and alchemical
reagents found nowhere else.

Multiple cultures coexist in the Emerald Deeps, often unaware of each
other. Elven tree-cities exist in the canopy. Druidic circles maintain
sacred groves. Tribal communities live in harmony with beasts. Human
settlements cling to the forest edges. All share one fundamental belief:
the forest must be respected. Druids hold ultimate authority here, for
they are servants of nature itself.

**Major Settlements** include Aethermere (population 38,000), the
capital of Aethoria built among the world-trees where the city grows
organically from the trees themselves; and Fernwatch (population 3,200),
a forest guardian outpost.

**Notable Locations** include Wildgrove, a druidic sanctuary built
around world-trees containing a library of natural lore; the Heartwood
Grove, ancient trees thousands of years old at the center of the
forest's consciousness where visitors report time distortion; and the
Underbough, the forest floor region of perpetual twilight with
bioluminescent fungi and rarely-explored ruins.

#### The Brightwater Valley (Central)


A fertile river valley where the greatest concentration of Aethorian
agriculture exists. The rivers here sparkle with natural magic, making
crops grow larger and faster than anywhere else. Rice paddies stretch
across valley floors, terraced hillsides support other crops, and the
region has a gentle, pastoral quality unusual for Aethoria.

The climate is temperate and mild year-round. River pirates, bandits,
and occasional monsters from surrounding regions pose threats, but the
dangers are manageable. The resources include grain, fruit, vegetables,
and magical produce enhanced by the waters.

Valley folk are farmers, fishermen, and craftspeople who have learned to
work with nature rather than against it. They flood rice paddies
annually, rotate crops carefully, and maintain good relations with local
nature spirits. It is perhaps the most peaceful region in Aethoria.

**Major Settlements** include Riverrun (population 4,500), a market town
at the confluence of several rivers; and Harvest Hall (population
3,800), an agricultural center.

#### The Mistwood Reaches (Northeast)


Highlands covered in perpetual mist and ancient pines, the Mistwood
Reaches have a haunting beauty that draws mystics, seers, and those who
study the veil between worlds. The fog here is thick, magical, and
sometimes sentient. Travelers report the mist showing visions, leading
them astray, or protecting them from danger.

The climate consists of cool temperate highlands with perpetual mist.
Will-o'-wisps lead travelers to their doom, hags lurk in hidden
hollows, shadow creatures hunt in the fog, and the terrain itself is
treacherous. The resources include rare fungi, ghost orchids, and
mist-touched timber with unusual properties.

Those who live in the Mistwood are either adapted to its strangeness or
actively seeking it. Mystics, seers, and those who study the boundary
between material world and Feywild make their homes here. Communities
are small, isolated, and often secretive.

**Major Settlements** include Mistview (population 3,500), a highland
town where fog-navigation is a required skill.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page

#### The Thornmire Marches (South-Central)


Vast wetlands where water and land blur together, the Thornmire Marches
form a maze of swamps, bogs, and bayous rich in unique resources but
deadly to the unprepared. The "solid" ground is actually floating mats
of vegetation. Trees grow from the water itself, their roots forming
tangles above the surface. The air is thick, hot, and alive with
insects.

The climate is subtropical swamp, humid and warm year-round. Venomous
creatures, disease, quicksand, hostile denizens, and toxic plants all
threaten intruders. The resources include rare poisons, medicinal
plants, exotic leathers, and swamp gas with alchemical applications.

Swamp-dwellers are hardy, independent, and resourceful. Humans,
lizardfolk, and others have adapted to the environment. They navigate by
boat, build on stilts, and know which plants are edible versus deadly.
Outsiders are viewed with suspicion---many who enter the swamp never
leave.

**Major Settlements** include Marshaven (population 8,000), a fortified
stilt-city known for alchemical trade built on platforms above the
waters; and Bogrest (population 2,200), a swamp village.

#### The Singing Fens (Southeast)


Southern wetlands where unusual acoustic properties make the swamp
"sing" with wind and water, the Singing Fens are more hospitable than
the Thornmire but still treacherous for the unwary.

The climate consists of warm wetlands with musical winds that give the
region its name. Territorial lizardfolk defend their domains, poisonous
flora dots the landscape, and sink holes can swallow the unwary. The
resources include reed instruments, singing crystals with acoustic
properties, and medicinal mud.

**Major Settlements** include Reedwatch (population 2,800), a marsh
town.

#### The Verdant Wall (Southern Mountains)


A mountain range covered in jungle growth; the Verdant Wall differs
dramatically from the barren peaks of Thaldros. These mountains are
alive with vegetation from base to summit, draped in tropical growth
that makes them appear more like enormous green hills than traditional
peaks.

The climate is tropical mountain, varying significantly by elevation.
Territorial apes, giant insects, landslides, and hidden predators all
pose dangers. The resources include tropical hardwoods, rare orchids,
and mountain herbs found only at specific elevations.

**Major Settlements** include Highgrove (population 3,200), a mountain
settlement.

#### The Split Peninsula (Southwest)


The southwestern peninsula appears torn from Thaldros' Reaching Claws,
as if the Worldrend literally ripped the land apart. Dramatic cliffs,
hidden coves, and a wild frontier feeling define this region where
pirates find harbor and druids guard ancient groves.

The climate is coastal subtropical. Pirates, storms, territorial druids,
and cliff creatures all pose threats. The resources include fish, rare
shells, sea caves, and occasionally pirate treasures.

**Major Settlements** include Wildgrove (population 5,000), a druidic
sanctuary that serves as neutral ground for nature worship; and
Thornhaven (population 1,800), an island monastery.

### 2.6 Aethoria Climate Patterns


Aethoria experiences less seasonal variation than Thaldros, with the
climate generally warmer and wetter. The continent's forests create
their own weather patterns, and some areas experience localized magical
climate effects that defy natural explanation.

The Verdant Wall mountains trap moisture from the sea, creating the
ultra-humid environment of the western forests while leaving the
Brightwater Valley relatively mild. The Emerald Deeps generate their own
rainfall through transpiration from the massive trees, creating a
self-sustaining cycle that has persisted since before recorded history.

### 2.7 The Contested Lands


While technically part of Thaldros, several regions exist where Crown
authority is nominal at best. These "Contested Lands" or frontier
territories operate semi-independently, governed by local strongmen,
merchant councils, or guild law rather than royal decree.

These regions share common characteristics: limited royal tax
collection, no permanent Crown military presence, local justice systems
(often harsh), and service as havens for those fleeing royal law.
Mercenary guilds often maintain what order exists, and the distinction
between law enforcement and protection racket can be academic.

#### The Reaching Claws


The southwestern badlands peninsula, where volcanic terrain and distance
from Kaer Thandros make royal control impractical. Settlements here
answer to whoever can enforce their will---which changes frequently.

#### The Deep Frontier


Remote settlements in the Silverwood's western reaches, where logging
camps and mining outposts operate under guild law rather than Crown law.
The forest itself provides cover for those who wish to disappear.

#### The Border Marches

The transitional zone between the Heartlands and the Reaching Claws,
where "frontier justice" is the norm and mercenary towns have sprung
up to service those operating outside normal society. Crossroads
(population 2,400) is the largest of these---a lawless 

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page

mercenary town at the junction of three trade routes, governed by the Iron Guild where
violence is common but regulated.

**Political Significance:** The Crown periodically attempts to bring
these regions under control, while frontier leaders resist
centralization. This ongoing tension creates opportunities for
mercenaries, adventurers, and those seeking to profit from
instability---and ensures these regions remain dangerous but profitable
for those bold enough to operate there.

### 2.8 Cultural Geography


The geography of Tirvandor has shaped distinct cultural zones across
both continents:

**Mountain Folk (Thaldros):** Dwarves, goliaths, and hardy humans
inhabiting the Ironspine region, focused on mining and craftsmanship.
They value clan loyalty, skilled work, and endurance above all.

**Plains Dwellers (Central Thaldros):** Primarily humans organized into
feudal kingdoms, focused on agriculture and trade. They follow
traditional values, respect social hierarchy, and observe the rhythms of
planting and harvest.

**Desert Nomads (Sundaran Wastes):** Mixed races who have adapted to
desert life, maintaining ancient traditions passed down through
generations. They navigate by stars and respect the harsh beauty of
their homeland.

\column

**Forest Elves (Aethoria):** Elves and half-elves who live in harmony
with ancient forests, preserving old magic and answering to druidic
councils. They measure time in centuries and view the forest as a living
entity deserving respect.

**Swamp Folk (Thornmire):** Lizardfolk, humans, and half-orcs who have
adapted to wetland life. They are resourceful, independent, and
suspicious of outsiders who do not understand their ways.

**Islanders:** Mixed cultures with traditions from both continents,
focused on maritime trades. They are practical, cosmopolitan, and loyal
to their crews above distant governments.

### 2.9 Unexplored Regions


Despite centuries of civilization, large portions of Tirvandor remain
unexplored or poorly mapped. The highest peaks of the Ironspine
Mountains have never felt humanoid footsteps. The deepest parts of the
Emerald Deeps hide secrets even the elves do not know. The ocean floor
of the Sundering Sea contains the ruins of Palace Port and countless
other lost places. Various small islands remain uncharted on any map.

These regions hold secrets, ancient ruins, lost civilizations, and
dangers unknown to most inhabitants of Tirvandor. They represent both
threat and opportunity---for those brave or foolish enough to venture
into the unknown.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 2: Geography}}
\page

## Chapter 3: Roads and Trade Routes

The major settlements of Tirvandor are connected by an extensive road
network that represents centuries of civilization-building, engineering
achievement, and commercial necessity. Roads vary significantly in
quality by region, from well-paved highways near major cities to
barely-marked trails in the wilderness that only locals can follow. This
network forms the arteries through which trade, information, and culture
flow across both continents.

### 3.1 Major Roads of Thaldros (17 Named Routes)


The western continent maintains an extensive network of named highways
connecting its major settlements. These routes are generally
well-maintained and patrolled, though conditions vary by season and
proximity to civilization.

**The King's Highway** runs from Kaer Thandros through Silverpine and
Crossvale to Goldreach. This is the primary artery of western Thaldros,
well-maintained and regularly patrolled by Crown forces. It represents
the spine of Thaldrosian commerce and military movement.

**The Northern Pass** connects Kaer Thandros to Ironhold and continues
to Frostholm. This mountain route passes through the Ironspine Holds and
closes during deep winter when snow makes the high passes impassable.
Military garrisons maintain the route during travel season.

**The Coastal Way** follows the western shore from Goldreach through
Harborpoint to Port Silverfish. This western coastal trade route serves
the fishing communities and smaller ports that dot the Goldcoast.

**The Sundaran Road** stretches from Crossvale through Graincross to
Sundara. This major desert trade route features fortified waystations at
regular intervals
\column

{{margin-top:290px}}


where travelers can find water, shelter, and
protection from both the elements and raiders.

**The Ashgate Trail** runs from Crossvale through Ashgate to Emberforge.
This volcanic region route required special heat-resistant construction
methods and is maintained by workers accustomed to the extreme
conditions.

**The Silverwood Path** winds from Silverpine through Oakenheart to
Greenleaf. This forest route passes through the ancient woods along
carefully maintained paths that respect the druids' sacred groves.

**The Heartland Highway** connects Silverpine directly to Crossvale.
This central agricultural route serves the farming communities of the
Heartlands and carries much of Thaldros' grain to market.

**The Eastern Reach** extends from Crossvale through Ashgate to the
Reaching Claws. This frontier route leads to the badlands and is less
well-maintained than other major roads, reflecting the limited Crown
authority in the region.

**The Mountain Road** connects Kaer Thandros to Deepforge and continues
to Stonehaven. This inner mountain route links the great dwarf holds and
carries the mineral wealth of the Ironspine to the capital.

**The Shore Road** runs from Silverpine through Stormhaven to Clifftop
along the northeast coast. This route serves the communities of the
Shattered Shore and provides access to the fishing grounds.

**The Gold Run** connects Goldreach to Saltmere and the Western Islands
via ferry services. This route facilitates trade with the Splintered
Isles and provides access to island resources.

**The Deep Desert Route** extends from Sundara through Oasis Rest to
Dustkeep. This caravan route penetrates deep into the Sundaran Expanse,
connecting the scattered oasis communities.

**The Volcanic Highway** runs from Ashgate through Cinderfall to
Flamekeep. This specially constructed route was built to withstand the
volcanic terrain and provides the only reliable path through the Ashfall
Barrens.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 3: Roads and Trade Routes}}
\page

**The Western Loop** forms a coastal circuit from Goldreach through
Harborview and Shellcove back to Goldreach. This route connects the
fishing villages and smaller ports of the western coast.

**The Trade Triangle** connects Silverpine, Crossvale, and Goldreach in
a continuous circuit. This primary commercial route carries the majority
of Thaldros' internal trade and is considered the most economically
vital road network in the kingdom.

**The Border Road** runs from Ironhold to Stormhaven along the northern
frontier. This northern defensive route was built primarily for military
purposes and is maintained by the garrisons it connects.

**The Claw Peninsula Road** extends from Ashgate to Southpoint at the
tip of the Reaching Claws. This southern frontier route serves the
isolated communities of the badland's peninsula.

### 3.2 Major Roads of Aethoria (10 Named Routes)


The eastern continent's road network reflects its different geography
and culture---more emphasis on forest paths and causeways, fewer
straight imperial highways.

**The Greenway** is the primary forest road running from Aethermere
through Crystalbrook to Wildgrove. Rather than a single paved road, it
consists of a series of wooden causeways and ancient paths that wind
through the primordial forests.

**The Starpath** connects Starfall to Aethermere. This
celestially-aligned road was constructed according to astronomical
principles and glows faintly at night, a phenomenon attributed to the
star iron dust mixed into its stones.

**The Lake Circuit** follows the shoreline of the great lakes from
Crystalbrook through Lakeshire and Clearwater before returning to
Crystalbrook. This scenic route provides access to the fishing
communities and water-based industries of the Crystalvale.

**The River Road** runs from Crystalbrook through Riverrun to Harvest
Hall, following the course of the Brightwater River. This route serves
the agricultural heartland of Aethoria and carries food to the larger
settlements.

**The Marsh Causeway** connects Crystalbrook to Marshaven via an
elevated wooden road built above the wetlands. This engineering
achievement makes travel through the Thornmire Marches possible without
wading through swamp water.

**The Highland Path** leads from Aethermere to Mistview through the
Mistwood Reaches. This mountain trail winds through some of Aethoria's
most mysterious territory and is known for travelers losing their way in
the perpetual fog.

**The Coastal Track** follows the Fractured Coast from Haven's Rest
through Seaspray to Tidebreak. This route connects the isolated
communities of the broken coastline and requires local knowledge to
navigate safely.

**The Southern Way** runs from Aethermere through Wildgrove to Highgrove
in the Verdant Wall mountains. This route connects the capital to the
southern regions and passes through some of Aethoria's most pristine
wilderness.

**The Swamp Road** links Marshaven to Reedwatch, connecting the two
major settlements of the wetland regions. Like the Marsh Causeway, this
route required specialized construction to remain passable year-round.

**The Peninsula Path** extends from Wildgrove to Thornhaven (via ferry)
and continues to Splitcove on the Split Peninsula. This southwest
coastal route serves the druidic communities and isolated settlements of
the peninsula.

### 3.3 Secondary Roads (23 Named Routes)


Beyond the major highways, an extensive network of secondary roads
connects smaller settlements and provides alternative routes between
major destinations.

#### Thaldros Secondary Roads (14 Routes)


**The Deepforge Connector** links Kaer Thandros directly to Deepforge,
providing a shorter route to the mining town than the main Mountain
Road.

**The Stonehaven Trail** continues from Deepforge to Stonehaven,
completing the mountain circuit through the dwarf holds.

**The Forest Track** winds from Oakenheart to Willowbrook through the
Silverwood, serving the logging and paper-making communities.

**The Heartland Crossway** is actually a network of roads connecting
various heartland villages, allowing farmers to reach markets without
traveling to major cities.

**The Desert Caravan Route** links multiple oases across the Sundaran
Expanse, providing alternative paths for caravans seeking to avoid
bandits or sandstorms.

**The Ash Trail** connects Smokehollow to Ashvale through the volcanic
regions, serving the mining communities of the Ashfall Barrens.

**The Cindervale Path** links the volcanic villages of the Ashfall
Barrens, providing local connections between obsidian mining
communities.

**The Eastern Frontier** is a loose network of roads serving multiple
badlands settlements in the Reaching Claws region.

**The Coastal Villages Route** connects the fishing villages of the
Goldcoast, allowing small communities to trade without traveling to
Goldreach.

**The Mountain Village Path** links the scattered hamlets of the
Ironspine region, connecting mountain communities to larger towns.

**The Northern Settlements Road** serves the Frostwatch area, connecting
the hardy communities of the Frostmarches.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 3: Roads and Trade Routes}}
\page

**The Desert Oasis Circuit** forms a loop connecting the desert towns of
the Sundaran Expanse, allowing traders to visit multiple communities on
a single journey.

**The Southern Peninsula Track** serves the Reaching Claws region,
connecting frontier settlements to the main road network.

**The Crossroads Network** connects major junctions across Thaldros,
providing alternative routes when main roads are blocked or dangerous.

#### Aethoria Secondary Roads (9 Routes)


**The Fernwatch Connection** links Aethermere directly to Fernwatch,
providing access to the forest guardian outpost.

**The Valley Road** connects the various villages of the Brightwater
Valley, serving the agricultural communities that feed Aethoria.

**The Mistwood Trail** links the highland settlements of the Mistwood
Reaches, though travelers often report difficulty following it in the
perpetual fog.

**The Thornmire Track** connects the swamp villages of the Thornmire
Marches, though this route is often partially flooded during the wet
season.

**The Singing Path** winds through the Singing Fens, named for the
acoustic properties of the region that make travelers hear music in the
wind.

**The Verdant Ridge Road** connects the mountain villages of the Verdant
Wall, climbing through jungle-covered slopes.

**The Coastal Villages Way** links the settlements of the Fractured
Coast, providing connections between the isolated island-like
communities.

**The Starwood Circuit** connects the settlements of the northwest
forest region, allowing trade between elven communities.

**The Peninsula Coastal Road** follows the shore of the Split Peninsula,
connecting the druidic and fishing communities of the southwest.

### 3.4 Minor Trails (31 Networks)


Beyond the named roads, numerous minor trails connect smaller villages
and hamlets. These routes are often seasonal, poorly maintained, and
require local guides to navigate safely. They include:

**Mountain Hamlet Trails:** Eight separate networks in the Ironspine
region connect the scattered mountain communities to each other and to
larger settlements. These trails often involve rope bridges, narrow
ledges, and paths that disappear under winter snow.

**Forest Footpaths:** Seven networks wind through the Silverwood of
Thaldros and the Starwood of Aethoria, maintained by rangers and druids
who know the subtle markers that guide travelers.

**Desert Trade Paths:** Four networks cross the Sundaran Expanse, known
only to desert nomads who navigate by stars and subtle landscape
features invisible to outsiders.

**Swamp Channels:** Five networks in the Thornmire Marches and Singing
Fens are actually water routes navigable by shallow-draft boats rather
than traditional land paths.

**Coastal Fishing Trails:** Four networks along the coasts of both
continents connect fishing communities, often following clifftop routes
or beaches passable only at low tide.

**Remote Frontier Paths:** Three networks in the badland's regions
connect isolated settlements, marked by stone cairns and known primarily
to those who live in these harsh territories.

### 3.5 Sea Routes


Maritime trade routes complement the land-based network, enabling
commerce between the continents and serving coastal communities.

**The Merchant Lanes** are established shipping routes passing through
the archipelagos that have enabled continental trade for centuries.
These routes are charted, reasonably safe during good weather, and
serviced by the various island communities.

**The Continental Crossing** runs from Goldreach to Port Myrthen to
Haven's Rest, representing the primary route for intercontinental
trade. This voyage typically requires multiple stops in the Drifting
Chain for resupply and rest.

**The Southern Island Route** extends from Port Myrthen through Saltmere
to the Southern Islands, serving the scattered tropical communities and
bringing exotic goods north.

**The Northern Fishing Grounds** route runs from Stormwatch to the rich
waters of the northern Sundering Sea, serving the fishing fleets that
supply much of Thaldros' coastal population.

**Coastal Shipping Routes** follow both continental coastlines, carrying
goods between ports too distant for practical land travel. These routes
vary by season and weather conditions.

### 3.6 Travel Considerations


Several factors affect travel throughout Tirvandor beyond simple
distance.

**Seasonal Variations:** Winter closes mountain passes, floods swamp
routes, and makes desert travel more practical during the day but
dangerous at night. Spring flooding can make river crossings impossible
for weeks. Summer heat makes desert travel best undertaken at night.
Autumn is generally the best season for long-distance travel on most
routes.

**Regional Hazards:** Mountain travel risks avalanches and sudden
storms. Forest routes require guides to avoid becoming lost in the
ancient woods. Desert crossings demand careful water management and
knowledge of oasis locations. Swamp travel requires boats or elevated
causeways. Volcanic regions present dangers from toxic gases and
unstable terrain.

**Political Considerations:** Some routes pass through contested
territory where neither Crown nor council authority holds sway.
Travelers on these roads must rely on their own resources or hire
protection. Other

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 3: Roads and Trade Routes}}
\page

routes cross boundaries between noble territories, and
tolls or taxes may apply.

**Magical Phenomena:** Certain areas experience wild magic surges that
can affect travelers. Ley line intersections create nodes of unusual
power. Some forest paths seem to change length depending on the
intentions of those who walk them. The Starpath of Aethoria glows at
night, but some report that it shows different destinations to different
travelers.

\column

**Infrastructure:** Major routes feature waystations, inns, and patrol
posts at regular intervals. Secondary roads may have only occasional
villages for resupply. Minor trails offer nothing but what travelers
bring with them. Sea voyages require knowledge of safe harbors and
resupply points.

The road network of Tirvandor represents one of civilization's greatest
achievements---the binding together of distant communities into a
functioning whole. Yet even the best-maintained highway passes through
wild country, and travelers who forget this truth often do not complete
their journeys.

## Chapter 4: The Magic System


### 4.1 The Nature of Magic in Tirvandor


Magic in Tirvandor is not merely a force to be commanded---it is woven
into the very fabric of reality, flowing through the world like blood
through a living body. This magical energy courses through channels
called ley lines, invisible rivers of power that crisscross both
continents, run beneath the Sundering Sea, and connect to forces that
predate mortal civilization.

The world's magical saturation varies by region. Natural
areas---ancient forests, untouched mountains, primordial swamps---tend
to have high magical saturation, their environments shaped over
millennia by the energies flowing through them. Settled regions where
civilization has taken root typically show moderate saturation, the
natural magic somewhat dampened by the presence of roads, fields, and
cities. And in places scarred by catastrophe or corruption, the magical
flow may be disrupted, weakened, or twisted into something dangerous.

Those trained in the arcane arts perceive ley lines as faint threads of
luminous energy, visible only to those who know how to look. Druids and
rangers, attuned to the natural world, sense them as part of the
landscape itself---as natural and obvious as the flow of water downhill.
For ordinary folk, ley lines remain invisible, though their effects
shape daily life in countless subtle ways.

### 4.2 Ley Lines: Rivers of Power


Ley lines are ancient channels of magical energy that run beneath the
surface of Tirvandor. Their origins are debated---some scholars believe
they formed during the world's creation, others that they are the
remnants of the Primordials' power, and still others that they
represent scars from the Worldrend, channels carved by
\column
{{margin-top:290px}}

the cataclysmic
release of magical energy that tore the continents apart.

Whatever their origin, ley lines follow patterns that have remained
largely stable since the earliest records. They flow like underground
rivers, invisible to ordinary sight but perceptible to those with
magical training. Where multiple ley lines cross, they form
nexuses---nodes of concentrated power that have attracted settlement,
worship, and conflict throughout history.

The major settlements of Tirvandor were often built on or near ley line
nexuses, either deliberately by those who understood the advantages of
such locations, or unconsciously drawn by the subtle influence magical
power exerts on mortal minds. Great cities, ancient temples, and sites
of historical significance cluster along ley lines with a frequency that
cannot be coincidental.

### 4.3 Known Ley Line Nexuses


Throughout Tirvandor, certain locations have been identified as major
ley line nexuses---places where multiple lines of magical energy
converge, creating concentrations of power that have shaped history and
continue to influence the present.

**Aethermere Nexus** lies beneath the elven capital of Aethoria. The
city was built atop this major nexus, which contributes significantly to
Aethermere's status as a center of magical learning and practice. The
world-trees that form the city's framework draw upon this power, and
the nexus has been carefully tended by elven mages for millennia. It is
considered one of the most stable and well-understood nexuses in the
world.

**The Silverpine Nexus** rests beneath Silverpine's famous Magical
Academy. This stable nexus has been heavily monitored and studied for
centuries, making it perhaps the most thoroughly documented ley line
intersection in existence. The academy was founded specifically to take
advantage of this nexus, and generations of scholars have mapped its
flows and fluctuations with meticulous care.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 4: The Magic System}}
\page

**The Ironhold Deep Forge** is a nexus controlled by the dwarves of the
Ironspine Mountains. They have learned to channel its energies to power
their legendary magical forges, using the ley line energy to create
items of extraordinary quality and enchantment. The dwarves guard the
secrets of this nexus jealously, and their mastery of its power explains
much of their reputation as master craftsmen.

**The Ironspine Peaks** contain multiple ley lines that converge within
the mountain range. This concentration of magical energy explains the
presence of magical ores found nowhere else---veins of mythril, deposits
of crystals that glow with inner light, and metals that take enchantment
with unusual ease. The mountains themselves seem to hum with power to
those sensitive enough to perceive it.

**The Kaer Thandros Vault** is a secret nexus known only to the royal
family and their most trusted advisors. Located deep beneath the
fortress-city, this nexus serves as an emergency power source---a
reserve of magical energy that could theoretically be tapped in times of
desperate need. Its existence is one of the Crown's most closely
guarded secrets.

**The Goldreach Harbor Nexus** lies underwater, beneath the famous port.
This nexus powers the Lighthouse of Eternal Flame that guides ships into
harbor, as well as the magical wards that protect the city from sea
monsters and hostile naval forces. Its underwater location makes it
difficult to access but also difficult for enemies to target.

**35.2 The Singing Stones** mark a nexus maintained by druidic circles
in the wilderness of Thaldros. This ancient site serves as a portal to
the Feywild, and the stones themselves produce haunting melodies when
the wind passes through them---sounds that change with the phase of the
moon and the alignment of the stars. The druids who tend this nexus
guard it against those who would misuse its power.

**The Ashgate Catacombs** contain an unstable nexus that has become
partially corrupted over time. The volatile nature of this nexus
contributes to the volcanic activity in the region, and some scholars
believe the corruption stems from the Worldrend itself. Attempts to
stabilize or purify this nexus have met with limited success, and the
catacombs are considered dangerous even by the standards of ley line
sites.

**The Nexus of Seven Sorrows** is a fully corrupted nexus located on the
floor of the Sundering Sea, in the waters above what was once the great
city of Palace Port. This is where the first seal was broken during the
events leading to the Worldrend, and the nexus now radiates void energy
that warps reality in its vicinity. The site is considered mythical by
most, its exact coordinates lost to history, but those who seek to
prevent another catastrophe---or cause one---search for it still.

**The Deep Wildwood Nexus** lies somewhere in the heart of Aethoria's
southern rainforests, an unnamed convergence of power considered sacred
ground by the tribes and druids who know of its existence. Few outsiders
have ever reached it, and those who have speak of a place where time
moves strangely and the boundary between the material world and other
planes grows thin.

**The Sundaran Ruins** were built upon ley line nexuses by ancient
civilizations that flourished before the desert claimed the land. Now
buried beneath the sands, these forgotten nexuses occasionally surge
with power, causing strange phenomena in the desert above. Treasure
hunters and scholars alike seek these buried sites, though the desert
guards its secrets jealously.

### 4.4 How Ley Lines Affect the World


The presence of ley lines shapes Tirvandor in ways both obvious and
subtle, influencing everything from where cities rise to how creatures
evolve.

**Settlement Patterns:** Throughout history, sentient beings have been
drawn to settle near ley lines and nexuses. Sometimes this was
deliberate---mages seeking power, temples seeking connection to divine
forces. More often, it was unconscious, early settlers simply feeling
that a place was "right" without understanding why. The result is that
the great cities and sacred sites of Tirvandor cluster along ley lines
with remarkable consistency.

**Magical Flora and Fauna:** Creatures and plants that evolve near ley
lines often develop magical properties. The glowing forests of the
Starwood, the singing crystals of the Crystalvale, the fire-resistant
flora of the Ashfall Barrens---all reflect the influence of ley line
energy on natural development over countless generations. Some creatures
have become so attuned to ley lines that they cannot survive far from
them.

**Weather and Climate:** Ley lines influence weather patterns in ways
that meteorologists still struggle to explain. The perpetual mists of
the Mistwood Reaches, the unusual storm patterns of the Sundering Sea,
the localized climatic effects found throughout Aethoria---all correlate
with ley line flows. Some scholars believe that major ley line
disruptions could alter climate on a continental scale.

**Planar Boundaries:** Where ley lines are strong, the boundaries
between the material world and other planes grow thin. The Singing
Stones' connection to the Feywild is one example, but similar phenomena
occur throughout Tirvandor. Ghost sightings cluster along certain ley
lines. Demonic incursions tend to occur near corrupted nexuses. Some
ancient sites exist partially in multiple planes simultaneously.

**Magical Instability:** In the Contested Lands and other regions where
ley lines have been disrupted---whether by the Worldrend, deliberate
sabotage, or natural catastrophe---magic becomes unpredictable. Spells
may fail without warning, produce unexpected effects, or trigger wild
magical surges that reshape reality in their immediate vicinity. Mages
who operate in such regions must exercise extreme caution.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 4: The Magic System}}
\page

### 4.5 Ley Line Corruption


Not all ley lines flow clean and pure. Some have become
corrupted---their energies twisted by catastrophe, deliberate malice, or
the influence of dark powers. Corrupted ley lines and nexuses pose
unique dangers to Tirvandor and its inhabitants.

The most common cause of corruption is trauma---the magical equivalent
of scar tissue forming where the world has been wounded. The Worldrend
left numerous corrupted ley lines in its wake, and smaller catastrophes
have added to their number over the centuries. Some corruption is the
result of deliberate action: dark rituals performed at nexuses,
imprisoned entities leaking their influence into the magical flow, or
the cumulative effect of necromancy and other forbidden practices.

Corrupted nexuses amplify magical power but at a price. The energy they
provide is tainted, prone to wild fluctuations and dangerous side
effects. Those who draw upon corrupted ley lines risk more than magical
backlash---prolonged exposure can twist the mind and body, gradually
transforming the user into something no longer entirely mortal.

The Ashgate Catacombs represent a partially corrupted nexus, unstable
and dangerous but not yet beyond hope of redemption. The Nexus of Seven
Sorrows is fully corrupted, a wound in reality that some believe could
tear open further if not contained. Between these extremes lie dozens of
lesser corrupted sites, each presenting its own challenges to those who
would cleanse or contain them.

### 4.6 The Silver Circle


The study and protection of ley lines falls primarily to the Silver
Circle, an organization of mages dedicated to understanding Tirvandor's
magical infrastructure and preventing its misuse. Founded in the
centuries following the Worldrend, the Circle maintains political
neutrality, operating in both Thaldros and Aethoria without allegiance
to either power.

Circle members---called Initiates during training and simply Circle
Mages thereafter---devote their lives to mapping ley lines, monitoring
nexuses, and responding to magical disturbances. They maintain
chapterhouses near major nexuses and ley line junctions, staffed by
researchers who spend years studying the flows of magical energy.

The Circle's political neutrality is both its greatest strength and its
most controversial aspect. By refusing to take sides in the ongoing
tensions between Thaldros and Aethoria, the Circle can operate freely
across both continents. Critics argue that this neutrality amounts to
cowardice---that the Circle should use its knowledge and power to
actively shape events rather than merely observing and containing
dangers.

Among the Circle's most important functions is the identification and
remediation of ley line corruption. When a nexus shows signs of
instability or taint, Circle mages respond, working to stabilize the
flow and contain any dangerous effects. Their success rate is
imperfect---some corrupted sites prove beyond their ability to
cleanse---but without their efforts, the magical infrastructure of
Tirvandor would likely have degraded significantly since the Worldrend.

### 4.7 Magic and the Worldrend


The Worldrend was, at its core, a magical catastrophe of unprecedented
scale. The event tore the continents apart, created the Sundering Sea,
and disrupted ley lines across the entire world. Understanding what
happened---and preventing it from happening again---remains one of the
central concerns of magical scholarship in Tirvandor.

Before the Worldrend, magic flowed more freely and predictably. The
great civilization that spanned what are now two continents had learned
to harness ley line energy on a massive scale, powering cities, enabling
communication across vast distances, and achieving feats that modern
mages can only dream of replicating.

Then something went wrong. The details remain disputed---records from
that era are fragmentary at best, deliberately destroyed at worst. What
is known is that a ritual of unprecedented power was attempted at a
major nexus, that the ritual failed catastrophically, and that the
resulting release of magical energy tore the world apart.

The ley lines never fully recovered. While they continue to flow, they
do so with less power and less stability than before the Worldrend. Some
scholars believe this weakening is temporary, that given enough
time---perhaps millennia---the magical infrastructure will heal. Others
argue that the damage is permanent, that Tirvandor will never again know
the magical abundance of the pre-Worldrend era.

Most concerning are those who believe that the instability is growing
worse---that the Worldrend set in motion a slow degradation that will
eventually lead to a second catastrophe. These scholars point to
increasing reports of wild magic surges, the difficulty of cleansing
corrupted nexuses, and subtle changes in ley line flow patterns as
evidence that time is running out.

Whether their fears are justified remains to be seen. But in the halls
of the Arcanum, in the chapterhouses of the Silver Circle, and in the
secret councils of both Thaldros and Aethoria, the possibility of a
second Worldrend is never far from the minds of those who understand
what is truly at stake.

{{footnote Chapter 4: The Magic System}}
