## Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists


The antagonists of Tirvandor represent moral complexity at its
finest---many are victims themselves, driven by legitimate grievances to
terrible ends. Understanding their motivations is essential to
understanding the world's conflicts.

### 44.1 Corvus Blackwood (Lord Shadows)

![44.1 Corvus Blackwood (Lord Shadows)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-corvus-blackwood.jpg){width:305px}

{{margin-top:290px}}

**The Last Heir of House Blackwood, Leader of The Unbound**

**Full Name:** Corvus Aldric Blackwood

**Titles:** Lord Shadows, The Shadow of House Blackwood, The Last
Blackwood

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 55 (born 1192 CR)

**Current Location:** Raven's Keep (ancestral Blackwood seat) and
various hidden locations

**Role:** Revolutionary Leader, Tragic Villain/Antihero

**Alignment:** Lawful Neutral (trending Chaotic as desperation grows)

#### Physical Description


A gaunt man in his mid-fifties who moves like someone two decades
younger. Corvus has sharp features with angular cheekbones and a strong
jaw softened only slightly by age. His hair, once raven-black like all
Blackwoods, is now streaked with gray, worn longer than fashion dictates
and often tied back. His eyes are his most striking feature---dark gray,
almost silver, with an intensity that makes people uncomfortable. When
angry, they seem to absorb light.

His hands are those of someone who has learned to kill---precise,
steady, scarred from decades of clandestine work. He moves with a
predator's economy, never wasted motion, always aware of exits and
threats. Despite his revolutionary role, he carries himself with the
unconscious grace of nobility---an inheritance he cannot shed no matter
how far he's fallen.

When operating openly, he wears practical dark clothing with the
Blackwood sigil (a raven clutching a shadow) hidden beneath his collar.
As "Lord Shadows," he wears a dark hooded cloak that seems to drink in
light, and a mask that conceals his features. When adopting his
"scholar" persona for recruitment, he wears elegant robes and
spectacles, appearing as a harmless academic.

A tattoo of the Blackwood family sigil covers his entire back---the only
possession he retained from his childhood. The curse mark from Raven's
Keep 

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

manifests as black veins spreading slowly from his left hand toward
his heart.

#### Personality


**Core Traits:**

-   Brilliant strategist and meticulous planner

-   Speaks with measured precision, choosing every word carefully

-   Possesses a dark, bitter humor forged by tragedy

-   Capable of tremendous patience but increasingly desperate

-   Genuine care for those wronged by the powerful

-   Terrifying capacity for violence when necessary

**Behavioral Patterns:**

-   Constantly watching exits and reading people

-   Touches weapons when nervous, books when calm

-   Stands with back to walls, never fully relaxed

-   Eyes go flat and cold before violence

-   Speaks softly when most dangerous

-   Uses people's names frequently---a manipulation technique

**Philosophical Foundation:**

Corvus believes the powerful inevitably abuse their authority, and that
systems designed to deliver justice are merely tools of oppression
dressed in legitimacy. He sees himself not as a villain but as an
accountant---the bill for centuries of lies is due, and he intends to
collect.

**Defining Quotes:**

-   "They took everything. Name, family, future. But they gave me
    purpose."

-   "I'm not a villain. I'm an accountant, and the bill is due."

-   "Justice deferred is justice denied."

-   "You want truth? Truth is dangerous. Sure you can handle it?"

-   "They wear crowns built on graves. Time someone reminded them."

#### Complete Background & History


**The Blackwood Legacy (Before 1089 CR)**

House Blackwood was one of the oldest noble houses in Thaldros, tracing
their lineage to Lord Garrett Blackwood in 750 BW. They claimed descent
from the First Men who settled Thaldros after the Worldrend, and their
bloodline carried traces of fey ancestry that manifested as unusual
magical talents---particularly an affinity for shadow magic and
divination.

What few knew was the Blackwoods' sacred trust: for generations, they
had served as guardians of the Shadow Shard, the First Component of the
World-Splitter. This artifact, a remnant of the cataclysm that tore the
continents apart, was too dangerous to use and too powerful to destroy.
The Blackwoods kept it sealed in vaults beneath Raven's Keep, their
vigilance unbroken for centuries.

\column

**The Blackwood Rebellion (1089-1092 CR)**

In 1089 CR, Lord Aldric Blackwood III claimed the throne of Thaldros
through his grandmother's royal blood. This claim was legitimate under
ancient law, but the reigning Thandris dynasty refused to yield. Civil
war erupted.

What history records as a treasonous rebellion was, in truth,
manufactured. The Crown had discovered the existence of the Shadow Shard
and wanted it. When Lord Aldric refused to surrender his family's
sacred charge, false evidence was planted, witnesses were threatened or
killed, and the Blackwoods were branded traitors conspiring to trigger a
Second Worldrend---the very catastrophe they had spent centuries
preventing.

The war lasted three years. At the Battle of Raven's Keep in 1092 CR,
Blackwood forces were crushed. Lord Aldric and all known heirs were
publicly executed for treason. Raven's Keep was burned, lands
distributed to loyalist houses, and the Blackwood name was forbidden.
The family line was declared extinct.

**The Hidden Survivors**

But some Blackwoods escaped the purge. Distant relatives, minor
branches, servants who had married into the family---they fled to remote
regions, adopted new names, and lived in hiding. For over a century,
these survivors maintained their secret identity, passing down the truth
from parent to child.

**The Second Blackwood Purge (1204 CR)**

In 1192 CR, Corvus was born to Marcus and Elaine Blackwood, survivors
living under the name "Ashford" in a remote village near the
Silverwood. They believed themselves safe after more than a century of
hiding.

They were wrong.

In 1204 CR, Crown intelligence discovered the Ashford family's true
identity. King Aldric III---whose eldest son Prince Aldric had recently
committed a terrible crime involving the World-Splitter Components---saw
an opportunity. By eliminating the surviving Blackwoods and blaming them
for Prince Aldric's crimes, he could protect his son and tie up loose
ends from a century ago.

The soldiers came at night. Twelve-year-old Corvus was hiding in a
barrel in the wine cellar when they broke down the door. He watched
through a crack as his father was cut down defending his mother. He
heard her screams as they set the house ablaze, proclaiming her
family's innocence even as flames consumed her. A servant who had
discovered his hiding place pushed the barrel out a back window before
she too was killed.

Corvus crawled from the ashes at dawn. His family was dead. His home was
cinders. He had nothing but the clothes on his back and the truth
branded into his soul.

**The Lost Years (1204-1230 CR)**

For twenty-six years, Corvus survived in the shadows of society. He was
a beggar, a thief, a dock worker, a sellsword---whatever kept him alive
while he learned. He sought out those who could teach him the skills of

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

survival: assassins taught him to kill, spies taught him to gather
information, forgers taught him to create false identities, and rogue 
scholars taught him the forbidden histories the Crown had tried to erase.

He found mentors among the desperate and the vengeful. An old assassin
named Kaelar trained him in the killing arts before dying of plague. A
disgraced court historian named Maren showed him how to research the
past, to find truth buried beneath official lies. She died never knowing
her student would use that knowledge to shake the foundations of
kingdoms.

Throughout these years, Corvus investigated his family's destruction.
Every thread he pulled revealed deeper corruption. He discovered the
truth: House Blackwood had been guardians, not conspirators. The
rebellion of 1089 CR had been manufactured to justify seizing the Shadow
Shard. And the Second Purge of 1204 CR had been ordered to cover up an
even darker crime.

**The True Conspiracy Revealed**

Through decades of investigation, Corvus pieced together the terrible
truth:

**The Goldshore Keepers:** A cadet branch of House Goldshore had
secretly served as guardians of the Second Component---the Flame
Heart---hidden in vaults beneath Kaer Thandros. For centuries, they
fulfilled this trust alongside the Blackwoods.

**Prince Aldric's Crime:** Around 1200 CR, Crown Prince Aldric (eldest
son of King Aldric III) discovered the Keepers' secret. Influenced by
fire cultists and ambitious beyond reason, he murdered the entire
Goldshore Keeper family to steal the Flame Heart. He made it look like
plague and blamed distant Blackwood descendants for orchestrating the
deaths.

**The Cover-Up:** When King Aldric III learned what his son had done, he
faced an impossible choice: expose his heir as a mass murderer or find a
scapegoat. He chose family over justice. The Second Blackwood Purge was
ordered not to eliminate traitors, but to eliminate witnesses and create
a convenient explanation for the Keeper deaths.

**The Execution:** When Prince Aldric's instability threatened to
expose everything, King Aldric III secretly had his own son killed in a
staged "hunting accident." The middle son Marcus briefly inherited but
died of fever as an infant-king. The current King Aldric IV---the third
son---knows nothing of his family's crimes. He believes the official
history completely.

**The Birth of Lord Shadows (1230 CR)**

Armed with the truth and trained in deadly arts, Corvus began building
his network. He adopted the title "Lord Shadows"---the shadow of House
Blackwood, refusing to die---and sought out others wronged by the
powerful. Former servants of destroyed houses, victims of noble
injustice, survivors of Crown brutality---he offered them community,
purpose, and the promise of accountability for those who had escaped
justice.

The Unbound was born.
\column
**The Present Day (1247 CR)**

Now fifty-five years old, Corvus has spent forty-three years building
toward his goals. The Unbound has grown from a handful of survivors to
hundreds of operatives across Thaldros. He has gathered evidence proving
his family's innocence, documented the Crown's crimes, and located the
World-Splitter Components.

But time is running out. During his escape from Raven's Keep years ago,
he triggered an ancient curse---Blackwood blood cannot leave the
ancestral seat without permission from the living head of house. Since
no such person exists to grant permission, the curse slowly kills any
Blackwood who departs. The black veins spreading from his left hand
toward his heart mark his remaining time: perhaps five years at most.

This desperation drives his timeline. What might have been decades of
careful planning must now be compressed into years. The threat of the
Second Worldrend---of actually reassembling the World-Splitter---is
leverage, not genuine intent. Corvus doesn't want to destroy the world;
he wants justice. But desperation can change even the most principled
person.

#### Goals & Motivations


**Primary Goal: Vindication**

Above all else, Corvus wants the truth exposed. House Blackwood was
innocent---guardians who died protecting the realm from the very
artifact they were accused of seeking. He wants their name cleared,
their memory honored, and history corrected.

**Secondary Goal: Accountability**

Those who orchestrated the Blackwood destruction must face consequences.
This includes the Thandris dynasty, which has perpetuated the lie for
generations, and the noble houses that profited from Blackwood lands.

**Tertiary Goal: Systemic Change**

The Unbound believe House Blackwood's fate reveals fundamental
corruption in the kingdom's power structures. They seek to tear down
systems that allow such injustice---though members disagree on what
should replace them.

**The World-Splitter Threat**

Corvus claims he will reassemble the World-Splitter and trigger a Second
Worldrend if justice is denied. Whether this threat is genuine or
leverage depends on his desperation level. He doesn't want to destroy
the world---but if the world refuses him justice, how far will he go?

**Hidden Motivation: Peace**

Deep beneath his rage and determination, Corvus is exhausted. He has
been fighting for forty-three years. Part of him simply wants to be
done---to clear his family's name and finally rest. If he could achieve
vindication without violence, he would. But he no longer believes such a
path exists.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

#### Methods & Operations


**Recruitment**

The Unbound target the desperate---those who have lost hope in
legitimate systems, victims of injustice who see no other path to
redress. Corvus approaches potential recruits using his "scholar"
persona: a brilliant academic offering a better world. He speaks of
philosophy, not violence, of justice, not revenge. Only those who prove
trustworthy learn about Lord Shadows.

**Intelligence Networks**

Corvus has spent decades building information networks. The Unbound
knows secrets about noble houses, government officials, and ancient
conspiracies that would shake kingdoms. Information is their greatest
weapon---and their greatest currency.

**Component Recovery**

Lord Shadows seeks the World-Splitter Components for multiple reasons:
as leverage to force accountability, as proof of his family's guardian
role (only Blackwood blood can open certain vaults), and as insurance
against betrayal. He currently possesses the First Component (Shadow
Shard) and seeks the others.

**Direct Action**

When diplomacy and negotiation fail, the Unbound resorts to violence.
They have conducted assassinations, kidnappings, sabotage, and terrorist
attacks against targets they consider complicit in injustice. These
actions are surgical rather than indiscriminate---Corvus has rules his
predecessors did not.

#### The Dual Persona


**Lord Shadows (True Identity)**

As Lord Shadows, Corvus is a terrifying figure---a ghost who commands
loyalty through fear and respect. He wears a dark hooded cloak and mask,
speaks in measured tones, and demonstrates lethal competence. This is
his identity among the Unbound leadership and when dealing with enemies.

**The Scholar (Recruitment Persona)**

When recruiting potential allies, Corvus adopts a completely different
persona. He wears scholar's robes, speaks of philosophy and history,
and appears as a brilliant but harmless academic passionate about
changing the world. This "recruiter persona" is how he appears
throughout normal society---and how players in the Blood & Coin campaign
first encounter him. The deadly assassin beneath the scholarly mask is a
deliberate shock.

#### Connections & Relationships


**Family:**

-   **Marcus Blackwood (brother):** Corvus has a younger brother who
    survived the purge separately. Marcus now leads refugees in the
    western frontier near Crossroads under an assumed identity. He is
    the "Lost Heir" mentioned in prophecy---and Corvus would die to
    protect him.

-   **Parents (deceased):** Marcus and Elaine Blackwood haunt his
    memories. He speaks to them sometimes when alone.

**The Unbound:**

-   **The Lich of Raven's Keep (Arcanus):** His most powerful
    lieutenant, bound to serve House Blackwood beyond death. Their
    relationship is complex---Arcanus serves out of oath but has his own
    agenda.

-   **Captain Malthus Voidcaller:** Military commander of Unbound
    forces, a decorated soldier who turned revolutionary after the
    system destroyed his family.

-   **Sister Mortua:** A death priest who believes she's serving
    justice but has been manipulated into supporting causes she would
    abhor if she knew the truth.

**Enemies:**

-   **House Thandris:** The entire dynasty bears responsibility for his
    family's destruction, though King Aldric IV is ignorant of his
    ancestors' crimes.

-   **The Crown:** Every institution that perpetuates the Blackwood lie
    is his enemy.

-   **Those Who Know:** Anyone aware of the true history who has chosen
    to maintain the lie.

**Complex Relationships:**

-   **Lady Morgana Blackwater:** Provides intelligence and resources in
    exchange for considerations. Their alliance is pragmatic, not
    ideological.

-   **Master Crimson (Shadow Syndicate):** An uneasy relationship---the
    Syndicate is useful but has its own agenda.

-   **King Aldric IV:** The current king is innocent of his family's
    crimes and genuinely tries to be a good ruler. Corvus struggles with
    this---how do you punish a dynasty through someone who did nothing
    wrong?

#### Secrets


1\. **The Component Locations:** He knows where each World-Splitter
Component is hidden and how to access them. The Shadow Shard is beneath
Raven's Keep. The Flame Heart is in vaults near Dragon Infernalix's
lair. The Void Fragment sank with Palace Port. The Stone Crown is
embedded in the Crown of Thaldros itself.

2\. **The Evidence Cache:** Corvus possesses documented proof of the
Blackwood conspiracy---forged documents, false witness testimonies,
records of the cover-up. This evidence would shake the kingdom but
requires the right platform to present.

3\. **The True Conspiracy:** He knows Prince Aldric murdered the
Goldshore Keepers, King Aldric III covered it up, and the current king
knows nothing. This creates a moral dilemma---punish the dynasty through
an innocent man?

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

4\. **The Dying Curse:** The black veins spreading from his hand mark
the curse killing him. He has perhaps five years to live. Only he and
the Lich know this secret.

5\. **The True Motivation:** Despite his rhetoric about the Second
Worldrend, Corvus doesn't actually want to destroy the world. The
threat is leverage. But he fears what desperation might drive him to if
all other options fail.

6\. **The Brother's Location:** Marcus Blackwood's identity and
location are Corvus' most guarded secret. If the Crown discovered
another Blackwood heir\...

7\. **The Possible Redemption:** Corvus knows that King Aldric IV, if
presented with evidence of his family's crimes, might actually choose
justice over dynasty. But he's afraid to hope---and afraid of what
failure would mean.

#### Story Potential


**Tragic Villain Arc:**

Corvus can serve as a complex antagonist whose legitimate grievances
make him sympathetic even as his methods become monstrous. Heroes must
stop him while acknowledging he was wronged.

**Redemption Path:**

If heroes can prove justice is possible within the system, Corvus might
be convinced to pursue vindication without apocalypse. This is the
hardest ending to achieve but creates the best outcome.

**Information Source:**

His knowledge of conspiracies, ancient history, and noble house secrets
makes him invaluable as an information source---if heroes can navigate
his agenda.

**Alliance Possibility:**

Under the right circumstances, heroes might ally with Corvus against
shared threats. Such alliances are always complicated by his ultimate
goals.

**Living Legacy:**

Even if Corvus dies, his evidence survives. His brother Marcus survives.
The truth survives. The question becomes what happens next.

### 44.2 Dragon Infernalix (The Vanished Flame)


**Ancient Red Dragon Sleeping Beneath Kaer Thandros**

**Full Name:** Infernalix the Eternal Flame (self-proclaimed title)

**Titles:** The Vanished Flame, The Dragon of Kaer Thandros, The
Sleeping Terror

**Species:** Ancient Red Dragon

**Age:** Over 3,000 years

**Current Location:** Caverns beneath the Royal Palace of Kaer Thandros

**Status:** Asleep (since 1201 CR)

**Threat Level:** Catastrophic

#### Physical Description


Infernalix is gargantuan even by ancient dragon standards---his wingspan
could shelter a village, and each scale is the size of a warrior's
shield. His coloration is deep crimson darkening to near-black along his
spine and wing edges, with golden-orange undertones that glow when he
stirs. His horns curve back like obsidian spears, and his eyes---when
open---burn with intelligence and ancient malice.

Age has not diminished him. If anything, centuries of slumber have
allowed his power to concentrate. His breath alone heats the caverns
beneath the palace; the warmth that rises through the Royal Palace's
lower levels comes from his presence. The faint sulfur smell in certain
cellars is not geological---it is him.

His hoard is legendary: gold coins by the millions, gems scattered like
sand, ancient artifacts from fallen kingdoms, weapons, armor, art,
jewelry---the accumulated wealth of two millennia of conquest and
tribute.

#### Personality


Infernalix is patient in ways mortals cannot comprehend. He has watched
kingdoms rise and fall like flowers blooming and withering. This
perspective makes him dismissive of short-lived races while
simultaneously fascinated by their accomplishments.

**Core Traits:**

-   Possesses vast intelligence beyond mere cunning

-   Patient to the point of seeming inactive

-   Utterly confident in his superiority

-   Fascinated by mortal ambition despite his disdain

-   Capable of negotiation when it serves his purposes

-   Absolutely merciless when crossed

**Philosophical Outlook:**

Infernalix sees himself as a force of nature rather than a villain.
Dragons ruled before mortals crawled from caves; they will rule again
when mortal civilizations crumble. His actions are not evil from his
perspective---merely the natural order reasserting itself.

**Defining Quote:** *"I am eternal. I am patient. I am inevitable."*

#### Complete Background & History


**Origins (Before the Worldrend)**

Infernalix hatched in the volcanic ranges of southern Aethoria more than
three thousand years ago, long before the Worldrend split the
continents. In those ancient days, dragons ruled vast territories, and
Infernalix carved out a domain that stretched across what would later
become multiple kingdoms.

The Worldrend changed everything. The cataclysm that separated the
continents also separated Infernalix from his ancestral territory. He
spent centuries in a rage, burning anything that reminded him of what
he'd lost. Eventually that rage cooled to something more dangerous:
patience. He began to plan.

**The Dragon Crisis (1156-1201 CR)**

In 1156 CR, Infernalix emerged from volcanic chambers and attacked Kaer
Thandros. The assault was devastating---outer districts destroyed,
hundreds killed, royal family members among the casualties.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page
House Emberthorn lost half their holdings in a single day when they refused to
pay tribute. House Ironforge saw three mines destroyed.

For forty-five years, Infernalix terrorized Thaldros. But this was never
random destruction---he was searching for something. He had learned of
the World-Splitter Components and believed one could reunite the
continents, restoring his domain.

**The Bargain (1201 CR)**

In 1201 CR, King Thandris V made a secret bargain with Infernalix. The
exact terms are lost, but the dragon withdrew to slumber in ancient
caverns beneath Kaer Thandros itself. He found what he sought---the
Flame Heart, Second Component of the World-Splitter, hidden in nearby
vaults. Now he sleeps, dreaming of the other pieces, waiting for his
bargain to come due.

**The Present (1247 CR)**

Infernalix has slept for forty-six years. The heat from his presence
warms the palace's lower levels. Few know the dragon slumbers directly
below the Royal Palace. Fewer still know what he found, what he dreams,
or when he will wake.

The bargain with House Thandris comes due in 1250 CR---just three years
away. When it does, every Thandris will feel the call.

#### Goals & Motivations


**Primary Goal: Continental Reunification**

Infernalix doesn't want to destroy civilization---he wants to reshape
the world by reuniting Thaldros and Aethoria, with himself as
god-emperor of the restored supercontinent. He believes the
World-Splitter Components can accomplish this.

**Secondary Goal: Component Collection**

His hoard already contains the Second Component (Flame Heart). He has
been dreaming of the other pieces' locations, psychically searching
while he sleeps.

**Tertiary Goal: The Bargain's Fulfillment**

The deal with Thandris V involves the royal bloodline. When it comes
due, every Thandris will feel the call---an obligation written into
their very blood.

**Hidden Agenda: Legacy**

Ancient even by dragon standards, Infernalix thinks about what he will
leave behind. His plan isn't just conquest---it's the establishment of
a new world order that will persist for millennia.

#### Connections


-   **House Thandris:** Bound by ancient pact. Cannot directly harm the
    ruling Thandris until the bargain comes due.

-   **The World-Splitter:** Possesses the Flame Heart. Seeks the others.

-   **Dragon Morveth:** Ancient rival. They've fought twice with no
    clear victor.

-   **Fire Cults:** Some fanatics worship him and seek to wake him
    prematurely.

-   **Kael Dragonsbane:** Master hunter who has studied Infernalix for
    decades---the only mortal who might know his weaknesses.

#### Secrets


1\. **The Sleeping Location:** His lair lies directly beneath the Royal
Palace. The heat from his presence warms the lower levels.

2\. **The Artifact Fragment:** His hoard contains the Flame Heart,
Second Component of the World-Splitter. He's been dreaming of the other
pieces' locations.

3\. **The True Bargain:** The deal with Thandris V wasn't just for
peace---it was for the king's bloodline. When it comes due, every
Thandris will feel an irresistible compulsion.

4\. **The Dream Network:** While sleeping, Infernalix has been
psychically influencing certain individuals, preparing agents for his
awakening.

5\. **The Vanishing Flame:** He possesses the ability to become
invisible and intangible---how he "withdrew" in 1201 CR. Few know this
power exists.

### 44.3 Arcanus the Undying (The Lich of Raven's Keep)


**Ancient Lich Bound to House Blackwood**

**True Name:** Magistar Corvellian (original identity, mostly forgotten)

**Titles:** The Lich of Raven's Keep, Arcanus the Undying, The Eternal
Servant

**Species:** Lich (formerly human)

**Age:** Approximately 300 years undead

**Current Location:** Raven's Keep, vaults and sanctum

**Role:** Lord Shadows' most powerful lieutenant

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil

#### Physical Description


Arcanus appears as a skeletal figure in ancient robes that seem woven
from shadow itself. His skull is yellowed with age but perfectly
preserved, and pinpoints of cold blue light burn in his empty eye
sockets. Arcane sigils cover his bones, etched there during his
transformation. He wears a robe of the archmagi and carries a staff
topped with a void-black crystal.

Despite his undead nature, he moves with surprising grace, and his
voice---though hollow---retains the cultured tones of the court wizard
he once was.

#### Background & History


Three centuries ago, Magistar Corvellian served as Court Wizard to House
Blackwood during their glory days. A brilliant wizard obsessed with
immortality, he performed the ritual to become a lich with the Blackwood
lord's blessing---on the condition that he serve the house eternally.

When House Blackwood fell in 1092 CR, Arcanus survived in the deepest
vaults of Raven's Keep. His phylactery was hidden in a pocket dimension
accessible only through specific rituals, protected from the Crown's
destruction. For over a century, he existed alone, guardian of Blackwood
secrets and prisoner of his oath.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

When Corvus Blackwood discovered Raven's Keep and proved his bloodline,
Arcanus' oath compelled him to serve. The relationship is
complex---Arcanus is bound to obey but has his own agenda, and his
centuries of experience often clash with Corvus' more urgent timeline.

**Dark Secret:** Arcanus has spent three centuries studying soul
transference. Corvus Blackwood, with his fey-touched Blackwood blood and
approaching death from the curse, represents the perfect vessel. The
lich hasn't decided whether to tell Corvus about this "gift" or
simply take what he needs when the time comes.

#### Connections


-   **Lord Shadows:** Master through ancient oath. Arcanus serves but
    also manipulates.

-   **The Blackwood Legacy:** Guards all family secrets and the Shadow
    Shard vault.

-   **House Thandris:** Witnessed their rise. Knows secrets about the
    dynasty that even they have forgotten.

#### Secrets


1\. **The Vessel Plan:** Intends to use Corvus as his new body when the
curse finally kills him.

2\. **The Hidden Archives:** Possesses knowledge of pre-Worldrend magic
that could change everything---if he chose to share it.

3\. **The True Loyalty:** Despite his oath, Arcanus serves his own
immortality first. He will betray anyone to preserve his existence.

### 44.4 Captain Malthus Voidcaller


**Military Commander of The Unbound**

**Full Name:** Malthus Voidcaller (adopted title; birth name abandoned)

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 45

**Current Location:** With Unbound forces

**Role:** Unbound Military Commander, Elite Soldier

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil (from his perspective, Lawful Neutral)

#### Physical Description


Malthus is a scarred veteran in his mid-forties with the bearing of
someone who has spent his life at war. His face bears the marks of
countless battles, and his eyes carry the weight of every soldier he's
commanded---and lost. He wears consecrated plate armor of excellent
quality, clearly taken from a previous life of legitimate service.

#### Background & History


Malthus was once a decorated officer in the Thaldros army, serving with
distinction for two decades. His family---wife and two children---lived
in a border village that was sacrificed to military strategy during a
conflict with Aethoria. When he protested, he was silenced. When he
sought justice, he was discharged. When he went public, his family was
"lost in a bandit raid."

![44.4 Captain Malthus Voidcaller](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-malthus-voidcaller.jpg){width:325px}

He knows the Crown ordered the attack. He knows the generals who
abandoned the village are now lords. He knows the system will never hold
them accountable.

Lord Shadows offered him something better than justice---he offered
vengeance with purpose. Now Malthus commands the Unbound's military
arm, bringing tactical brilliance and genuine conviction to their cause.

**Quote:** *"The system killed my family. I was a 'hero' once.
Decorated. Praised. I know exactly what heroes are capable of in the
dark."*

#### Personality


Malthus is quiet, measured, and tired. He speaks like someone who has
seen too much but keeps going anyway. Military precision defines his
every word and movement. He genuinely cares for the soldiers under his
command, referring to them as "my people" rather than followers.

He fights not for personal glory but to protect those under his command
and to ensure no other family suffers as his did.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

#### Connections


-   **Commander:** Lord Shadows Blackwood (absolute loyalty; Shadows
    saved him from himself)

-   **Peer:** Sister Mortua (respects her devotion, concerned about her
    methods)

-   **Former Life:** Commander Thrain Ironoak (served together in the
    royal guard, now enemies)

-   **Target:** Captain Thalia Lightbringer (represents everything he
    once believed in and hates himself for it)

#### Secrets (DM Only)


1\. **The Witness:** He personally witnessed Prince Aldric (eldest son
of King Aldric III) ordering the Blackwood murders during the Second
Blackwood Purge of 1204 CR. He has names, dates, methods memorized. If
he ever testified publicly, the royal family's legitimacy would be
destroyed.

2\. **The List:** Keeps a list of every soldier who participated in the
Purge. Has been systematically hunting them down for twenty years.
Fourteen names crossed off. Eight remain. One is now a respected general
in Kaer Thandros.

3\. **The Doubt:** Sometimes wonders if Lord Shadows' methods have gone
too far. The cause is just, but innocent people have died in Unbound
operations. He suppresses these thoughts, but they're growing stronger
with each civilian casualty.

4\. **The Daughter:** Has a daughter he's never met. now 19 years old.
Her mother fled when she discovered what Marcus had become. The
daughter, Sera Thornwood, is now a paladin of Aethor actively hunting
the Unbound. Malthus has been secretly protecting her from a distance,
redirecting Unbound operations away from her assignments.

5\. **The Exit Strategy:** If Lord Shadows ever orders intentional
targeting of civilians, Malthus has a plan to assassinate him and take
command of the Unbound, redirecting them toward legitimate military
targets only. He hopes it never comes to that.

#### Plot Hooks


1\. **The Confrontation:** Party captures Malthus. He offers information
about Crown crimes in exchange for promise to investigate. Will they
believe an Unbound commander?

2\. **The Daughter:** The party encounters Sera Thornwood, a zealous
young paladin hunting the Unbound. They discover her father leads the
very organization she hunts. Does the party tell her? Use her? Protect
her?

3\. **The List:** Party discovers Malthus' kill list. Some names are
people they know, a kindly innkeeper, a retired guardsman, a beloved
teacher. Do they warn the targets or let justice play out?

4\. **The Defection:** If shown proof that Shadows plans mass civilian
casualties, Malthus may switch sides, bringing troops, intelligence, and
legitimacy to the party's cause.

5\. **The Testimony:** He's willing to testify about the Purge
publicly, but only if guaranteed safety. Who can protect someone from a
king's assassins?

### 44.5 Sister Mortua


**Death Priest Deceived into Serving The Unbound**

**Full Name:** Sister Mortua (religious name; birth name forgotten)

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 45

**Current Location:** With The Unbound

**Role:** Death Priest, Religious Leader within The Unbound

**Alignment:** Lawful Neutral (being manipulated toward evil)

#### Background & History


Sister Mortua serves Mordain the Sentinel, god of death and judgment.
She believes death is natural, necromancy is obscene violation, and the
dead deserve rest. Grimly principled, she dedicated her life to ensuring
the dead find peace.

**The Deception:** Sister Mortua has been recruited by The Unbound under
false pretenses. She believes they are working to *prevent* the Second
Worldrend by recovering dangerous artifacts before corrupt governments
misuse them. She doesn't know about Lord Shadows' true goals or the
plan to wake Dragon Infernalix. In her mind, she's preventing
catastrophe, not enabling it.

**The Dark Past:** She was once a necromancer herself---converted after
her experiments killed her parents. Her younger sister was turned into a
vampire that Mortua has been unable to destroy. This guilt drove her to
The Unbound's "proactive" approach.

When the truth becomes clear, she faces a crisis: follow orders from
those who deceived her, or break her oath and oppose the very
organization she joined to serve justice.

**Quote:** *"Death comes for all. I merely arrange the meetings."*

#### Story Potential


Sister Mortua can be turned against The Unbound if confronted with their
true goals. Her testimony could expose the organization, and her crisis
of faith makes for compelling drama. Mid-combat, a successful persuasion
check revealing the truth might cause her to hesitate, switch sides, or
flee.

### 44.6 The Dread King

*Ancient Lich from the Northern Wastes**

**True Name:** Unknown (lost to history)

**Titles:** The Dread King, Lord of the Frozen Kingdom, Master of the
Dreadhost

**Species:** Lich

**Age:** Over 1,000 years undead

**Current Location:** The Frozen Kingdom (Northern Wastes)

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

**Role:** External Existential Threat

**Alignment:** Neutral Evil
:

![44.6 The Dread King](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-dread-king-undead-throne.jpg){width:325px}


#### Physical Description


The Dread King is ancient even by lich standards. He wears robes that
once were royal finery, now tattered by a millennium of decay. A crown
of bone adorns his skull, and a staff of dark crystal serves as both
weapon and symbol of authority. His eyes glow with centuries of hatred
and ambition.

Unlike many liches who preserve their physical form through magic, the
Dread King wears his decay openly---a reminder that death is his domain.

#### Background & History


Over a thousand years ago, during the chaos following the Worldrend, an
ambitious king in the far north attempted to achieve immortality through
forbidden necromancy. He succeeded---becoming a lich. His kingdom fell,
its citizens converted to undead servants. For centuries, he remained
isolated in the frozen wastes, building his forces, refining his magic,
and preparing.

Now, the Dread King moves south. His Dreadhost---an army of over 10,000
undead commanded by six Necromancer Lords---advances steadily,
converting every settlement they encounter. Villages become new
soldiers. The dead serve purpose.

**The Phylactery:** The Dread King's crown IS his phylactery---he wears
his own soul-prison, ensuring it's always with him. To truly destroy
him, the crown must be destroyed: either by dealing massive damage
(resistant to all but radiant and force), successful disintegration
magic, or casting it into volcanic fire.

#### Goals


The Dread King seeks conquest and conversion. He views the living as raw
material---soldiers waiting to be recruited. His Dreadhost grows with
every battle because the enemy's dead become his reinforcements.

His ultimate vision: a world of perfect order under his eternal rule,
where the chaos of mortal ambition has been replaced by the peace of
undeath.

#### The Dreadhost Composition


-   **10,000+ Zombies and Skeletons:** Basic troops, mindlessly obedient

-   **Wights:** Officers commanding smaller units

-   **Six Necromancer Lords:** Powerful casters serving as generals

-   **The Dread King:** Supreme commander

**Tactical Note:** Every battle strengthens the Dreadhost. Allied
casualties rise as undead within hours. Victory requires killing the
Necromancer Lords to stop the raising, then destroying the Dread King
himself.

### 44.7 Merchant Prince Davos Goldshore

**Ruthless Merchant and Primary Antagonist of Blood & Coin**

**Full Name:** Davos Aldris Goldshore

**Titles:** Merchant Prince, Lord of Goldshore Trading

**Race:** Half-elf

**Age:** 67

**Current Location:** Goldreach

**Role:** Merchant Prince, Criminal Mastermind

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil

#### Physical Description


Davos is a half-elf in his late sixties who looks decades younger due to
his heritage. He dresses immaculately in expensive but tasteful
clothing, projecting wealth without ostentation. His eyes are
calculating, his smile warm but never reaching those eyes, and his hands
soft---hands that have never worked but have signed death warrants.

#### Background & History


Born to a cadet branch of House Goldshore, Davos always resented his
cousins' legitimate status. Through shrewd deals, ruthless elimination
of competitors, and strategic marriages (both wives died of
"illness"), he built a trading empire controlling approximately 40% of
maritime trade between continents.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

![44.7 Prince Davos Goldshore](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/tirvandor-npc-merchant-prince-davos-goldshore.jpg){width:325px}


**The Takeover Plan:** Davos has spent decades positioning himself to
seize control of the main Goldshore house. He has forged documents,
bribed witnesses, compiled blackmail on Lord Aldris IV, and arranged the
deaths of potential heirs. When the elderly Lord Aldris III dies, Davos
will challenge the succession and claim the entire house.

**Criminal Operations:** While publicly opposing the Shadow Syndicate,
Davos secretly funds certain operations and receives a cut of profits.
He maintains a poisoner on permanent staff (seven business rivals
eliminated, never caught) and has insurance files on dozens of nobles
and officials.

**War Profiteering:** Davos funds both sides of several conflicts. He
has destabilization agents creating tensions between Thaldros and
Aethoria because war is profitable. He is not patriotic---purely
mercenary.

#### Personality


Publicly charming, privately ruthless. Davos projects warmth and
trustworthiness while calculating every interaction for advantage. He
uses people's names frequently, asks questions that gather information
while seeming casual, and makes others feel clever for accepting his
terms.

**Quote:** *"Gold opens doors that armies cannot breach, and silence is
the most profitable investment."*

### 44.8 Master Crimson (The Shadow Syndicate)

![44.8 Master Crimson (The Shadow Syndicate)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/tirvandor-npc-master-crimson.jpg){width:325px}


**Mysterious Leader of the Criminal Underworld**

**True Identity:** Elena Thornwood (current holder)

**Public Identity:** Unknown

**Titles:** Master Crimson, The Syndicate Master

**Race:** Human (current holder)

**Age:** Unknown (title has existed 40+ years)

**Current Location:** Unknown (rumored to be in the Free Cities)

**Role:** Leader of the Shadow Syndicate

**Alignment:** Neutral Evil (organization), with moral limitations

#### The Mask and the Title


No one knows who Master Crimson really is---that's rather the point.
The name has been used for over forty years, possibly by multiple
individuals. What's known: Master Crimson controls the Shadow
Syndicate's operations across central Thaldros, coordinates regional
operations through lieutenants, and appears in person only for the most
important negotiations.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

#### The Shadow Syndicate


The Syndicate isn't a traditional thieves' guild---it's a business.
Criminal business, but business nonetheless. They provide services:
smuggling, theft, assassination, information, protection. Everything has
a price, and Master Crimson sets the prices.

Under Crimson's leadership, the Syndicate has become almost respectable
in certain circles. They honor contracts, don't target civilians
unnecessarily, and maintain order in the underworld. Several city watch
commanders have quiet arrangements. Some noble houses retain their
services.

#### The Current Master Crimson


**Secret Identity:** The current Master Crimson is Elena
Thornwood---Captain Vex Darkwater's sister, who Vex believes lives a
quiet life in Silverpine. She inherited the title from her mentor ten
years ago.

**Moral Rules:** Elena has rules her predecessors didn't---no targeting
children, no slavery, limited assassination. Some lieutenants chafe at
these restrictions; others appreciate them. She has been slowly
preparing to dissolve the Syndicate and transform it into legitimate
business.

**Regional Lieutenants:** Silas the Fence (Silverpine), The Iron Hand
(Crossvale), Whisper (Goldreach), and others coordinate regional
operations under her direction.

### 44.9 Lady Morgana Blackwater


**Necromancer Ruler of Marshaven**

**Full Name:** Lady Morgana Blackwater

**Titles:** Lady of Marshaven, Mistress of the Thornmire, The Widow
Blackwater

**Race:** Human

**Age:** Mid-forties

**Current Location:** Marshaven

**Role:** Noble Ruler, Secret Necromancer

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil

#### Physical Description


Lady Morgana carries herself with the cold dignity of old nobility. She
dresses in dark colors befitting her widowed status and the perpetual
gloom of Marshaven. Her features are sharp, and her eyes miss nothing.

#### Background & History


Born to a minor noble family in the Thornmire swamps, Morgana married
into the Blackwater name---the oldest family in Marshaven. Her husband
died three years into the marriage under mysterious circumstances.
She's ruled the city ever since.

![44.9 Lady Morgana Blackwater](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/tirvandor-npc-lady-morgana-blackwater.jpg){width:325px}

Marshaven has always been overlooked: too swampy, too poor, too strange.
The continental powers take its taxes but provide nothing in return.
Morgana decided to change that.

**The Undead Army:** Using forbidden texts found in swamp ruins, she's
learned to create undead that retain their intelligence and free
will---not shambling corpses, but thinking soldiers. She currently
commands approximately two hundred such servants, hidden in the swamps,
with the number growing. Her plan: build an army where no one looks,
then declare independence.

**The Dragon's Interest:** Unknown to Morgana, the ancient black dragon
Morveth has been secretly encouraging her experiments---and waiting for
them to cause maximum suffering when they inevitably escape control.

#### Goals


Independence for Marshaven---by any means necessary. She sees herself as
a liberator, not a villain, believing the ends justify the means. The
continental powers have abandoned her people; she will give them the
strength to survive alone.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

### 44.10 Dragon Morveth (The Thornmire Terror)
![44.10 Dragon Morveth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/tirvandor-npc-morveth-shadowmane.jpg){width:325px}

**Ancient Black Dragon of the Thornmire Swamps**

**True Name:** Morveth

**Titles:** The Thornmire Terror, Mistress of Rot, The Patient One

**Species:** Ancient Black Dragon

**Age:** Over 2,000 years

**Current Location:** The Thornmire Swamps

**Alignment:** Chaotic Evil

#### Background


Ancient black dragon who has claimed the Thornmire swamps for two
thousand years. Unlike Infernalix's ambition, Morveth simply wants to
make the world suffer. She's been secretly guiding Lady Morgana's
necromancy experiments, waiting for the inevitable catastrophe.

Morveth delights in corruption, watching good intentions twist into
horror. Lady Morgana believes she discovered forbidden texts by
accident. In truth, Morveth planted them, and now watches with amusement
as the "liberator" builds an army that will eventually destroy
everything she loves.

\column

### 44.11 General Marthos Thandris

![44.11 General Marthos Thandris](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/tirvandor-npc-general-marthos-thandris.jpg){width:325px}

**Military Commander with Contingency Plans**

**Full Name:** General Marthos Aldric Thandris

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 58

**Current Location:** Kaer Thandros

**Role:** Supreme Commander of the Thaldros Military

**Alignment:** Lawful Neutral (with pragmatic darkness)

#### Background


Not a villain per se, but a dangerous man with contingency plans. A
distant cousin of the royal family, Marthos commands the Thaldros
military and has prepared detailed plans for seizing power if the
succession fails. His alliance with Lady Morgana Blackwater trades
political cover for intelligence.

Marthos served forty years in the military, rising through merit rather
than connections despite his royal blood. He's watched kings make
foolish decisions, seen good soldiers die for noble vanity, and
developed a deep pragmatism that some call cynicism.

**The Contingency:** In a locked vault, Marthos keeps detailed plans for
military takeover should the succession fail catastrophically. Not
ambition, insurance. He genuinely believes he'd be a better ruler, but
he'll never act unless the alternative is chaos.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

### 44.12 Warlock Kael Voidwhisper


**Unbound Warlock Losing His Mind**

**Full Name:** Kael Voidwhisper (birth name abandoned)

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 34

**Current Location:** With The Unbound

**Role:** Warlock, Magical Support

**Alignment:** Chaotic Evil

#### Physical Description


Kael is gaunt and hollow-eyed, with skin that seems slightly translucent
in certain light. His pupils are unnaturally dilated, as if always
looking at something just beyond normal perception. He mutters to
himself constantly, conversations with entities only he can perceive.

#### Background & History


Once a promising wizard's apprentice, Kael sought power beyond what
conventional magic could offer. He made a pact with a Great Old One, an
entity from beyond the stars whose very existence defies mortal
comprehension. The power he gained was immense, but the price was his
sanity.

The whispers never stop. The entity speaks to him constantly, sharing
knowledge that human minds weren't meant to contain. Each year, more of
Kael erodes as more of the Other fills the space.

Lord Shadows recruited him for his power, accepting the instability as
necessary cost. Kael serves the Unbound because the whispers told him
to, whether that serves Shadows' goals or something far stranger
remains to be seen.

**Quote:** *"The void speaks. I listen. You should fear what it says
about you."*

#### Personality


Kael alternates between lucid brilliance and dissociated rambling. When
focused, he's a devastating combatant and insightful advisor. When the
whispers overwhelm him, he might attack allies, share dangerous secrets,
or simply stand motionless while cosmic visions consume him.

He genuinely doesn't know if he serves Lord Shadows, the entity, or
some third purpose neither understands.

#### Secrets


1\. **The Entity's Name:** Kael knows his patron's true name, speaking
it aloud could summon something terrible

2\. **The Prophecy:** The whispers have shown him glimpses of the
future, including the party's role in coming events

3\. **The Cure:** There may be a way to sever his pact, but it would
require sacrificing someone else to take his place

### 44.13 Lord Crimson (Unbound Lieutenant)

**Corrupt Noble Funding the Revolution**

**True Name:** Lord Varen Ashford

**Titles:** Lord Crimson (Unbound codename)

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 47

**Current Location:** Ashford Estate (publicly), Unbound operations
(secretly)

**Role:** Financier, Commander, Infiltrator

**Alignment:** Neutral Evil

#### Physical Description


Lord Crimson maintains the appearance of a respectable noble,
well-groomed, expensively dressed, with the soft hands of someone who
has never worked. Only his eyes betray him: cold, calculating, always
assessing value and vulnerability.

#### Background & History


Born to wealth, Varen Ashford discovered early that money was simply
another form of power, and power was the only thing that mattered. He's
spent decades building a fortune through legitimate trade, illegal
smuggling, and strategic betrayals.

He joined the Unbound not from conviction but from calculation. Lord
Shadows' cause will either succeed (making early supporters wealthy and
powerful in the new order) or fail (at which point Varen will betray
them for immunity). Either way, he profits.

**Quote:** *"I invest in futures. This future looks profitable."*

#### Personality


Charming, cultured, and utterly without loyalty. Varen treats people as
assets to be leveraged. He's unfailingly polite because rudeness
creates enemies, not because he respects anyone.

He has escape plans prepared for every scenario. If the Unbound seems
doomed, he'll sell them out without hesitation. If they seem
victorious, he'll position himself as an essential supporter.

#### Secrets


1\. **The Escape Route:** Has a ship permanently provisioned for flight,
with enough wealth to start over anywhere

2\. **The Insurance:** Keeps records of every Unbound operation he's
funded, perfect for bargaining with authorities

3\. **The True Loyalty:** Loyal only to himself; will betray anyone for
the right price

**Note:** Not to be confused with Master Crimson of the Shadow
Syndicate, the shared name is coincidental and creates useful confusion
that both find advantageous.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

### 44.14 The Faceless Assassin
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/bc-faceless-assassin.jpg){width:325px}

**Legendary Killer Without Identity**

**True Name:** Unknown (possibly never had one)

**Titles:** The Faceless Assassin, The Unnamed, The Shape

**Race:** Unknown (appears human, but\...)

**Age:** Unknown

**Current Location:** Wherever needed

**Role:** Elite Assassin

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil

#### Physical Description


The Faceless Assassin has no consistent appearance. Every witness
describes someone different, different height, build, face, even gender.
The only constant: a sense of wrongness, as if something is missing
where a face should be.

Some believe the Assassin wears a magical mask that erases identity.
Others think they're a shapeshifter. The truth may be stranger, the
Faceless Assassin's identity has been magically erased, leaving them as
no one and everyone simultaneously.

#### Background & History


The Faceless Assassin has served multiple masters over decades, possibly
centuries. Records of their kills stretch back further than any human
lifespan, yet they show no signs of aging. They never speak, communicate
only through written notes that self-destruct after reading, and demand
payment in unusual currencies: memories, names, promises.

Lord Shadows employs them for the most sensitive operations. How he
earned their service, and what he promised in return, remains one of his
closely guarded secrets.

**Quote:** (Written on dissolving paper) *"You will never see me. You
will never know why."*

#### Personality


Completely amoral. The Faceless Assassin kills without pleasure or
displeasure, it's simply what they do. They've never been known to
break a contract, but they've also never shown mercy or accepted
excuses.

#### Secrets


1\. **The True Nature:** May be multiple people sharing a single magical
identity, or one immortal being

2\. **The Price:** What Lord Shadows promised them is potentially
dangerous information

3\. **The Weakness:** The magic erasing their identity requires periodic
"renewal---" they're vulnerable during these moments

### 44.15 The Ash Prophet

**Fire Genasi Sorcerer with Apocalyptic Visions**

**True Name:** Pyrius (fire genasi birth name)

**Titles:** The Ash Prophet, Voice of the Cleansing Flame

**Race:** Fire Genasi

**Age:** 43

**Current Location:** With The Unbound

**Role:** Sorcerer, Prophet, Fanatic

**Alignment:** Chaotic Neutral

#### Physical Description


The Ash Prophet appears as a fire genasi whose elemental nature has
grown dangerously strong. Flames flicker beneath their skin. Their hair
is literal fire, controlled but never extinguished. Their eyes glow like
embers, and the air around them shimmers with heat.

Ash follows where they walk. Paper ignites if held too close. They speak
in a voice that crackles like a burning forest.

#### Background & History


Born with unusual elemental power, Pyrius was drawn to fire magic from
infancy. A near-death experience during a volcanic eruption triggered
something, visions of a world cleansed by flame, purified through
destruction, reborn from ash.

These prophecies have proven partially accurate, earning Pyrius a
following among those who believe the old world must burn for a new one
to emerge. Lord Shadows recruited them for their genuine prophetic
abilities, though the apocalyptic fervor is harder to control.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

**Quote:** *"I have seen the cleansing flame. It is beautiful. It is
coming."*

#### Personality


Serene despite the terrifying content of their beliefs. The Ash Prophet
speaks of world-ending fire with the calm certainty of someone
discussing tomorrow's weather. They don't hate the world, they see
destruction as necessary transformation.

Genuinely kind to individuals even while planning mass conflagration.
Cognitive dissonance doesn't seem to trouble them.

#### Secrets


1\. **The Vision's Source:** Their prophetic abilities come from
accidental contact with a fire primordial's dreaming mind

2\. **The Truth:** Some of their prophecies are genuinely accurate, but
they can't tell which ones

3\. **The Fear:** Deep down, terrified their visions might be delusions
rather than divine truth

### 44.16 Cultist-Commander Theron

**Former Paladin Turned Unbound Leader**

**Full Name:** Theron Valoris (former title: Sir Theron)

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 51

**Current Location:** Unbound field operations

**Role:** Field Commander, Recruiter

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil

#### Physical Description


Theron still carries himself like a paladin, straight-backed,
commanding, with the physical conditioning of a lifetime warrior. But
his eyes hold a bitter emptiness where faith once burned. He wears armor
that was once consecrated, now defiled with Unbound symbols.

#### Background & History


Sir Theron Valoris served twenty years as a paladin of Aethor, rising to
command a chapter of holy warriors. His faith was unshakeable, until the
Temple of Light ordered him to execute prisoners he believed innocent,
children of a "heretical" sect.

He refused. He was stripped of rank, excommunicated, his family shamed.
His wife left. His children were taken. Everything he'd built was
destroyed because he showed mercy.

Lord Shadows found him drowning in a tavern and showed him that the
Temple's "heretics" had been right, and that the Temple had known and
covered up the truth. His faith didn't survive the revelation.

**Quote:** *"I was a hero once. Now I know what heroes really are,
murderers with better public relations."*

#### Personality


Cold efficiency masking deep pain. Theron no longer believes in anything
except the Unbound's mission. He recruits others by exposing
institutional hypocrisy, and he's very good at it.

He treats Unbound soldiers with the same care he once showed his
paladins. He fights with the same skill. Only the cause has changed.

#### Secrets


1\. **The Regret:** Part of him still believes in the ideals he once
served, just not the institutions

2\. **The Children:** His estranged children are now adult paladins
hunting the Unbound

3\. **The Mercy:** Sometimes lets prisoners escape rather than execute
them, old habits die hard

### 44.17 The Whispering Void

**Aberration Bound to The Unbound**

**True Name:** Unpronounceable (causes psychic damage to hear)

**Titles:** The Whispering Void, The Thing in Shadows

**Race:** Aberration (extra-dimensional entity)

**Age:** Unknown (possibly timeless)

**Current Location:** With The Unbound (contained)

**Role:** Interrogator, Psychic Weapon

**Alignment:** Chaotic Evil

#### Physical Description


The Whispering Void defies description. Witnesses report a darkness that
moves against the light, eyes that appear and disappear in impossible
places, limbs (or tentacles, or nothing) that reach from shadows.
Looking directly at it causes headaches and nosebleeds. Looking too long
causes worse.

It doesn't walk so much as exist in different locations consecutively.

#### Background & History


No one knows where the Whispering Void came from or what it actually is.
Lord Shadows found it (or it found him) in the deep vaults beneath
Raven's Keep, bound by ancient Blackwood wards. When he proved his
bloodline, the wards transferred to his control.

The entity serves because it must, but its goals, if it has any, remain
unknowable. It seems to feed on fear and psychic energy, growing
stronger after interrogations that shatter minds. Whether it's
genuinely loyal or simply waiting for the wards to weaken is a question
that keeps Lord Shadows awake at night.

**Quote:** (Psychically projected, causing pain) *"I am what waits. You
are what I wait for."*

#### Personality


Alien. The Whispering Void may not be sentient in any recognizable way.
It responds to commands, pursues objectives, and communicates (after a
fashion), but whether this reflects understanding or simply
stimulus-response remains unclear.

It seems to enjoy causing fear. Whether this is genuine emotion or just
efficient feeding behavior, none can say.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

#### Secrets


1\. **The Binding:** The wards controlling it are slowly weakening; in
perhaps a decade, it will be free

2\. **The Purpose:** It may have been summoned for a specific purpose
that hasn't triggered yet

3\. **The Connection:** Shows unusual interest in World-Splitter
Components, recognizes them somehow

### 44.18 The Necromancer Villains


These necromancers operate independently but may ally with various
factions or serve as campaign antagonists.

#### Glacius (The Ice Necromancer)
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-necromancer-glacius-frost.jpg){width:325px}

**True Name:** Unknown (possibly former academic name erased)

**Titles:** Glacius, The Cold Preserver

**Race:** Human (transformed)

**Age:** Unknown (appears frozen in time)

**Current Location:** Frostfell Crypts, Northern Wastes

**Alignment:** Neutral Evil

**Philosophy:** *"Cold preserves. Cold perfects. Death is merely warmth
leaving the body."*

Pale as snow with veins visible beneath translucent skin. Frost forms
where he walks. Eyes are chips of glacial ice. Formerly a scholar who
sought to preserve knowledge forever, now preserves corpses instead.

His frozen undead retain more personality than typical zombies, he
considers this an improvement. Seeks the Everice Heart, an artifact that
could freeze entire kingdoms.

**Secrets:**

-   Was once a respected academy researcher before an expedition to
    ancient ice tombs changed him

-   His frozen zombies remember their living lives, making them far more
    dangerous

-   Knows the location of a pre-Worldrend frost giant tomb

#### Kestra (The Blood Necromancer)
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-necromancer-kestra-blood.jpg){width:325px}

**True Name:** Kestra Sanguine

**Race:** Human (vampiric tendencies)

**Age:** Appears 30 (actually 200+)

**Current Location:** Crimson Spire, Blood Marshes

**Alignment:** Neutral Evil

**Philosophy:** *"Blood is life. I simply\... redistribute it."*

Crimson-stained fingers, lips perpetually dark. Beautiful in a predatory
way. Not a true vampire but uses blood magic that mimics their powers.

Seductive, hungry, every word drips with barely contained appetite.
Views mortals as resources but isn't wasteful. Has her own twisted
ethics about consent and worthy prey.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

**Secrets:**

-   Was rejected by a vampire clan, her blood magic was deemed
    "impure"

-   Seeks to create a new form of undeath superior to vampirism

-   Has a forbidden attraction to a paladin who hunts her

#### Mortis (The Plague Necromancer)
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-necromancer-mortis-plague.jpg){width:325px}

**True Name:** Abandoned

**Race:** Human (disease-touched)

**Age:** Unknown (constantly decaying and regenerating)

**Current Location:** Plague Warren, Thornmire Swamps

**Alignment:** Chaotic Evil

**Philosophy:** *"Disease is nature's way. I merely accelerate the
process."*

Covered in sores, wears layers of filthy robes. Flies constantly orbit.
Somehow maintains cheerful demeanor about spreading death. His touch
spreads disease, his breath carries contagion.

Wheezing, punctuated by coughs, disturbingly friendly tone. Genuinely
believes disease is natural selection and he's helping evolution.
\column
**Secrets:**

-   Was a healer who watched plague destroy his village, his mind broke

-   Carries samples of every disease he's encountered in specially
    preserved vials

-   Immune to disease but not to being hurt, very protective of his
    collection

#### Thraz (The Skeletal King)
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-necromancer-thraz-king.jpg){width:325px}

**True Name:** Unknown (slave name never recorded)

**Race:** Undead (skeletal)

**Age:** 300+ years dead

**Current Location:** The Bonefield, former slave burial grounds

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil

**Philosophy:** *"I was buried a slave. I rose a king."*

Skeleton in makeshift crown of finger bones. Built armies from mass
graves. Has twisted sense of justice for the oppressed dead. Wears
chains he died in as royal regalia.

Rattling, commanding, speaks of liberation through undeath. Sees himself
as revolutionary hero, freeing the dead from rest they never earned in
life.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

**Secrets:**

-   Remembers his slave life with perfect clarity, uses that rage to
    power his magic

-   Will not raise nobles or slaveholders, only common dead

-   Seeks the graves of legendary slave heroes to raise as his generals

#### Varis (The Academic Necromancer)
![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-necromancer-varis-classic.jpg){width:325px}

**Full Name:** Professor Varis Mordaine

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 45

**Current Location:** Academy of Forbidden Arts (hidden)

**Alignment:** Lawful Evil

**Philosophy:** *"The living waste life. The dead serve purpose."*

Typical necromancer appearance, pale, thin, permanently tired.
Surrounded by smell of preservatives. Takes notes constantly. More
professor than villain in demeanor.

Dry, academic, treats necromancy as scholarly pursuit. Genuinely
believes he's advancing magical knowledge. Frustrated that others
don't appreciate the elegance of his work.

**Secrets:**

-   Was denied tenure at legitimate academy, turned to forbidden arts
    out of spite

-   His research actually has valid applications if separated from
    ethical violations

-   Keeps a journal addressing his dead mother, seeking her approval

### 44.19 Unbound Agents and Allies


These NPCs serve The Unbound faction in various capacities.

#### Captain Blacksail


**Full Name:** Unknown (identity abandoned)

**Titles:** Captain Blacksail, The Pirate King of the Scattered Isles

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 52

**Current Location:** Aboard the *Void's Embrace*

**Role:** Pirate Fleet Commander, Smuggler

**Alignment:** Chaotic Neutral

**Quote:** *"The sea doesn't care who's king. Neither do I."*

Blacksail commands a fleet of twelve ships and over 600 pirates,
smugglers, and sailors of flexible morality. He transports weapons,
supplies, and personnel for the Unbound in exchange for territory and
eventual legitimacy.

He's not ideological, the Unbound pay well and promise him a charter to
rule the Splintered Isles when they win. If they seem likely to lose,
he'll simply sail away and find another employer.

**Secrets:**

-   Has a legitimate claim to a minor noble title he's never pursued

-   One of his ships is crewed entirely by intelligent undead, a gift
    from a necromancer ally

-   Knows the location of a pre-Worldrend treasure ship

#### Scholar Aldric the Fallen


**Full Name:** Aldric Moonshadow

**Former Title:** Professor Aldric Moonshadow, Chair of Forbidden
Studies (revoked)

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 61

**Current Location:** Unbound research facilities

**Role:** Magical Researcher, Artifact Expert

**Alignment:** Neutral Evil

**Quote:** *"Knowledge without wisdom is damnation. I should know, I
found both."*

Former professor at the Silverpine Academy, expelled for "dangerous and
forbidden research" after an experiment killed three students. What the
Academy doesn't admit: the research worked, and the knowledge gained
terrifies them.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

Aldric provides the Unbound with magical research, artifact
identification, and forbidden knowledge. He believes he's advancing the
cause of truth, though his definition of acceptable costs has expanded
considerably.

**Secrets:**

-   The experiment that killed his students also opened his mind to
    knowledge from beyond the veil

-   Knows how to safely disassemble World-Splitter Components
    (theoretically)

-   Still corresponds secretly with former colleagues who share his
    views

#### Mercenary Captain Vex Ironscar

**Full Name:** Vex Ironscar

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 38

**Current Location:** Wherever the contract leads

**Role:** Mercenary Commander

**Alignment:** True Neutral

**Quote:** *"I fight for coin. The Unbound pay well. That's all that
matters."*

Vex commands the Ironscar Company, 200 professional soldiers who fight
for whoever pays. Currently under contract to the Unbound, providing
security, training, and muscle for operations too dangerous for true
believers.

Not ideological. Not loyal. Would betray the Unbound instantly for a
better offer, everyone knows this, including Lord Shadows. He pays well
enough that it hasn't happened yet.

**Secrets:**

-   Has a standing offer from the Crown to betray the Unbound, hasn't
    accepted yet

-   One of his soldiers is secretly a Crown spy (he knows but hasn't
    exposed them)

-   Genuinely respects Lord Shadows as a tactician, which is the closest
    he comes to loyalty

#### Witch Morgana Shadowveil

**True Name:** Unknown (fey names are power)

**Titles:** Morgana Shadowveil, The Curse-Weaver

**Race:** Fey-touched Human (hag influence)

**Age:** Unknown (appears ageless)

**Current Location:** The Blackwood Depths

**Role:** Curse Creator, Dark Magic Specialist

**Alignment:** Neutral Evil

**Quote:** *"Curses are just promises the universe keeps."*

Note: Not to be confused with Lady Morgana Blackwater of Marshaven.

Morgana dwells in the darkest parts of the old forest, where hag
influence seeps through from the Feywild. She's not a hag herself, yet,
but she's bargained with them enough that the distinction grows
academic.

She creates cursed items for the Unbound: weapons that corrupt their
wielders, amulets that bring misfortune to enemies, trinkets that spread
plague. 

\column

Her prices are always strange, memories, names, promises, and
her services are always effective.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-morgana-shadowveil.jpg){width:325px}

**Secrets:**

-   Slowly transforming into a hag; has perhaps a decade before the
    change completes

-   Once was a village healer who made one bargain too many

-   Knows the true weakness of every curse she's created, insurance
    against clients who might betray her

### 44.20 Professor Miranda Questseeker


**Brilliant Scholar of Ancient Mysteries**

**Full Name:** Professor Miranda Elara Questseeker

**Titles:** Professor of Ancient Mysteries, Department Chair of
Probably-Shouldn't-Touch-This

**Race:** Human

**Age:** 35

**Current Location:** Aethoria University, Aethermere

**Role:** Scholar, Artifact Expert, Adventuring Academic

**Alignment:** Chaotic Good

#### Physical Description

Miranda is younger than expected for someone of her academic reputation,
thirty-five, with wild auburn hair perpetually escaping whatever tie
attempts to contain it.

{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 44: Villains and Antagonists}}
\page

Spectacles perch crookedly on her nose, and ink
stains cover her fingers regardless of how recently she washed. She
dresses in practical academic robes, pockets stuffed with books,
scrolls, and mysterious artifacts.

Her eyes light up with almost manic enthusiasm when discussing ancient
mysteries. She speaks rapidly when excited (which is always), and tends
to forget social niceties when focused on research.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/tirvandor-npc-professor-miranda-questseeker.jpg){width:325px}


#### Background & History


Miranda showed prodigious talent for magical research from childhood,
entering university at sixteen and earning her professorship at
twenty-eight, the youngest in Aethoria's history. Her specialty is
Pre-Worldrend artifacts and Primordial magic theory.

She's survived more "academic expeditions" than most adventurers
survive dungeons. The lich incident. The cursed library. The sentient
grimoire. The department stopped asking her to file safety reports
because they were too disturbing.

**Quote:** *"Tell me it's dangerous. Please tell me it's dangerous. I
haven't had proper excitement since the lich incident last year!"*
\column
#### Personality


Brilliant but chaotically organized. Enthusiastic about anything that
might kill her. Irreverent toward authority but genuinely kind beneath
the chaos. Talks fast when excited, forgets to eat when researching, and
has been known to break into restricted archives "for academic
purposes."

**Traits:**

-   Brilliant but disorganized

-   Enthusiastic about dangerous topics

-   Irreverent toward authority

-   Genuinely kind beneath the chaos

-   Talks fast when excited (which is always)

#### What She Offers


Miranda is the foremost expert on Pre-Worldrend artifacts and Primordial
magic. She can identify Components, explain their history, and craft
protective measures against their effects. Her academic connections
provide resources unavailable through other channels.

**Quote:** *"The Gods didn't MAKE these artifacts, they STOLE them
from beings that predate divine existence. This thing is OLDER than
theology!"*

#### Secrets


1\. **The Forbidden Archive:** Has memorized large portions of texts
that were supposed to be destroyed

2\. **The Truth About Aethoria:** Knows the founding myths of Aethoria
contain significant fabrications

3\. **The Book:** Is writing a comprehensive history that will expose
several powerful institutions, assuming she survives long enough to
publish
