## Chapter 59: Royal Regalia and Symbols of Office


The symbols of authority in Tirvandor carry weight beyond their material
value. Crowns, scepters, and ancestral weapons represent legitimacy,
bloodline, and the right to rule. Some date to before the Worldrend;
others were forged in the centuries since. All carry the accumulated
significance of generations.

### 59.1 The Pre-Worldrend High King's Regalia


Before the Worldrend, the High King ruled a unified continent from the
Palace of Eternal Spring. His regalia represented absolute authority
over all peoples and lands. When the cataclysm struck, these symbols of
unity were scattered, lost, or broken, their current status a permanent
reminder of what was lost.

#### The Sundered Crown


**Physical Description**

The Crown of the High Kings was a masterwork of magical craftsmanship,
combining dwarven metalwork with elven enchantment. It was designed as a
unified whole, but the Worldrend broke it into two pieces, a physical
manifestation of the continent's division.

*The Western Half (Held by House Thandris):* Forged primarily of iron
and gold, this half bears the martial symbolism favored by the western
territories. Mountains and swords are worked into its design. It feels
heavy with authority, weighted with the expectation of command.

*The Eastern Half (Held by House Aethermere):* Crafted of silver and
crystal, this half reflects the magical traditions of the eastern lands.
Stars and trees adorn its curves. It feels light but significant,
humming with ancient enchantment.

Each half bears half of an inscription. Neither house knows what the
complete inscription says, and neither is willing to bring their half
close enough to the other to find out.

**History**

The crown was worn by every High King from the founding of the unified
realm until King Aldric the Wise, the last to hold it whole. When the
Worldrend struck and the Palace of Eternal Spring was destroyed, the
crown was found broken, one half recovered by survivors fleeing west,
the other by those fleeing east.

Both Prince Theron (who became the first Thandris king) and Prince
Aethos (who founded the Aethermere line) claimed their half as proof of
succession. Neither would surrender their piece to the other. This
standoff has continued for 1,247 years.

**Significance**

The Sundered Crown is the most potent symbol of the division between
continents. Reuniting it would carry enormous symbolic weight, whoever
wore the complete crown would have a powerful claim to rule the
reunified realm.

But both houses fear what the complete inscription might reveal. What if
it names one brother over the other? What if it invalidates both claims?
What if it says something that neither side wants known?

The crown remains split. The question remains unanswered. And the
continents remain divided.

**Current Status**

The western half rests in the Royal Treasury of Kaer Thandros, brought
out only for the most significant ceremonial occasions. The eastern half
is kept in the Aethermere palace, similarly displayed. Neither has been
worn in centuries, wearing half a crown would be an admission of
incomplete authority.

#### The High King's Sword


**Physical Description**

Accounts describe a longsword of exceptional craftsmanship, its blade
inscribed with the founding laws of the realm, its hilt set with gems
representing each of the major houses that swore fealty to the first
High King. The sword was said to glow with inner light when wielded by a
legitimate heir.

**History**

The High King's Sword was last seen with King Aldric the Wise during
the Worldrend. When the Palace of Eternal Spring was destroyed and sank
beneath the newly-formed Sundering Sea, the sword was lost with it.

For 1,247 years, both House Thandris and House Aethermere have sponsored
expeditions to find it. The Palace ruins lie deep beneath the Sundering
Sea, in waters filled with dangerous currents, predatory creatures, and
the lingering magical chaos of the Worldrend itself. No expedition has
succeeded.

**Significance**

Whoever wields the High King's Sword would have an unimpeachable claim
to rule. The sword was the ultimate symbol of legitimate authority, if
it still glows for someone, that person is the rightful heir.

This makes finding it both desperately desired and secretly feared. What
if the sword recognizes neither claimant? What if it recognizes both?
What if it has been destroyed, and no one can ever claim its validation?

**Current Status**

Presumably at the bottom of the Sundering Sea, somewhere in the ruins of
the Palace of Eternal Spring. Both continents continue sponsoring
occasional recovery expeditions. None have returned with the sword. Some
have not returned at all.

#### The Royal Scepter


**Physical Description**

A rod of gold and silver, approximately two feet long, topped with a
large ruby that seems to contain flickering fire. The shaft is inscribed
with the names of every High King who wielded it. The final name,
Aldric, was never completed, the final letters trailing off as if the
engraver was interrupted mid-stroke.

**History**

Unlike the crown and sword, the Royal Scepter survived the Worldrend
intact. How it came to the east is disputed:

*Thandris Version:* Prince Aethos stole the scepter during the chaos of
the cataclysm, taking advantage of the disaster to grab symbols of
authority to which he had no right.

*Aethermere Version:* King Aldric entrusted the scepter to Prince Aethos
before the end, recognizing his younger son as the chosen heir. Aethos
carried it east as proof of his father's wishes.

Both versions have supporters. Neither can be verified. The scepter
itself offers no testimony.

**Significance**

The Royal Scepter is an obvious mark of authority, anyone who sees it
recognizes what it represents. Aethermere's possession of it
strengthens their succession claim, which is why Thandris demands its
return. Aethermere's refusal to surrender it suggests they consider
their claim legitimate, or that they fear what losing the scepter would
mean for their authority.

**Current Status**

Held by House Aethermere in the eastern palace. It is used in Aethorian
coronation ceremonies, though carefully, the Aethermere kings never
claim to be High Kings, merely the rightful successors to the High
King's authority in the east.

### 59.2 Thaldros Royal Regalia


The Kingdom of Thaldros has developed its own regalia over the twelve
centuries since the Worldrend. While they maintain the western half of
the Sundered Crown, the actual symbols of Thaldros royal authority are
items created since the founding.

#### The Iron Crown of Thaldros


**Physical Description**

A circlet of black iron set with a single large diamond at the front,
the Iron Crown is deliberately austere compared to the ornate Sundered
Crown. It represents Thaldros values: strength, endurance, and martial
virtue. The iron was forged from weapons taken from defeated enemies in
the wars of consolidation.

Unknown to most, including the current king, the Iron Crown incorporates
the Stone Crown, the Fourth Component of the World-Splitter. The
Component is embedded in the crown's structure, hidden in plain sight
for twelve centuries.

**History**

The Iron Crown was forged by King Theron I, founder of the Thandris
dynasty, during the early years after the Worldrend. He deliberately
chose iron over gold, stating that a king should be forged in hardship
like the metal of his crown.

The Stone Crown Component was incorporated during the original forging,
entrusted to the royal line as one of the guardian houses charged with
keeping the World-Splitter fragments separated. Over centuries, the
knowledge of what the crown truly contained faded. The current King
Aldric IV believes it to be merely ceremonial.

**Significance**

The Iron Crown represents Thaldros authority, wearing it marks the
legitimate king. It is worn at coronations, major state functions, and
when rendering judgments of particular importance. The crown's weight
is both physical and symbolic; kings speak of feeling the burden of rule
when it rests on their brow.

The hidden Component adds another layer of significance that most do not
understand. The crown's influence on political authority may not be
entirely natural, the Stone Crown grants subtle dominion over those who
would rule.

**Current Status**

Worn by King Aldric IV at ceremonial occasions, stored in the Royal
Treasury between uses. The king does not know he wears a World-Splitter
Component. Only a handful of scholars and conspiracy theorists suspect
the truth.

#### The Crown Jewels of Thaldros


**Physical Description**

The Crown Jewels are a matched set of three items, created together
during the reign of King Aldric II:

*The Ceremonial Crown:* A golden crown set with diamonds and rubies,
more ornate than the Iron Crown and used for less martial occasions. It
represents prosperity and civilization rather than conquest.

*The Royal Scepter of Thaldros:* Not to be confused with the original
High King's Scepter held by Aethermere. This scepter was created
specifically for Thaldros, a rod of gold topped with a large ruby. It
represents the king's authority to command.

*The Orb of State:* A golden sphere representing the world, symbolizing
the king's responsibility to his realm. It is held during coronation
ceremonies and certain state occasions.

**History**

King Aldric II commissioned the Crown Jewels to establish Thaldros
identity separate from the lost High Kingdom. He wanted symbols that
represented Thaldros specifically, not merely fragments of the old
unified realm.

The jewels have been used in every coronation since, and their presence
validates the transfer of power from one king to the next.

**Significance**

Together, the Crown Jewels represent complete royal authority, the right
to rule (crown), the right to command (scepter), and the responsibility
for the realm (orb). A king who possesses all three has full legitimacy;
losing any would damage that legitimacy.

**Current Status**

Stored in the Royal Vault beneath Kaer Thandros. They are among the most
heavily guarded items in the kingdom, protected by physical barriers,
magical wards, and elite guards.

#### Thrandil's Edge


**Physical Description**

A longsword of exceptional craftsmanship, its blade inscribed with the
Thandris family motto: "By Strength, Endurance." The hilt is wrapped
in dragon leather, the pommel set with a sapphire said to have been a
gift from the dwarves of Ironhold. The blade never loses its edge and
seems to glow faintly in moonlight.

**History**

Thrandil's Edge was forged during the reign of King Thrandil II, the
"Warrior King" who expanded Thaldros territory and defeated the last
of the border kingdoms. The sword has been passed from king to king ever
since, though not all have been warriors capable of wielding it
effectively.

**Significance**

The sword represents the martial aspect of Thaldros kingship, the
expectation that a king will lead from the front when necessary. Kings
who are skilled warriors gain prestige from wielding it; those who are
not face subtle questions about their fitness to rule.

**Current Status**

Currently wielded by King Aldric IV, who is a competent if not
exceptional swordsman. He carries it during military reviews and when
leading troops personally.

#### The Heir's Blade


**Physical Description**

A longsword slightly smaller than Thrandil's Edge, designed to be
wielded by a prince not yet grown to full strength. The blade bears the
inscription "A crown is earned through deeds, not birthright alone."
The hilt is wrapped in leather from the first horse each heir breaks,
personalized to the current bearer.

**History**

The Heir's Blade tradition began with King Theron III, who wanted to
ensure that his sons understood kingship was a duty to be earned, not a
privilege to be assumed. Each heir receives the blade upon beginning
martial training and carries it until coronation, when they transition
to Thrandil's Edge.

The current blade has been modified for Crown Prince Thorin, its leather
grip tanned from his first warhorse's saddle.

**Significance**

The Heir's Blade represents the transition from prince to king, the
period of preparation when the heir proves himself worthy. A prince who
never masters the blade faces questions about his readiness to rule.

**Current Status**

Carried by Crown Prince Thorin, who has proven skilled in its use during
his military service.

#### The Royal Signet Ring


**Physical Description**

A heavy gold ring bearing the Thandris family crest, a mountain peak
with a crown above it. The ring can be pressed into wax to seal official
documents, creating a mark that is legally equivalent to the king's
personal signature.

**History**

The original signet ring was created by King Theron I. It has been
passed down through generations, the gold wearing smooth with centuries
of use. The ring is never removed except for the coronation ceremony,
when it is formally passed from the old king (or his body) to the new.

**Significance**

Documents bearing the signet's seal carry the full weight of royal
authority. Forging the seal is one of the highest crimes in Thaldros,
punishable by death. The ring's presence on the king's finger is
constant proof of his identity and authority.

**Current Status**

Worn by King Aldric IV at all times. He has never removed it since his
coronation.

### 59.3 Aethorian Symbols of Leadership


The Aethorian Harmony developed different symbols of authority,
reflecting their different political philosophy. Where Thaldros
emphasizes royal power, Aethoria emphasizes wisdom, connection to the
land, and chosen leadership.

#### The Wisdom Crown of Aethermere


**Physical Description**

A delicate circlet of mithril and moonstone, designed to complement
elven features rather than dominate them. Unlike the heavy Iron Crown of
Thaldros, the Wisdom Crown seems to float on the wearer's brow.
Moonstones around its circumference glow faintly in darkness,
representing the wisdom that illuminates uncertainty.

**History**

The Wisdom Crown was created by Queen Aelindra I, founder of the
Aethermere royal line, as a deliberate contrast to western martial
symbolism. She wanted a crown that represented thought rather than
force, guidance rather than command.

**Significance**

The Wisdom Crown is worn by the reigning monarch of the Aethorian
Harmony, currently High Queen Aelindra III. It represents the
expectation that Aethorian rulers will lead through wisdom and
connection to their people rather than through force of arms.

**Current Status**

Worn by High Queen Aelindra III during formal occasions. Unlike the Iron
Crown, it is worn frequently, symbolizing that wisdom should be constant
rather than reserved for special occasions.

#### The Staff of the World-Trees


**Physical Description**

A living staff that grows and changes over time, connected to the
world-trees that form Aethoria's magical communication network. The
staff is rooted in wood from the original world-tree, grafted with
branches from each subsequent tree planted during Aethorian expansion.
Green leaves sprout from its length regardless of season.

**History**

The Staff was first carried by Queen Aelindra I, who planted the
original world-trees that would become Aethoria's communication and
transportation network. Each subsequent ruler has added wood from
world-trees planted during their reign.

**Significance**

The Staff represents the Aethorian ruler's connection to the land
itself. When the ruler holds it, they can communicate with the
world-tree network, sensing the health of the realm's forests and
receiving messages from far-distant groves.

**Current Status**

Carried by High Queen Aelindra III, who maintains daily communion with
the world-tree network through its connection.

#### The Eastern Sundered Crown (Aethermere Half)


**Physical Description**

The eastern half of the original High King's Crown, crafted of silver
and crystal with motifs of stars and trees. It bears half of the
inscription whose complete meaning remains unknown.

**History**

Recovered from the Worldrend by survivors who became the Aethermere
bloodline. They have held it for 1,247 years as proof of their claim to
High King succession.

**Significance**

Aethermere's possession of this half, combined with the Royal Scepter,
forms the foundation of their claim to be the legitimate successors to
the High Kingdom. They argue that Prince Aethos was the chosen heir, and
these symbols prove it.

**Current Status**

Displayed in the Aethermere palace, brought out only for the most
significant ceremonies. Like the western half, it is never worn, wearing
half a crown would acknowledge incomplete authority.

#### Valen's Pendant of Eloquence


**Physical Description**

A silver pendant set with an opal that shifts colors as the wearer
speaks. The pendant is warm to the touch and seems to pulse slightly in
rhythm with the wearer's heartbeat. It hangs from a chain of
interlocking silver leaves.

**History**

Created by the founders of the Aethorian Republic (before the current
Harmony structure) as a symbol of democratic leadership. It was given to
the first elected speaker of the People's Council and has been passed
to each subsequent leader of Aethorian diplomacy.

**Significance**

The Pendant represents Aethoria's commitment to persuasion over force,
to winning hearts rather than breaking bodies. The current Envoy to
Thaldros, Marcus Valen, wears it as symbol of his authority to speak for
the Harmony.

**Current Status**

Worn by Envoy Marcus Valen during diplomatic missions. It is considered
essential for legitimate Aethorian diplomatic representation.

### 59.4 Noble House Heirlooms


Each major noble house maintains heirlooms that represent their lineage
and authority. These items often carry as much significance within their
domains as royal regalia carries in the broader kingdom.

#### House Blackwood Relics


**The Shadow Rapier (Vengeance)**

Originally his mother's dress sword, reforged by Lord Shadows (Corvus
Blackwood) after her murder. The blade is made of Blackwood ancestral
steel combined with shadow magic, leaving trails of darkness in its
wake. The hilt is wrapped in shadow-silk, topped with an obsidian pommel
carved into a raven's head.

The rapier represents what House Blackwood became after their
destruction, instruments of vengeance rather than symbols of nobility.
Corvus carries it as both weapon and reminder.

**The Blackwood Family Shield**

A shield bearing the Blackwood family crest, a raven on a dark field.
This shield survived the Second Purge and now belongs to Marcus
Blackwood (Corvus' brother), living under an assumed identity near
Crossroads. The shield can prove noble heritage if shown to authorities,
though doing so would be dangerous for a Blackwood.

**The Blackwood Signet Ring**

A ring bearing the Blackwood seal that once legitimized house documents.
The ring that survived is worn by Corvus; it contains enough Blackwood
blood (literally, the ring was crafted with blood magic) to open the
blood-locked vault beneath Raven's Keep.

#### House Goldshore Relics


**The Goldshore Ancestral Blade**

A longsword with a blade of blue-tinted steel that always feels cold to
the touch. The crossguard is shaped like ocean waves, and the pommel
contains a sapphire that seems to hold a frozen wave inside it. Blessed
by an ancient sea-god and tempered in water from the deepest ocean
trench, the sword has defended Goldshore ships for six hundred years.

The blade was recovered from the sunken Goldshore Manor during one of
the plot events of the Shattered Oaths campaign.

**The Crown of the Depths**

A platinum crown set with blue-green pearls and aquamarines, styled to
resemble waves cresting. Once worn by House Goldshore's matriarch when
conducting underwater ceremonies, the crown allows its wearer to breathe
underwater, swim with supernatural speed, and command the respect of
aquatic creatures.

The crown was lost when Goldshore Manor sank during the Worldrend. It
lies somewhere in the underwater ruins, guarded by whatever now dwells
there.

#### House Ashborne Relics


**Desert Fang**

A scimitar that has been the weapon of House Ashborne sultans for three
generations. The blade is wickedly curved, designed for mounted combat
in desert terrain. The hilt is wrapped in serpent leather, and the
pommel is set with a fire opal. The current Sultan Rashid Ashborne
carries it, though he is more likely to use poison or politics than
direct combat.

**The Ashborne Signet Ring**

A heavy gold ring bearing the Ashborne crest, a desert sun over crossed
scimitars. The ring grants legal authority across all desert territories
that recognize Ashborne rule. Unlike most signet rings, this one is
actively magical, allowing the wearer to detect lies from those who have
sworn oaths upon it.

#### House Ironforge Relics


**The Forge-Master's Hammer**

The original hammer used to forge the Crown Forge of Kaer Thandros, now
a ceremonial item passed between Ironforge leaders. The hammer is said
to have been used by the legendary smith Durin Ironforge to create the
first masterwork weapons after the Worldrend. It cannot be used for
ordinary smithing, but for the most significant ceremonial forgings, it
is still employed.

**The Iron Covenant Ring**

A ring of pure iron bearing the Ironforge mark, given to those who hold
the unbreakable trust of the dwarven house. The ring represents the
alliance between Ironforge and Thandris, its continued existence proves
the covenant remains in force.

#### House Riverbrook Relics


**The Riverbrook Rapier**

A finely-crafted rapier that has been passed through the Riverbrook
family for generations. The blade is etched with flowing water patterns,
and the hilt is wrapped in blue leather. The current Lady Seraphina
Riverbrook carries it, proving herself capable with the blade as well as
the ledger.

The rapier represents the Riverbrook commitment to both martial
capability and administrative competence, the combination that has kept
their house prosperous for centuries.

### 59.5 Faction Authority Symbols


Beyond noble houses, various factions use symbols to identify members
and represent authority within their organizations.

#### The Black Raven Token (The Unbound)


**Physical Description**

A cold metal disc barely larger than a coin. One side bears the image of
a raven in flight, wings spread wide, rendered in tarnished silver
against black iron. The other side is smooth except for three words
etched in ancient script: "TRUTH UNBINDS ALL." The metal seems to
drink in light, and holding it too long makes fingers feel numb.

**History**

Lord Shadows created the Black Raven Token design as recognition symbols
for Unbound members. The raven references his family's heraldry, House
Blackwood's crest featured a raven, while the motto encapsulates the
Unbound philosophy: that truth, once revealed, will break the chains of
lies that bind society.

**Significance**

Carrying a Black Raven Token identifies someone as an Unbound member or
ally. Members use them to recognize each other in public without verbal
identification. Finding one on a body or at a crime scene confirms
Unbound involvement.

**Current Status**

Actively distributed among Unbound members. The tokens are magical; they
cannot be perfectly counterfeited, and Unbound leadership can sense when
one is destroyed.

#### Iron Guild Membership Tokens


**Physical Description**

Bronze medallions bearing the Iron Guild crest, an anvil crossed with a
sword, on one side and the member's identification number on the other.
Higher-ranking members have silver or gold tokens. The Guild Master's
token is platinum.

**History**

The Iron Guild established the token system to prevent impersonation and
ensure contracts go to legitimate members. Each token is registered to a
specific individual and cannot be transferred without Guild approval.

**Significance**

Presenting an Iron Guild token proves membership and allows access to
Guild halls, contract boards, and member services. It also identifies
the bearer as bound by Guild rules, attacking a token-holder invokes
Guild response.

**Current Status**

Issued to all Guild members in good standing. Lost tokens must be
reported immediately; found tokens can be returned for bounty.

#### The Magistrate's Robes of Office


**Physical Description**

Formal robes of deep purple with silver trim, worn by magistrates when
rendering judgments. The robes are enchanted to aid in the detection of
truth and lies. The silver trim depicts the scales of Thandros, god of
law and justice.

**History**

The robes were first created during the reign of King Aldric II, who
wanted to ensure that royal judges could discern truth from deception.
Each magistrate receives robes upon appointment and surrenders them upon
retirement.

**Significance**

Wearing the robes marks someone as an authorized dispenser of royal
justice. Verdicts rendered while wearing the robes carry the full weight
of the crown's authority. Wearing the robes fraudulently is a capital
offense.

**Current Status**

Worn by active magistrates throughout Thaldros during official
proceedings.

#### The Scales of Justice


**Physical Description**

An ancient artifact kept in the main courthouse of each major Thaldros
city. The Scales are actual balanced scales made of an unknown golden
metal that cannot be tarnished or damaged. When testimony is given near
the Scales, they tip toward truth or falsehood, a lie causes them to
swing dramatically.

**History**

The Scales predate the Worldrend; their origin is unknown. They were
discovered in ruins during the early post-Worldrend period and have been
used in courts ever since. No one knows how they work or who created
them.

**Significance**

Testimony given in the presence of the Scales is considered absolutely
reliable. Defendants and witnesses are brought before the Scales for
crucial evidence. The Scales cannot be removed from their locations and
cannot be deceived by any known magic.

**Current Status**

Permanently installed in major courthouses. Their presence is a major
reason why Thaldros courts are considered relatively fair despite the
kingdom's other problems.

#### The Peacekeepers' Badge


**Physical Description**

A badge of silver and gold showing clasped hands, one human, one elven,
above crossed swords. The badge is awarded to those who have served
peace between the continents at great personal cost.

**History**

The Peacekeepers' Badge was created after the last major war between
Thaldros and Aethoria, given to veterans who had fought for peace rather
than victory. It has since become a general symbol of cross-continental
cooperation.

**Significance**

Those who wear the Peacekeepers' Badge are recognized on both
continents as having earned the respect of both sides. They can cross
borders more easily, receive hospitality from either kingdom's
officials, and speak with authority on matters of continental relations.

**Current Status**

Rarely awarded in the current era of cold peace. Those who still bear it
are aging; a new generation has not yet earned the honor.

#### The Monument Coins


**Physical Description**

Commemorative coins minted to honor particular heroes or events. Unlike
regular currency, Monument Coins are not meant for spending, they are
collectibles and proof of participation in significant events.

**History**

The tradition of Monument Coins began after the Dragon Crisis, when
coins bearing the faces of heroes who drove back the dragons were minted
and distributed. Since then, Monument Coins have been created for
various occasions.

**Significance**

Possessing a Monument Coin proves the bearer was present for or involved
in the commemorated event. They are valuable as collectors' items but
far more valuable as proof of heroic service.

**Current Status**

New Monument Coins are minted when appropriate. Old coins from previous
eras are highly valued by collectors and historians.

*End of Chapter 54: Royal Regalia and Symbols of Office*

## Chapter 60: Weapons of Legend


The great weapons of Tirvandor carry histories as long as noble
bloodlines. Some have been wielded by heroes; others have corrupted
their bearers. All are significant enough that their locations and
ownership are matters of political concern.

### 60.1 Holy and Blessed Weapons


#### Mercy's Edge


**Physical Description**

A longsword of exceptional craftsmanship, its blade eternally bright
despite age or use. The hilt is wrapped in white leather that never
stains, and the pommel is set with a diamond that glows faintly with
inner light. The blade bears an inscription in an ancient tongue that
translates to "Strike True, Show Mercy."

**History**

Mercy's Edge was blessed by all Seven Ascended during a rare moment of
divine cooperation in the Age of Recovery. This blessing occurred when
the gods themselves appeared to the hero Aldric Lightbringer during the
darkest hours of the war against the Undead King.

The Undead King had risen from his frozen fortress with legions of the
dead, threatening to overwhelm the recovering civilizations that had
barely survived the Worldrend. Aldric Lightbringer, a paladin who served
no single god but honored all Seven, prayed for the strength to stop the
approaching horror.

All Seven answered. Thandros blessed the blade with unyielding justice.
Aethor infused it with the light of hope. Moira wove fate's protection
into its edge. Kael granted it swift fortune. Sera touched it with
merciful healing. Mordain bound it to death's proper order. Sylvara
rooted it in nature's resilience. The result was Mercy's Edge, perhaps
the only weapon ever blessed by all Seven Ascended simultaneously.

Aldric wielded the blade against the Undead King and struck him down,
ending the threat. But after Aldric's death from old age, the sword
passed through several worthy wielders before being lost during a battle
against dragon cultists approximately two centuries ago.

**Powers**

The sword grants its wielder immunity to fear and exceptional
effectiveness against undead and fiendish enemies. It can dispel evil
enchantments with a touch and protects its bearer from moral corruption.
The blade judges those who would wield it, the unworthy cannot lift it
from where it rests. Some who have tried report that the sword feels
impossibly heavy; others that it burned their hands.

**Significance**

Mercy's Edge is considered one of the holiest weapons in existence,
possibly the holiest. Its reappearance would be seen as a divine sign
that a great evil approaches and a champion has been chosen to face it.
Whoever wielded it would command enormous respect from the faithful of
all Seven Ascended, regardless of which god they primarily worship.

Religious scholars debate whether the sword could be wielded against the
Seven themselves, or whether the divine blessings would prevent it from
harming its creators. This remains theoretical.

**Current Location**

Unknown. Believed lost somewhere in the Contested Lands following a
battle with dragon cultists. Periodic expeditions search for it, but
none have succeeded. Some believe the sword will reveal itself when it
is truly needed, and not before.

#### The Dawnblade of the Knight-Commander


**Physical Description**

A longsword with a blade that sheds light like the rising sun. The light
can be controlled by the wielder, from a gentle glow to blazing radiance
that can illuminate entire halls. The hilt is wrapped in gold wire over
white leather, and the pommel is set with a large ruby that pulses
slowly like a heartbeat. The blade never dulls and is warm to the touch.

**History**

The Dawnblade was forged for the first Knight-Commander of Thaldros
three hundred years ago, during the reign of King Aldric I. The king
commissioned the blade from the legendary smith Durin Ironforge using
metal recovered from a fallen star and consecrated by the high priests
of all Seven temples.

The first Knight-Commander, Sir Aldric Dawnblade (who took the blade's
name as his own, establishing a tradition), wielded it to drive back a
vampire lord who had been terrorizing the northern territories. Since
then, the blade has been passed to each subsequent Knight-Commander at
their investiture ceremony.

The blade has seen service in every major conflict since its creation.
It was carried into the Dragon Crisis, where its light drove back the
shadow that Infernalix used to conceal his approach. It has been wielded
against demon incursions, undead risings, and human enemies who served
darker powers.

**Powers**

The blade's light can be intensified to damage undead and creatures of
darkness, causing them significant pain even before the blade strikes.
It enhances the wielder's martial abilities through divine inspiration
and inspires allies who fight nearby, granting them courage and
determination. The ruby in the pommel allows limited communication with
other Dawnblade wielders across distance, though currently, only one
Dawnblade exists.

Additionally, the blade can cast daylight once per day and its wielder
can sense the presence of undead within a moderate distance.

**Significance**

Carrying the Dawnblade marks the legitimate Knight-Commander of
Thaldros. Without it, claims to the position are legally questionable,
the blade's acceptance of a wielder is considered as important as royal
appointment. Two historical claimants to the position were rejected when
the blade would not ignite for them, ending succession disputes before
they began.

The Dawnblade is a symbol of Thaldros' commitment to fighting darkness
and protecting the innocent. Its existence reassures common folk that
someone stands between them and the horrors that lurk in shadow.

**Current Location**

Wielded by the current Knight-Commander Helena Dawnblade, who took the
title as her surname upon assuming the position following her
predecessor's death in the Dragon Crisis.

### 60.2 Royal and Noble Weapons


#### Thrandil's Edge


**Physical Description**

A longsword of exceptional craftsmanship, its blade inscribed with the
Thandris family motto: "By Strength, Endurance." The hilt is wrapped
in dragon leather taken from a wyrm slain by King Thrandil II himself,
and the pommel is set with a sapphire said to have been a gift from the
dwarves of Ironhold in recognition of the alliance between their
peoples. The blade never loses its edge and seems to glow faintly in
moonlight.

**History**

Thrandil's Edge was forged during the reign of King Thrandil II, the
"Warrior King" who expanded Thaldros territory significantly and
defeated the last of the independent border kingdoms that refused to
join the realm. The king named the sword for himself, establishing it as
the blade of Thaldros kings.

The sword has passed from king to king for over two hundred years. Not
all have been warriors capable of wielding it effectively, some kings
have been scholars, administrators, or diplomats who carried it only for
ceremony. But those who could wield it have done so with distinction in
battle.

During the Dragon Crisis, King Aldric IV's father carried Thrandil's
Edge into battle against Infernalix's minions, though he fell before he
could face the dragon itself.

**Powers**

The blade is supernaturally sharp and never loses its edge. It grants
its wielder confidence in battle and seems to guide the hand toward
effective strikes. Some claim it whispers tactical advice during combat,
though this may be legend.

**Significance**

Thrandil's Edge represents the martial aspect of Thaldros kingship, the
expectation that a king will lead from the front when necessary. Kings
who are skilled warriors gain prestige from wielding it visibly; those
who are not face subtle questions about their fitness to rule from
martial quarters.

The sword is also proof of succession. While the Iron Crown marks the
legitimate king politically, Thrandil's Edge marks him as a warrior.
Possessing both silences most succession challenges.

**Current Location**

Wielded by King Aldric IV during military reviews and when leading
troops personally. At other times, it rests in the Royal Treasury.

#### The Heir's Blade


**Physical Description**

A longsword slightly smaller than Thrandil's Edge, designed to be
wielded by a prince not yet grown to full strength but still capable of
serious combat. The blade bears the inscription "A crown is earned
through deeds, not birthright alone." The hilt is wrapped in leather
from the first horse each heir breaks, personalized to the current
bearer.

**History**

The Heir's Blade tradition began with King Theron III, who wanted to
ensure that his sons understood kingship was a duty to be earned rather
than a privilege to be assumed. The original blade was created
specifically for this purpose, a training weapon that was nonetheless a
serious instrument of war.

Each heir receives the Heir's Blade upon beginning martial training
(typically around age twelve) and carries it until coronation, when they
transition to Thrandil's Edge. The blade's leather grip is replaced
for each new heir, traditionally tanned from the saddle of their first
successfully broken warhorse.

The current blade has been modified for Crown Prince Thorin, its leather
grip tanned from his first warhorse's saddle, a stallion named
Stormhoof that he still rides.

**Powers**

The Heir's Blade is not magical but is of exceptional quality, light
enough for a young prince to wield effectively but strong enough to
serve in real combat. Its inscription glows faintly when wielded by a
legitimate heir of the Thandris line.

**Significance**

The Heir's Blade represents the transition from prince to king, the
period of preparation when the heir proves himself worthy. A prince who
masters the blade demonstrates readiness for the responsibilities of
rulership; one who fails to do so faces questions about his fitness.

The inscription is particularly significant. It reminds each heir that
their position is not guaranteed by birth alone, they must earn it
through action.

**Current Location**

Carried by Crown Prince Thorin, who has proven himself skilled in its
use during his military service in the northern territories.

#### Desert Fang


**Physical Description**

A scimitar of exceptional craftsmanship, its blade wickedly curved and
designed for mounted combat in desert terrain. The hilt is wrapped in
serpent leather, and the pommel is set with a fire opal that seems to
contain flickering flames. The blade is inscribed with desert prayers
and protective verses.

**History**

Desert Fang has been the weapon of House Ashborne sultans for three
generations. The first Sultan Ashborne, Rashid's grandfather, won the
blade in a legendary duel against a rival warlord who controlled the
oasis trade routes. The duel established House Ashborne's dominance
over the desert territories.

Each subsequent sultan has carried the blade, though Rashid's father
preferred poison and politics to direct combat. Rashid himself is a
capable swordsman but, like his father, prefers other methods of dealing
with problems.

The blade has seen combat in border skirmishes, bandit suppression
campaigns, and at least three assassination attempts where the sultan
was forced to defend himself personally.

**Powers**

The blade's edge is coated with a slow-acting venom that the Ashborne
alchemists refresh regularly. The poison is not immediately lethal but
causes weakness and disorientation, making it ideal for capturing
enemies rather than killing them outright. The fire opal grants the
wielder resistance to desert heat.

**Significance**

Desert Fang represents House Ashborne's dominance over the desert
territories. Losing it would be a significant blow to the family's
prestige. Rashid carries it primarily for symbolic reasons, its presence
reminds everyone that the Ashborne rose to power through martial
prowess, even if they now rule through wealth and cunning.

**Current Location**

Carried by Sultan Rashid Ashborne at formal occasions and during travel.
He is rarely without it, though he hopes never to need it.

#### Goldvein


**Physical Description**

A rapier with a golden blade and emerald pommel, designed more for
dueling than battlefield combat. The blade is inscribed with flowing
script that appears decorative but actually contains accounting
formulas, a subtle joke about the Goldshore family priorities. The guard
is shaped like intertwining coins.

**History**

Goldvein was commissioned by Davos Goldshore's grandfather as a
statement piece, a weapon that was undeniably valuable while still being
functional. The gold blade is magically reinforced to be as strong as
steel while remaining distinctive.

The blade has been passed through the Goldshore merchant princes, each
of whom has added their own poison to its edge. Davos uses a subtle
paralytic that allows targets to be questioned before they can flee or
fight back.

**Powers**

The blade is coated with a paralytic poison that must be regularly
renewed. The golden blade never tarnishes and the weapon grants its
wielder an air of wealth and success that aids in negotiations.

**Significance**

Goldvein represents House Goldshore's philosophy: appearance matters,
style is substance, and even weapons should be profitable. The blade has
never been used in open warfare, Goldshores don't fight wars, they
profit from them.

**Current Location**

Carried by Davos Goldshore, the current Merchant Prince of Goldreach and
leader of the Goldshore branch family.

#### The Goldshore Ancestral Blade (Frost Brand)


**Physical Description**

A beautiful longsword with a blade of blue-tinted steel that always
feels cold to the touch. The crossguard is shaped like ocean waves, and
the pommel contains a sapphire that seems to hold a frozen wave inside
it. Frost occasionally forms on the blade even in warm weather.

**History**

The ancestral sword of the main Goldshore line (not the merchant
branch), passed down through eight generations. It was blessed by an
ancient sea-god during the Age of Recovery and tempered in water from
the deepest ocean trench. The sword has defended Goldshore ships from
pirates, sea monsters, and rival houses for six hundred years.

When the main Goldshore line died out during the Keeper Massacre (the
secret guardians of the Flame Heart Component), the blade was believed
lost. It actually sank with Goldshore Manor during that disaster and
rested underwater for decades until recovered during the Shattered Oaths
campaign events.

**Powers**

The blade deals severe cold damage on every strike. On a perfect strike,
it can encase enemies in ice. Its wielder is immune to fire damage, a
protection that proved invaluable in battles against fire-breathing sea
serpents. The blade can freeze water it touches, creating ice bridges,
and glows brilliantly in cold environments.

**Significance**

The Goldshore Ancestral Blade represents the main Goldshore line's
naval heritage and their connection to the sea. Its recovery would prove
that the main line's legacy survives despite the Keeper Massacre,
significant for anyone researching the truth about what happened to the
Flame Heart's guardians.

**Current Location**

Recovered from the sunken Goldshore Manor during the Shattered Oaths
campaign. Current holder depends on campaign events.

#### The Riverbrook Rapier


**Physical Description**

A finely-crafted rapier etched with flowing water patterns along the
blade. The hilt is wrapped in blue leather, and the pommel is set with a
small aquamarine. The blade is lighter than it appears, designed for a
fencer's style rather than brutal force.

**History**

The Riverbrook Rapier has been passed through the Riverbrook family for
four generations. It was originally commissioned by Lord Riverbrook's
great-grandfather, who established the family's reputation for
combining martial skill with administrative competence.

The blade saw action during several border disputes and at least one
duel of honor. Lady Seraphina's father carried it into the Dragon
Crisis, where he died defending a refugee column. Seraphina recovered it
from his body.

**Powers**

The blade is of exceptional quality but not magical. However, its
perfect balance and light weight make it ideal for the quick, precise
strikes that characterize the Riverbrook fighting style.

**Significance**

The Riverbrook Rapier represents the family's commitment to both
martial capability and civilized refinement. Carrying it marks Lady
Seraphina as her father's heir in spirit as well as law, she is
prepared to fight for her lands and people, not merely administer them.

**Current Location**

Carried by Lady Seraphina Riverbrook.

### 60.3 Weapons of Shadow and Vengeance


#### Vengeance (Lord Shadows' Rapier)


**Physical Description**

A masterwork rapier with a blade that seems to absorb light rather than
reflect it. The hilt is wrapped in shadow-silk and topped with an
obsidian pommel carved into a raven's head. When swung, the blade
leaves trails of darkness in its wake.

**History**

The blade was originally Lady Elaine Blackwood's dress sword, an
elegant weapon she wore to court functions. After Corvus watched
soldiers murder his mother during the Second Blackwood Purge, he
recovered her sword from her body.

Years later, when Corvus had mastered shadow magic and made his pacts
with Primordial forces, he reforged his mother's sword into something
darker. Using Blackwood ancestral steel, shadow magic, and the cold fury
of justified vengeance, he created a weapon that embodies his purpose:
to destroy those who destroyed his family.

**Powers**

The blade deals necrotic damage on every strike, channeling shadow
energy through its edge. In dim light or darkness, it can blind struck
enemies. The wielder can become invisible in shadow and cast darkness
from the blade itself. The weapon feeds on justified anger, it grows
stronger when wielded by someone with genuine grievances against their
enemies.

**Attunement**

To attune to this weapon, one must spend a night in complete darkness
meditating on a personal injustice. The weapon feeds on that anger and
bonds with those who have legitimate cause for vengeance.

**Destruction**

The blade can be destroyed by exposing it to continuous sunlight for
thirty days, or by using it to strike down someone the wielder loves
while speaking their name. This destruction method is itself a form of
tragic irony, the weapon of vengeance can only be destroyed through an
act that creates new vengeance.

**Significance**

Vengeance represents what House Blackwood has become, or at least what
Corvus has become. Once symbols of noble guardianship, the Blackwoods
are now instruments of retribution. The sword is both weapon and
reminder: Corvus carries his mother with him into every battle.

**Current Location**

Carried by Lord Shadows (Corvus Blackwood).

#### The Void Staff


**Physical Description**

A quarterstaff of black wood that seems to absorb light rather than
reflect it. The top is set with a purple crystal that pulses with dark
energy. Shadows seem to deepen around the staff, and those nearby feel a
subtle chill and occasional whispers at the edge of hearing.

**History**

Lord Shadows created the Void Staff using shadow magic and fragments of
void energy obtained through dangerous pacts with entities that exist in
the spaces between planes. It took him three years to complete the
staff, during which he nearly lost himself to the void twice.

The staff was crafted specifically to channel the shadow magic that
Corvus specializes in, amplifying his abilities and providing a focus
for the darkest aspects of his power.

**Powers**

The staff enhances all necromantic and shadow magic cast through it. It
allows travel through shadow, creates zones of impenetrable darkness,
and can cast hunger of Hadar at will. On critical strikes, enemies may
be temporarily banished to a void-space. The staff also corrupts, those
who wield it must resist its influence daily or begin to lose themselves
to the darkness.

**Significance**

The Void Staff marks Lord Shadows as a serious magical threat capable of
manipulating forces that most mages consider too dangerous to approach.
Its existence proves he has accessed powers beyond normal mortal reach.
Destroying the staff would significantly weaken him, but might also
release the void energies contained within.

**Current Location**

Carried by Lord Shadows (Corvus Blackwood).

#### The Voidblade


**Physical Description**

A longsword with a matte black blade that seems to devour light. Runes
of death glow faintly purple along the fuller. The crossguard is wrapped
in void-silk, and the pommel is carved from dark crystal. Whispers
emanate from the blade in combat, the voices of souls it has claimed.

**History**

Captain Malthus Voidcaller commissioned this blade after losing his
family in the border conflicts between Thaldros and Aethoria. Consumed
by grief, he sought out a death god's herald and made a pact,
channeling his sorrow into the weapon. Each soul the blade takes feeds
the void within.

Malthus served as a mercenary captain in the Contested Lands for
decades, his blade growing more powerful with each kill. When he finally
died in battle, the sword was taken by his killer, who was in turn
corrupted by it. The blade has passed through several hands since,
always leaving tragedy in its wake.

**Powers**

The blade deals severe necrotic damage on every strike. On critical
hits, it can paralyze enemies as death energy courses through them. The
blade whispers to its wielder, urging them toward violence and feeding
on their grief. It grows stronger the more enemies it kills.

**Curse**

The Voidblade feeds on grief and loss. Wielders become increasingly
obsessed with death and vengeance, eventually losing the ability to feel
joy or hope. Most wielders eventually seek out dangerous battles,
half-hoping to finally fall and end their torment.

**Significance**

The Voidblade represents the danger of seeking power through grief.
Captain Malthus thought he was creating a tool for vengeance; instead,
he created a prison for his own soul and a trap for whoever came after.

**Current Location**

Unknown. Last confirmed sighting was in the Contested Lands
approximately twenty years ago.

#### The Unbound Dark Blade


**Physical Description**

A longsword of black steel that crackles with lightning. The blade seems
to vibrate with contained energy, and those who hold it feel power
surging through their veins, intoxicating, addictive, dangerous.

**History**

Created by Unbound artificers as a weapon for their cause, the Dark
Blade was designed to embody the Unbound philosophy: power without
restraint, freedom without limit. The blade was given to several Unbound
champions over the years, each of whom eventually succumbed to its
influence.

The blade's creators believed they were forging a tool of liberation.
Instead, they created a curse, the blade promises freedom but delivers
only a different kind of chain.

**Powers**

The blade deals additional lightning damage on every strike and can cast
chain lightning once per day. It cannot be removed without magical
intervention once attuned. The blade whispers to its wielder daily,
requiring them to resist its influence or become obsessed with power and
destruction.

**Curse**

The blade is cursed with obsession. Wielders become increasingly
convinced that they alone understand true freedom and that everyone else
is either an obstacle or a potential convert. The whispers encourage
ever-more-extreme actions in the name of "liberation."

**Significance**

The Unbound Dark Blade represents the dark side of the Unbound cause.
Even those fighting for justice can create tools of oppression. The
blade is both weapon and warning.

**Current Location**

Believed to be in Unbound possession, though some claim it was destroyed
after the last wielder had to be put down by his own allies.

### 60.4 Weapons of Nature and Forest


#### Red Wolf's Longbow


**Physical Description**

A longbow carved from ancient oak, its wood dark with age and care. Wolf
motifs are carved along its length, and the grip is wrapped in wolf
leather. Arrows fired from it make no sound, neither the release nor the
flight nor the impact.

**History**

The bow was blessed by forest spirits when Elara Thornwood, the Red
Wolf, first took up arms against those who had stolen her family's
lands. The spirits recognized her cause as just and her connection to
the forest as genuine, so they blessed her weapon with their power.

Elara carved the wolf motifs herself during the long nights in hiding,
before she had gathered followers, when she hunted alone in the forests
that should have been hers. The bow became her signature, the silent
death that struck from nowhere.

**Powers**

In forest terrain, arrows from the bow strike with supernatural
accuracy. The bow makes no sound when fired, and arrows in flight are
silent until they strike. The wielder can make additional shots beyond
normal capability through the bow's blessing.

**Significance**

Red Wolf's Longbow represents the Thornwood cause, justice sought
through guerrilla action, the forest itself rising against those who
abuse it. The bow is as much symbol as weapon, proof that nature
supports the Thornwood claim.

**Current Location**

Wielded by Elara "Red Wolf" Thornwood, leader of the Thornwood
Syndicate.

#### Thornstrike


**Physical Description**

A legendary elven longbow of exceptional craftsmanship, created from
wood so ancient it predates the Worldrend. The bow seems alive, its
surface shifts subtly, and those who hold it feel connected to every
tree in the forest. Arrows fired from it seem guided by the forest
itself.

**History**

Thornstrike was crafted by elven artisans in the Age of Dawn for a great
elven ranger-lord whose name is no longer spoken, he fell to corruption
and was erased from elven records. The bow, however, was reclaimed and
purified, passing through several worthy hands over the millennia.

The current wielder, Ranger-Lord Thalion Silverleaf, received the bow
upon assuming command of House Silverleaf's military forces. He has
carried it for over a century, defending the Silverwood from countless
threats.

**Powers**

In forest terrain, arrows from Thornstrike never miss their intended
target, the forest guides them. The bow grants its wielder perfect
awareness of the surrounding wilderness and the ability to communicate
with plants and animals. Arrows are never in short supply; the bow
generates them from forest matter.

**Significance**

Thornstrike represents the ancient bond between elves and forest. Its
existence proves that some things have survived from before the
Worldrend, connections and powers that predate the catastrophe.

**Current Location**

Wielded by Ranger-Lord Thalion Silverleaf, military commander of House
Silverleaf forces.

### 60.5 Weapons of Shadow Organizations


#### Kael's Poisoned Blades


**Physical Description**

A matched pair of shortswords with hollow cores containing concentrated
venom. The blades appear ordinary at first glance, the poison reservoirs
are hidden within the handles, with tiny channels directing venom to the
blade edges when a hidden mechanism is activated.

**History**

Kael Shadowbane, master assassin of the Black Chains organization,
commissioned these blades from a poisoner who specializes in creating
tools for professional killers. The blades have been used in dozens of
assassinations, each kill adding to Kael's reputation and the blades'
legend.

**Powers**

The blades can be coated with poison as a swift action by activating the
reservoir mechanism. The poison causes severe damage to those struck,
and the reservoirs refill naturally from the venom sacs built into the
handles, a disturbing innovation that required harvesting glands from
venomous creatures.

**Significance**

Kael's Poisoned Blades represent the Black Chains at their most
efficient, death delivered professionally, without emotion, as a service
rendered for payment. The blades are tools, nothing more, but they have
ended many lives.

**Current Location**

Wielded by Kael Shadowbane, master assassin of the Black Chains.

#### Blackblade


**Physical Description**

A greatsword of dark metal that seems to drink in light. The blade is
inscribed with runes that occasionally pulse with faint illumination.
The weapon is heavy even for a greatsword, requiring exceptional
strength to wield effectively.

**History**

Blackblade is an heirloom that has been in the family of Elite Guard
Commander Taran Steelheart since the Worldrend itself. According to
family legend, the sword was forged from meteoric iron that fell during
the cataclysm, a piece of sky-metal that landed in the family's
ancestral lands.

The sword has been carried by warriors in every generation since, each
adding to its legend. Commander Taran is the current wielder, having
inherited it from his father.

**Secret**

The sword whispers to Taran during battle. He has never told anyone
about this, uncertain whether it is magic or madness. The whispers seem
to offer tactical advice, where to strike, how to move, but they grow
louder and more insistent over time.

**Powers**

The blade is supernaturally sharp and scores critical hits more easily
than normal weapons. On a devastating blow, struck enemies must resist
or be stunned by the impact.

**Significance**

Blackblade connects Commander Taran to the Worldrend itself, a piece of
that catastrophe made into an instrument of protection. The sword's
whispers may be magical guidance, residual spirits, or something else
entirely, Taran is afraid to find out.

**Current Location**

Wielded by Commander Taran Steelheart, Commander of the Elite Guard of
Thaldros.

### 60.6 Amulets and Magical Foci


#### The Amulet of the Black Raven


**Physical Description**

An amulet bearing a raven design in black metal, hung on a chain of
shadow-links that seem to shift between solid and insubstantial. The
raven's eyes are set with black opals that occasionally seem to blink.

**History**

Created by Lord Shadows as a focus for his most powerful abilities and
as protection against those who would scry or track him. The amulet
incorporates fragments of Blackwood family magic dating back centuries,
combined with shadow-pact power obtained at great personal cost.

The amulet took years to create, requiring Corvus to sacrifice portions
of his own life force to power it. This is one reason he appears older
than his years, he has given pieces of himself to the amulet.

**Powers**

The amulet protects its wearer from all divination magic, scrying,
detection, mind reading, and similar effects simply fail. It grants the
ability to step through shadows for short-range teleportation and
provides powerful protection against all magical effects. Most
significantly, it serves as a phylactery of sorts, if Lord Shadows is
killed while wearing it, his soul is preserved within for potential
resurrection.

**Significance**

The Amulet is Lord Shadows' most treasured possession, combining
practical protection with deep personal significance as a connection to
his destroyed family. The Blackwood family magic woven into it is among
the last surviving examples of their ancestral traditions.

**Current Location**

Worn by Lord Shadows at all times. He would sooner lose a limb than the
amulet.

*End of Chapter 55: Weapons of Legend*

{{footnote Chapter 61: Cursed Items}}
