## Chapter 61: Cursed Items


Some items in Tirvandor carry burdens as heavy as their power. Curses
may be intentional, the result of corrupted creation, or acquired
through tragic history. All demand caution from those who encounter
them.

### 61.1 The Dread King's Crown

![61.1 The Dread King's Crown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-dread-king-undead-throne.jpg){width:200px,float:right,margin:5px}


**Physical Description**

A crown of black ice that never melts, set with gems of frozen darkness.
Wearing it produces an aura of supernatural cold. The crown whispers
constantly, promises of power, threats of destruction, memories of
ancient evil.

**History**

The Dread King's Crown belonged to the Undead King who nearly conquered
the recovering civilizations during the Age of Recovery. When he was
defeated by Aldric Lightbringer, the crown was seized but could not be
destroyed. It has been sealed away ever since, but its whispers reach
out to those susceptible to its influence.

**Curse**

Anyone who wears the crown begins transforming into an undead creature.
The process takes weeks but is irreversible once begun. The crown also
corrupts the wearer's mind, filling it with the Undead King's memories
and ambitions. Eventually, the wearer becomes a new vessel for the
Undead King's consciousness.

**Significance**

The Dread King's Crown represents the persistent danger of ancient
evils. It cannot be destroyed by known means and constantly seeks new
wearers. Its prison must be maintained, its guardians must remain
vigilant, and its location must be kept secret.

**Current Location**

Sealed in a hidden vault maintained by the Grave Wardens, a religious
order dedicated to keeping the undead imprisoned. The exact location is
known to only three people, none of whom can access the vault alone.

### 61.2 Lord Pembroke's Signet Ring


**Physical Description**

A gold ring bearing the Pembroke family crest, set with a small diamond.
The ring appears ordinary but carries a subtle corruption that affects
its wearers.

**History**

The ring was originally created as a standard noble signet. However,
generations of Pembroke arrogance imprinted upon it, creating a minor
curse that reinforces aristocratic disdain for common folk.

**Curse**

The wearer becomes increasingly arrogant over time. They begin viewing
commoners with contempt, assuming superiority in all situations, and
dismissing advice from those of lower station. The effect is subtle, it
feels like natural confidence rather than magical corruption.

**Significance**

The ring demonstrates how items can become cursed through use rather
than creation. It also explains, in part, why House Pembroke has
produced so many insufferable nobles.

**Current Location**

Presumably still worn by the current Lord Pembroke, who is unaware of
its effects and attributes his arrogance to natural superiority.

*End of Chapter 56: Cursed Items*


{{pageNumber,auto}}
{{footnote Chapter 62: Objects of Power}}

\page

## Chapter 62: Objects of Power


Beyond weapons and royal regalia, Tirvandor contains numerous objects of
significant power, items created for specific purposes, bound to
particular factions, or carrying importance far beyond their material
value.

### 62.1 Items of Justice and Authority


#### The Scales of Justice


**Physical Description**

An ancient set of golden scales mounted in courthouses throughout
Tirvandor. The design is simple, two golden pans suspended from a
crossbar, but the craftsmanship predates the Worldrend. Runes in a
language no living scholar can read cover the base.

**History**

The Scales of Justice are among the oldest artifacts in continuous use.
They were created during the High Kingdom era, before the Worldrend
split the continents, and have survived every catastrophe since. The
original set remains in the High Court of Kaer Thandros; copies (also
ancient) exist in major courthouses throughout both continents.

**Powers**

The Scales tip toward truth or falsehood during testimony. Those
speaking within their presence find lies more difficult, not impossible,
but requiring genuine effort. The Scales cannot be deceived by magic,
moved from their mountings, or damaged by any known means.

**Significance**

The Scales represent the ideal of impartial justice that transcends
political boundaries. Even during the darkest periods of continental
rivalry, courts on both sides have honored their verdicts. Some scholars
believe the Scales were created by Thandros himself, though the faith
officially denies creating artifacts.

**Current Locations**

The original set remains in Kaer Thandros. Secondary sets exist in
Aethermere, Goldreach, Ironhold, and Sundara. All are permanently
mounted and cannot be taken.

#### The Magistrate's Robes of Office


**Physical Description**

Deep purple robes with silver trim depicting the scales of Thandros. The
fabric shimmers slightly, and the silver threading seems to move when
observed in peripheral vision. Senior magistrates throughout Thaldros
wear these robes during official proceedings.

**History**

The robes were created by the Temple of Thandros as gifts to the secular
courts, establishing a connection between religious law and civil law
that persists to this day. Each set is individually enchanted and
tracked; losing one's robes is considered a grave matter.

**Powers**

The robes enhance their wearer's ability to detect deception and
investigate evidence. They provide mental protection against attempts to
charm or influence the magistrate. Once per day, the wearer can invoke a
zone of truth during proceedings.

**Significance**

Wearing fraudulent Magistrate's Robes is a capital offense in Thaldros,
one of the few crimes that carries automatic death penalty. The robes
represent the sacred trust placed in judicial officers and the
expectation that they will render fair judgment.

**Current Locations**

Worn by senior magistrates throughout Thaldros. Each set is registered
and tracked. Magistrate Ravens in Kaer Thandros wears one of the oldest
and most powerful sets.

#### The Peacekeepers' Badge


**Physical Description**

A badge of silver and gold showing clasped hands, one human, one elven,
above crossed swords. The design symbolizes peace achieved through
mutual respect and the willingness to defend it. Each badge is
personally crafted for its recipient.

**History**

The Peacekeepers' Badge tradition began during the last major peace
treaty between Thaldros and Aethoria. Heroes who served the cause of
peace, regardless of which side they originally came from, were honored
with these badges as recognition of their service.

**Powers**

The badge grants its wearer authority recognized by officials on both
continents. It provides advantages when dealing with bureaucracy and
border crossings. Guards and soldiers on both sides are trained to
recognize and respect the badge.

**Significance**

Peacekeepers' Badges cannot be bought, sold, or transferred. They are
awarded for genuine service to peace between the continents. Possessing
one marks the bearer as a hero trusted by both sides, a rare and
valuable status in a world where continental loyalty is often assumed.

**Current Locations**

Worn by their recipients. The most recent badges were awarded following
the Dragon Crisis and the events of the Blood & Coin campaign.

### 62.2 Items of Prophecy and Knowledge


#### The Prophecy Fragment


**Physical Description**

A fragment of ancient scroll, its edges burned and crumbling. The text
is written in Old Common, barely legible, in faded ink that might once
have been red. The fragment radiates faint magical energy and is warm to
the touch.

**History**

The Prophecy Fragment is one of several pieces of the Codex of Endings,
an ancient text that predicted the Worldrend and, some believe, predicts
events yet to come. The complete Codex was destroyed (or hidden) before
the Worldrend, but fragments survive in various locations.

**Contents**

The fragment contains cryptic verses:

*"\...when shadows wear the face of justice\...*

*\...and vengeance claims the name of truth\...*

*\...five fragments sundered shall seek reunion\...*

*\...the wound that broke the world shall bleed again\..."*

*"\...the last of the fallen house shall rise\...*

*\...bearing grief older than kingdoms\...*

*\...and the choice shall fall to strangers\...*

*\...to heal the wound or let it consume all\..."*

**Significance**

The prophecy appears to describe Lord Shadows' quest for the
World-Splitter Components. "Shadows wearing justice" refers to Corvus
Blackwood. "Five fragments sundered" are the Components. "Last of the
fallen house" is the surviving Blackwood heir. The verses suggest that
outsiders, adventurers, will ultimately determine whether the world is
saved or destroyed.

**Current Locations**

Fragments exist in the Thornwood Shrine, various ancient temples, and in
the collections of those who study prophecy. Finding all pieces would
reveal the complete prediction, for good or ill.

#### The Orb of Prophecy


**Physical Description**

A crystal orb approximately six inches in diameter, filled with swirling
mists that shift between colors. Visions appear within the mists to
those attuned to the orb. The surface is always slightly warm, and the
mists react to strong emotions.

**History**

The Orb of Prophecy was created by the Temple of Moira centuries ago as
a tool for their seers. It has passed through many hands since, some
worthy, some not. The orb seems to choose its own path, appearing where
it is needed rather than where it is wanted.

**Powers**

The orb allows scrying, divination, and communion with divine powers.
Interpreting its visions requires skill, the images are symbolic rather
than literal, and many have been led astray by misunderstanding what
they saw.

**Significance**

The Orb is one of the most powerful divination tools in existence, but
its cryptic nature makes it as dangerous as it is useful. Those who rely
too heavily on its visions often find themselves fulfilling prophecies
they sought to avoid.

**Current Location**

The orb's location changes. It has been reported in the Starfall
Observatory, various Moira temples, and in the possession of private
collectors. Some believe it moves itself.

#### The Book of Forgotten Names


**Physical Description**

A massive tome bound in leather that seems to absorb light. The pages
are made from an unknown material, not paper, not parchment, not vellum.
Text appears and disappears on its pages, and no two readers see the
same contents.

**History**

The Book of Forgotten Names is believed to predate the Worldrend,
possibly predating the current age entirely. It contains the true names
of beings, places, and concepts, names that grant power over the named.
How it came to exist is unknown; some believe it writes itself.

**Powers**

The book contains twenty spells of various levels, which can be learned
through study, though each spell carries a risk of mental corruption.
The book can reveal true names, cast legend lore, and provide
information that no living source possesses.

**Dangers**

Reading the book is dangerous. Each spell learned requires mental
resistance to avoid corruption. The true names it reveals carry their
own dangers, knowing a being's true name grants power over it, but also
draws its attention.

**Significance**

The Book of Forgotten Names is sought by scholars, wizards, and those
who wish to control others. Possessing it marks one as either a great
sage or a dangerous fool, sometimes both.

**Current Location**

Unknown. The book appears and disappears according to its own logic. It
has been reported in the libraries of Aethermere, the vaults of Kaer
Thandros, and in the possession of various powerful mages.

#### The Staff of Dynasties


**Physical Description**

A staff of pale wood topped with an emerald-studded crown design. The
wood is from a tree that no longer grows, and the emeralds glow faintly
when the staff is used. The crown design changes subtly depending on who
holds it, always resembling the royal regalia of the holder's homeland.

**History**

The Staff of Dynasties was created by a mage who served as advisor to
multiple royal houses. Frustrated by false claimants and disputed
successions, he created a tool that could reveal the truth of
bloodlines. The staff has been used to settle dozens of succession
disputes, and to start a few when its revelations proved inconvenient.

**Powers**

The staff grants advantage on persuasion with nobility, who recognize
its authenticity. Once per day, it can cast legend lore. Most
importantly, it can reveal true bloodlines, showing who is genuinely
descended from whom, regardless of official records or family claims.

**Significance**

The Staff of Dynasties is politically explosive. Its revelations about
bloodlines could delegitimize ruling families or validate claims that
have been suppressed for generations. Many powerful people would prefer
it destroyed or permanently hidden.

**Current Location**

The staff moves between various collections. It has been seen in the
Royal Treasury of Thaldros, the archives of Aethermere, and in the
possession of private collectors who understand its value, and danger.

### 62.3 Faction-Specific Items


#### The Black Ledger


**Physical Description**

A leather-bound ledger, unremarkable in appearance except for a small
symbol on the cover, a coin split by a dagger. The pages are filled with
names, numbers, and transactions in coded shorthand.

**History**

The Black Ledger was created and maintained by Lord Pembroke as an
insurance policy. It contains records of every bribe, forged deed,
fraudulent contract, and corrupt magistrate the Merchant Consortium has
employed. Pembroke kept it as protection, if he fell, others would fall
with him.

**Powers**

The ledger has a magical lock that self-destructs if opened by the wrong
person. The information within is worth far more than the object itself,
it could bring down the Merchant Consortium and expose corruption
throughout Thaldros.

**Significance**

Whoever possesses the Black Ledger holds leverage over dozens of
powerful people. It could be used for blackmail, for justice, or for
destruction of the corrupt system it documents. The Consortium wants it
destroyed; reformers want it published; and opportunists want it for
profit.

**Current Location**

Hidden in the Pembroke Estate vault. During the Blood & Coin campaign,
adventurers may recover it, the consequences of that recovery shape the
future of Thaldros commerce.

#### Ring of Shadows


**Physical Description**

A simple black ring that seems to deepen the shadows around its wearer.
The metal is unidentifiable, not quite iron, not quite obsidian, but
something in between. It feels slightly cold to the touch.

**History**

Rings of Shadows are standard issue for senior members of the Black
Chains assassin organization. They are created in a secret forge and
distributed only to those who have proven themselves through successful
contracts. Possessing one marks the bearer as a professional killer of
significant accomplishment.

**Powers**

The ring enhances stealth, particularly in dim lighting. It allows the
wearer to pass without trace once per day. Shadows seem to gather around
the wearer, providing concealment even in moderate light.

**Significance**

Possessing a Ring of Shadows without being a Black Chains member is
dangerous, the organization protects its symbols jealously. However, the
ring is useful enough that some take the risk.

**Current Location**

Worn by senior Black Chains assassins throughout Tirvandor. Kael
Shadowbane, master assassin of the organization, wears a particularly
powerful variant.

#### The Cloak of the Thornwood


**Physical Description**

A cloak woven from actual thorn vines, though it is surprisingly
comfortable to wear. The thorns lie flat against the fabric when worn by
an ally of the forest but rise threateningly when enemies approach. The
cloak changes color with the seasons, green in spring and summer, brown
and gold in autumn, gray in winter.

**History**

The Cloak of the Thornwood was created by forest spirits who blessed
Elara "Red Wolf" Thornwood when she first took up arms against those
who had stolen her family's lands. The spirits recognized her as a true
protector of the forest, not merely someone using it for shelter.

**Powers**

The cloak grants advantage on stealth in natural terrain, allows passage
without trace once per day, provides resistance to poison, and permits
communication with plants. The thorns can be commanded to attack enemies
who grasp the wearer.

**Significance**

The cloak marks Red Wolf as blessed by the forest itself, a distinction
that grants her authority among druids, rangers, and others who serve
nature. It is proof that her cause is just, at least in the eyes of the
wild.

**Current Location**

Worn by Elara "Red Wolf" Thornwood, leader of the Thornwood Syndicate.

#### Valen's Pendant of Eloquence


**Physical Description**

A silver pendant containing a color-shifting opal that seems to hold
captured sunlight. The pendant is warm to the touch and seems to vibrate
slightly during important speeches or negotiations.

**History**

The Pendant of Eloquence was a gift from Aethoria's founders to the
first speaker of their democratic assembly. It has been passed to each
subsequent speaker and Senate leader, symbolizing the importance of
persuasion over force in Aethorian governance.

**Powers**

The pendant enhances persuasion and public speaking. It allows the
casting of charm and suggestion spells, though using these on fellow
senators is considered deeply dishonorable. The opal glows when the
wearer speaks truth and dims when they lie, a feature that makes
deception difficult.

**Significance**

The pendant represents Aethorian democratic ideals, the belief that
words and reason should triumph over violence and coercion. Envoy Marcus
Valen wears it during his diplomatic missions, and it has helped
negotiate treaties that saved thousands of lives.

**Current Location**

Worn by Envoy Marcus Valen, chief diplomat of the Aethorian Harmony.

### 62.4 Items of the Undead


#### The Dread King's Staff


**Physical Description**

A staff carved from darkwood, its surface covered in runes that glow
with sickly green light. The top is capped with an obsidian skull whose
eye sockets burn with cold fire. The staff is cold to the touch, and
living creatures feel uncomfortable merely standing near it.

**History**

The Dread King's Staff was created by the Undead King during the Age of
Recovery as a focus for his necromantic power. When Aldric Lightbringer
defeated him, the staff was seized and sealed away. It has since been
recovered by those who sought to restore the Dread King's power.

**Powers**

The staff massively enhances necromantic magic, allows the creation of
undead armies, and serves as a devastating melee weapon dealing necrotic
damage. Its power is undeniable, and its corruption equally so.

**Curse**

Each use of the staff's greater powers requires the wielder to resist
necrotic corruption. Those who fail gradually become more like the
undead they create, cold, distant, obsessed with death and preservation.

**Significance**

The Dread King's Staff represents one of the greatest necromantic
focuses ever created. Whoever wields it commands power over death
itself, but risks becoming death's servant rather than its master.

**Current Location**

Wielded by the current Dread King (the restored Undead King) in the
Frostfell Crypts. It can be claimed by those who defeat him.

#### The Dread Crown (Phylactery)


**Physical Description**

A crown of black ice that never melts, set with gems of frozen darkness.
The crown whispers constantly, promises, threats, memories of ancient
evil. Wearing it provides instant power and inevitable doom.

**History**

The Dread Crown was created by the original Undead King as his
phylactery, the vessel containing his soul. Unlike most liches, who hide
their phylacteries in secret locations, the Undead King wore his on his
head, ensuring it would never be far from his grasp.

**Powers**

The crown grants massive mental enhancement, the ability to read and
dominate minds, and immunity to aging. These powers are seductive, and
they are the trap.

**Curse**

Wearing the crown begins an irreversible transformation into a lich. The
process takes approximately one year, but becomes irreversible after one
month. The wearer's alignment shifts to evil, their body decays while
remaining animate, and eventually, the original Undead King's
consciousness awakens within them.

**Significance**

The Dread Crown is both the source of the Dread King's power and the
key to destroying him permanently. While it exists, he will eventually
return, but destroying it while he "lives" is nearly impossible. The
crown must be destroyed while the Dread King is defeated but before he
regenerates.

**Destruction**

The crown can be destroyed by dealing massive damage from radiant or
force sources, by disintegration magic, or by casting it into a volcano.
These methods only work when the Dread King is currently "dead."

**Current Location**

Worn by the Dread King, even when he is temporarily destroyed.

### 62.5 Items of Ice and Winter


#### The Ice Golem Heart


**Physical Description**

A crystalline heart that radiates constant cold. Frost forms on any
surface it touches, and those who hold it feel the chill seeping into
their bones. The crystal pulses slowly with an inner light that
resembles a frozen flame.

**History**

Ice Golem Hearts are harvested from destroyed Ice Golems, massive
constructs created by ancient frost magic. Each heart represents the
core of a being that was never truly alive but was animated by elemental
cold.

**Powers**

Carrying an Ice Golem Heart grants resistance to cold and immunity to
exhaustion from cold environments. Once per day, the bearer can unleash
the heart's power as a devastating cone of cold.

**Significance**

Ice Golem Hearts are valuable both for their magical properties and
their rarity. Ice Golems are dangerous to fight and relatively rare;
their hearts are correspondingly precious to collectors and cold-weather
travelers.

**Current Location**

Ice Golem Hearts can be harvested from defeated Ice Golems. They are
occasionally found in treasure hoards or magical item shops, though the
prices are substantial.

#### The Eternal Winter Shard


**Physical Description**

A shard of ice that never melts, even in fire. The shard is clear as
glass but cold as death. Those who touch it with bare skin risk
frostbite within seconds. It glows faintly with blue-white light in
darkness.

**History**

Eternal Winter Shards are fragments of primordial ice, the frozen
essence of the concept of cold itself. They were created during the
formation of the world and have survived unchanged since the beginning
of time. How they come to be found is unknown; some believe they surface
during particularly harsh winters.

**Powers**

The shard provides resistance to cold, enhances cold-based magic, and
serves as a potent focus for ice spells. Once per day, the wielder can
call down a devastating ice storm.

**Significance**

Eternal Winter Shards are among the most valuable magical components in
existence. Wizards who specialize in cold magic seek them desperately,
and collectors pay fortunes for authentic specimens.

**Current Location**

Eternal Winter Shards appear rarely and are quickly claimed. They exist
in various magical collections, wizard towers, and occasionally in the
hordes of frost-based creatures.

#### The Cloak of the Frozen Wastes


**Physical Description**

A heavy cloak of white fur that seems to blend with snow and ice. The
fur is from no identifiable animal, and it never gets wet or dirty. The
cloak is surprisingly warm, protecting its wearer from the worst cold
while remaining light and easy to wear.

**History**

Cloaks of the Frozen Wastes were created by the frost giants for their
human allies during an ancient war against fire giants. When the
alliance ended, many cloaks remained with the human tribes of the north,
passed down through generations as treasured heirlooms.

**Powers**

The cloak grants advantage on saves against cold effects and the ability
to cast ice storm once per day. Its warmth keeps the wearer comfortable
in temperatures that would kill ordinary travelers.

**Significance**

In the Frostmarches and other cold regions, a Cloak of the Frozen Wastes
is more valuable than gold. It represents the difference between
survival and death during the harsh winters that dominate the northern
reaches.

**Current Location**

Cloaks of the Frozen Wastes exist in various northern communities,
particularly among those who trace their lineage to the ancient frost
giant alliance. They are occasionally found in the hordes of cold-based
creatures or in ancient northern ruins.

### 62.6 Items of Protection


#### Dragon-Warding Amulets


**Physical Description**

Small amulets made of dragonscale, each enchanted with protective wards.
The amulets glow faintly when dragons are near and grow warm in the
presence of dragon breath. Each is single-use but provides powerful
protection when needed most.

**History**

Dragon-Warding Amulets were crafted by Professor Miranda Questseeker
using scales donated by a brass dragon ally. They were created
specifically for the Unbound crisis when confronting Dragon Infernalix
became necessary.

**Powers**

While worn, the amulets enhance perception of dragons, provide
protection against breath weapons, and grant advantage against Frightful
Presence. Most importantly, a single amulet can absorb one dragon breath
weapon completely, though this destroys the amulet.

**Significance**

Dragon-Warding Amulets represent one of the few reliable defenses
against dragon attacks. During the Dragon Crisis, they saved numerous
lives. The crafting technique is known but requires dragon scales,
limiting production.

**Current Location**

Dragon-Warding Amulets were distributed during the Dragon Crisis. Some
remain with the heroes who carried them; others have been collected by
those preparing for future dragon encounters.

#### The Ring of Protection (Tirvandor Variant)


**Physical Description**

A platinum ring set with a small diamond that sparkles with inner light.
Inscribed inside the band is a prayer to Aethor, The Liberator. The ring
is warm to the touch, and the diamond glows faintly when undead
approach.

**History**

This particular Ring of Protection was worn by a Goldshore family priest
who drowned defending the manor during the Keeper Massacre. His spirit
remained with the ring as a wraith until defeated by those investigating
the manor's secrets. The ring retains his protective blessing.

**Powers**

The ring provides standard protection to its wearer. Additionally, it
glows when undead are within thirty feet. Most remarkably, if the wearer
suffers a mortal wound, the diamond shatters in a burst of radiant
energy that damages nearby enemies and automatically stabilizes the
wearer.

**Significance**

This ring represents the sacrifice of a priest who died protecting
others. The protective burst is a manifestation of his continuing desire
to shield the innocent, even after death. The ring becomes mundane after
this power activates, the priest's final blessing expended.

**Current Location**

Recovered from the sunken Goldshore Manor. Current holder depends on
campaign events.

### 62.7 Recognition and Honor Items


#### Monument Coins


**Physical Description**

Commemorative coins minted to honor particular heroes or events. Unlike
regular currency, Monument Coins bear the faces and names of those they
commemorate. Each is unique to its recipient and cannot be duplicated.

**History**

The tradition of Monument Coins began after the Dragon Crisis, when
coins bearing the faces of heroes who drove back the dragons were minted
and distributed. Since then, Monument Coins have been created for
various occasions, great victories, diplomatic achievements, and acts of
exceptional heroism.

**Powers**

Monument Coins have no magical power. Their value lies in what they
represent, proof that the bearer was present for or involved in the
commemorated event.

**Significance**

Possessing a Monument Coin marks the bearer as a hero recognized by the
realm. The coins cannot be purchased and are given only to those who
have earned them through genuine service. They are valuable as
collectors' items but far more valuable as proof of heroic deeds.

**Current Location**

Monument Coins are given as gifts to heroes at the conclusion of major
events. Recent coins were minted following the Dragon Crisis and the
peace established by the Blood & Coin campaign. Heroes who participated
in these events carry their coins as proof of their service.

*End of Chapter 57: Objects of Power*

## Chapter 63: Lost and Sought Items


Some of Tirvandor's most significant items remain lost, hidden,
forgotten, or waiting for worthy finders. These items are sought by
various factions for various reasons, and their recovery could change
the balance of power in the world.

### 63.1 Items Lost Beneath the Waves


#### The High King's Sword


**Last Known History**

The sword of the last High King was lost when the Worldrend split the
continents. King Aldric fell with his Palace of Eternal Spring, which
now rests somewhere beneath the Sundering Sea. The sword's location is
unknown but presumed to be within the sunken palace.

**Description**

A longsword of exceptional craftsmanship that glows in the presence of a
legitimate heir to the High Kingdom. The glow intensifies based on the
strength of the claim, and would blaze with full radiance for the true
heir.

**Why It Is Sought**

The High King's Sword could resolve the succession dispute between
Thaldros and Aethoria permanently. Whoever bears it and makes it glow
would have an undeniable claim to rule both continents. Both nations
sponsor expeditions to find it, and sabotage expeditions from the other
side.

**Dangers**

The Palace of Eternal Spring is deep beneath the Sundering Sea, guarded
by whatever creatures have made it their home over twelve centuries.
Pressure, darkness, and the remnants of ancient wards protect the sword.
Previous expeditions have failed without exception.

**Political Implications**

Some believe the sword should remain lost. Its recovery would not create
peace, it would create war, as both sides rejected any claim that
didn't favor them. Others believe only the sword can end the eternal
standoff.

#### The Crown of the Depths


**Last Known History**

The Crown of the Depths was the regalia of House Goldshore's main line,
allowing them to govern both surface and underwater territories. It was
lost when Goldshore Manor sank during the Keeper Massacre, presumably
still within the sunken structure.

**Description**

A platinum crown set with blue-green pearls and aquamarines, styled to
resemble cresting waves. The crown grants water breathing, swimming
speed, control over water, and authority over aquatic creatures.

**Why It Is Sought**

The Crown of the Depths would grant its wearer significant power in
coastal and maritime affairs. It would also prove the legitimacy of any
Goldshore heir who recovered it, relevant to those investigating the
truth about the Keeper Massacre.

**Dangers**

Goldshore Manor is underwater and haunted by the spirits of those who
died in the massacre. The secrets the Goldshores were keeping make the
location dangerous in ways beyond mere ghosts.

**Current Status**

The crown may have been recovered during the Shattered Oaths campaign
events. Its current holder and status depend on those events'
resolution.

### 63.2 Items of Ancient Evil


#### The Everice Heart


**Last Known History**

The Everice Heart is an artifact that could freeze entire kingdoms,
sought by the ice necromancer Gelidus Frostbone. Its location is
unknown, but legends place it somewhere in the deepest glaciers of the
northern Frostmarches.

**Description**

A fist-sized crystal of primordial ice that never melts and radiates
cold capable of killing the unprepared. Those who touch it become frozen
from within; those who wield it gain control over winter itself.

**Why It Is Sought**

Gelidus Frostbone believes the Everice Heart would allow him to create a
frozen kingdom of perfectly preserved undead, a realm of eternal winter
where death and cold become one. Others seek it to prevent this
catastrophe.

**Dangers**

The Everice Heart is hidden in glacial depths guarded by ancient ice
creatures. The cold alone would kill most seekers. And if found, the
artifact itself is dangerous to handle, its power can overwhelm even
those who believe themselves its masters.

**Political Implications**

If the Everice Heart were recovered by the wrong hands, it could
threaten not just the north but the entire world. The artifact
represents a potential extinction-level threat.

### 63.3 Items of the Pre-Worldrend Era


#### Fragments of the Worldrend


**Last Known History**

When the World-Splitter was activated and the continents were torn
apart, pieces of the artifact scattered across the world. These
fragments, distinct from the Components, are smaller pieces that retain
traces of the original power.

**Description**

Small crystalline shards that shimmer with reality-bending energy. Each
fragment allows minor manipulation of local reality, useful but
dangerous. Prolonged exposure causes mental instability.

**Why They Are Sought**

Scholars seek the fragments to understand what happened during the
Worldrend. Mages seek them for their power. The Unbound may be
collecting them as part of Lord Shadows' plans.

**Dangers**

The fragments are inherently unstable. Reality warps around them,
creating localized anomalies. Those who carry them too long begin seeing
impossible things, other timelines, possible futures, alternate versions
of themselves.

**Current Locations**

Fragments have been reported in various locations, ancient ruins,
magical nexuses, the sites of reality anomalies. No complete survey
exists; new fragments are occasionally discovered.

#### The Obsidian Keystone


**Last Known History**

The Obsidian Keystone controls seals on ancient volcanic threats, bound
fire elementals, imprisoned fire giants, or something worse. Its
location is unknown, but it is believed to be somewhere near Ashfall or
the volcanic regions of southern Thaldros.

**Description**

A key-shaped stone of pure obsidian that radiates heat. The keystone can
open or close volcanic seals, releasing or binding whatever lies
beneath.

**Why It Is Sought**

Those who control the keystone control what lies beneath the volcanoes.
This could mean an army of fire elementals, imprisoned fire giant kings,
or access to ancient volcanic forges capable of creating legendary
weapons.

**Dangers**

The keystone is hidden in volcanic regions where heat, toxic gases, and
fire creatures make exploration deadly. And whatever the keystone seals
was imprisoned for a reason, releasing it could be catastrophic.

**Political Implications**

House Ashborne and other desert powers would pay handsomely for the
keystone. Control over volcanic threats could shift the balance of power
in the southern regions dramatically.

### 63.4 Items of Legendary Heroes


#### Mercy's Edge


**Last Known History**

The sword blessed by all Seven Ascended was lost approximately two
centuries ago during a battle with dragon cultists in the Contested
Lands. The exact location is unknown, the battle was chaotic, and
survivors couldn't agree on where the sword fell.

**Description**

A longsword that glows with divine light, bearing the blessings of all
Seven Ascended. It grants immunity to fear, effectiveness against undead
and fiends, and protection from corruption. The sword judges its
wielders, only the worthy can lift it.

**Why It Is Sought**

Mercy's Edge appearing would be seen as a divine sign. The worthy
wielder would command respect from all faithful and would have access to
one of the most powerful weapons ever created.

**Dangers**

The Contested Lands are dangerous, a lawless region between the
continents where anything might lurk. The sword's last battle was
against dragon cultists, and their descendants may still guard the area.
And the sword itself might not accept just anyone.

**Religious Implications**

If Mercy's Edge were recovered, the churches of all Seven Ascended
would have opinions about who should wield it. The sword's reappearance
would likely trigger theological debates and political maneuvering.

### 63.5 Items Hidden by Design


#### The Hidden Component Vaults


**Nature of the Hidden Items**

The five World-Splitter Components were deliberately hidden after the
Worldrend, each entrusted to a guardian family who would protect it
across generations. The locations were known only to the guardians, and
when House Blackwood was destroyed, some of that knowledge was lost.

**Why They Are Sought**

Lord Shadows seeks the Components to reunite the World-Splitter. Others
seek them to prevent this. Some scholars simply want to study them. And
some believe the Components could be used for purposes other than
destruction.

**Current Status**

As of the campaign events:

-   The First Component (Shadow Shard) is in Lord Shadows' possession

-   The Second Component (Flame Heart) was with House Goldshore (now
    destroyed)

-   The Third Component (Stone Crown) is hidden in the Iron Crown of
    Thaldros

-   The Fourth Component (Star Prism) was in the Temple of Echoes

-   The Fifth Component (Blood Vessel) is carried unknowingly by General
    Marcus Vale

The hunt for these Components drives much of the conflict in the
Shattered Oaths campaign.

*End of Chapter 58: Lost and Sought Items*

# Part X: Stories & Narratives

## Chapter 64: The Blackwood Conspiracy (Shattered Oaths™ Campaign)


### 64.1 Campaign Overview


The Shattered Oaths campaign is fundamentally a tragedy---a story about
what happens when a victim of terrible injustice seeks justice through
catastrophic means, and heroes must choose between protecting a corrupt
system or allowing apocalyptic vengeance.

**The Central Question:** How do you stop a villain who is also a
victim? How do you protect a system built on murder and lies?

**Core Themes:**

-   **Oaths and Obligations:** What happens when oaths conflict? When
    duty to country means protecting injustice?

-   **Truth vs. Stability:** Is comfortable falsehood better than
    destructive truth?

-   **Victim and Villain:** Corvus Blackwood's cause is just; his
    methods are monstrous

-   **Justice vs. Vengeance:** They look similar from outside---the
    difference is in the aftermath

### 64.2 The Premise


Forty-three years before the campaign begins, House Blackwood was
destroyed. Official history claims they were traitors who attempted to
trigger a Second Worldrend. This history is a lie.

In truth, House Blackwood were guardians. For generations, they
protected one component of the World-Splitter---a Primordial artifact of
unimaginable power split into five pieces after the original Worldrend.
Five noble houses were entrusted to keep them separated forever. The
Blackwoods guarded the First Component, the Shadow Shard, in vaults
beneath their ancestral fortress, Raven's Keep.

The conspiracy began when Prince Aldric, eldest son of King Aldric III,
discovered another Component---the Flame Heart---hidden beneath the
capital. The Goldshore Keepers, a secret branch of House Goldshore, were
its guardians. Prince Aldric wanted the artifact for himself, to sell to
dragon cults for personal power. When the Keepers refused, he murdered
them all---men, women, and children---in a single night.

King Aldric III faced a choice: execute his son for genocide, or find a
scapegoat. He chose his son over justice. Royal soldiers attacked
Raven's Keep at night, burned the estate, and slaughtered the entire
Blackwood family---declaring them traitors.

One person survived: Corvus Blackwood, twelve years old, hidden in a
barrel in the wine cellar. He listened to his family die. Smelled their
flesh burning. When silence came, he crawled out to find everything
gone. Everyone dead.

For forty-three years, Corvus prepared his revenge. He became "Lord
Shadows," founded the Unbound---an organization of those wronged by the
kingdoms---and began hunting for all five Components of the
World-Splitter. His goal: assemble the artifact and use its power to
tear down the corrupt kingdoms, force them to admit the truth, and
reshape society.

### 64.3 Act One: Shadows in Silverpine


The campaign opens in Silverpine, where strange disappearances plague
the town. The heroes investigate, discovering Unbound cult activity and
black raven tokens bearing the extinct House Blackwood crest.

**Key Events:**

-   Rescue of kidnapped villagers from the Thornwood shrine.

-   Discovery of the Shadowmark conspiracy within Silverpine itself.

-   Confrontation with Unbound operatives at the old mill.

-   Journey through dangerous territory to Raven's Keep.

-   First encounter with the legacy of House Blackwood.

**Key Revelations:**

-   The Unbound believe themselves righteous---fighting against genuine
    injustice.

-   Lord Shadows is the last Blackwood heir.

-   The World-Splitter Components exist and can reshape reality.

-   Something called "the awakening" is planned.

**The Raven's Keep Assault:** The heroes infiltrate the ruined
Blackwood fortress, now an armed Unbound camp. In the Courtyard of
Ravens, they discover a note written by twelve-year-old Corvus: "They
say we're traitors. They're lying."

In the vault, they finally encounter Lord Shadows Blackwood himself. He
offers them a choice: help him, oppose him, or let him go. Whatever they
choose, Act One ends with the heroes understanding that this is not a
simple cult---it's a conspiracy touching the foundations of
civilization itself.

### 64.4 Act Two: The Conspiracy Unveiled


A mysterious letter summons the heroes to the capital, where access to
the Black Archive---a secret library beneath the royal palace---reveals
the full truth. They meet Arcturus, the legendary High Mage who should
have died three thousand years ago, now a ghost bound to the archive.

**The Black Archive Revelation:** Arcturus confirms everything:

-   The Blackwoods were innocent guardians.

-   King Aldric III murdered them to cover Prince Aldric's crimes.

-   The World-Splitter Components are Primordial artifacts predating the
    gods.

-   Lord Shadows intends to awaken Dragon Infernalix to reach the Second
    Component.

**The Dragon Heist:** The heroes must infiltrate the lair of Dragon
Infernalix---an ancient red dragon sleeping beneath the capital---to
retrieve the Flame Heart before the Unbound can claim it.

**Key Events:**

-   Gathering allies: Professor Miranda Questseeker, Master Hunter Kael
    Dragonsbane, Captain Thalia Lightbringer, Druid Elder Silvaris.

-   The descent through Primordial ruins older than gods.

-   The heist: crossing the dragon's hoard, extracting the Component.

-   The Unbound assault---three-way battle as the dragon awakens.

-   Dragon Infernalix erupts from beneath the palace, devastating three
    city blocks.

**The Truth Revealed:** The confrontation with Corvus comes at last. He
removes his mask---no more Lord Shadows, just a man, fifty-five years
old, gray-haired, scarred, exhausted.

*"I was twelve years old when King Aldric III murdered my family. I
don't want revenge. I want TRUTH. I want justice. I want the kingdoms
to ANSWER for what they did."*

**The Defining Moral Choice:**

-   **Join Corvus:** Accept his cause, help gather the remaining
    Components, use the World-Splitter to reshape the world.

-   **Oppose Corvus:** Refuse his offer, fight him, protect the corrupt
    system to prevent catastrophic cure.

-   **The Middle Path:** Convince Corvus there's another way---expose
    the conspiracy through evidence and diplomacy.

### 64.5 Act Three: The Second Worldrend


**The Third Component:** The Void Fragment lies beneath the Sundering
Sea, in the ruins of Goldshore Manor---the Goldshore Keepers' secret
sanctuary that sank forty-three years ago. The heroes must navigate the
drowned halls, facing deep-sea predators and the ghost of Lady Corvina
Goldshore herself.

*"My family died screaming. Prince Aldric murdered us all. Tell me:
what will you do with the Component?"*

**The Assembly:** With three Components in hand (or in opposition), the
heroes must decide their fate:

-   **Destroy them** (requires divine intervention)

-   **Hide them separately** (repeat history)

-   **Give to the Temple** (trust divine custody)

-   **Give to the Crown** (trust reformed authority)

-   **Keep them** (become new guardians)

-   **Assemble them** (harness the power---dangerous)

**The Primordial Rift:** The final confrontation takes place at the site
of the original Worldrend---a massive canyon where reality was torn
three thousand years ago. Time moves wrong. Gravity fluctuates. The
Unbound army surrounds the Assembly Site, five pedestals waiting for
five Components.

**Corvus' Final Plea:**

*"I was twelve years old when they came. I watched my mother die
screaming. For forty-three years, I've lived with that. Please. I'm so
tired of being the villain. Just once\... let me be the hero of my own
story."*

If the heroes cannot persuade him to stand down, the World-Splitter
begins to assemble. They have six rounds to stop activation before the
Second Worldrend becomes unstoppable.

### 64.6 The Four Endings


**Ending 1: Heroic Victory (Traditional Ending)**

The heroes stop the World-Splitter. Corvus falls---defeated, captured,
or slain. The Components are secured.

At the royal court, the heroes present Corvus' evidence. King Aldric IV,
inheritor of his father's crimes, asks: "What would you have me do?
The kingdom is yours to reshape."

**The Great Choice:**

-   **Full Public Revelation:** Political crisis, riots, eventual
    reform. The Blackwood Memorial rises in the capital square. Truth
    commissions address historical injustices.

-   **Private Justice:** Quiet reform, truth acknowledged behind closed
    doors. Hidden justice---perhaps the only kind possible.

-   **Revolutionary Change:** Nobility abolished. Three months of
    violence, then the Republic of Tirvandor emerges.

-   **The Cover-Up:** Bury the truth again. Heroes become complicit.
    Peace, but at what cost?

**Ending 2: Revolutionary Victory (Heroes Joined Corvus)**

The heroes helped Corvus reshape the world through controlled
transformation. The World-Splitter activated, but guided, precise.
Corrupt systems unmade. Unjust laws erased.

The first year brings chaos as the old order collapses. Five years
later, the New Tirvandor is complicated---better in many ways, but
messier. New forms of corruption emerge.

*Corvus at Sixty: "I spend my life fighting to unmake kings. And now I
realize: I became one. A benevolent tyrant is still a tyrant."*

**Ending 3: Redemption Ending (Peaceful Resolution)**

The heroes convinced Corvus to stand down through words alone. He steps
back from the Components, weeping: "I've become what I hated. My
mother would be ashamed."

**The Reconciliation:** One month later, Corvus stands before the Truth
and Reconciliation Commission. He testifies for three days---everything.
His crimes. His evidence. He hides nothing.

**The Sentence:** Twenty years of service. He will work to undo the
damage he caused, help reform the systems he rebelled against.

**Twenty Years Later:** Freedom earned. Thousands attend his pardon
ceremony. "I don't deserve this. But I can try. Every day, I can try
to be the man my mother hoped I'd become."

**Ending 4: Tragic Ending (The Second Worldrend Succeeds)**

The heroes failed. The World-Splitter completed. Reality tore---not
controlled, but raw, cataclysmic. Mountains crumbled. Seas boiled. Tens
of thousands died in the initial event.

*Corvus' Horror: "What have I done? WHAT HAVE I DONE?"*

The campaign transforms from "save the world" to "survive the broken
world." The heroes become wardens of survival itself.

**Thirty Years Later:** Life goes on. The Shattered World is dangerous
but livable. New generations don't remember united Tirvandor. *"Could
you have stopped it?" someone asks. "Maybe. Sometimes heroes fail. The
question isn't whether we failed. It's what we did after."*

### 64.7 Corvus Blackwood: The Tragic Antagonist

![64.7 Corvus Blackwood: The Tragic Antagonist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mixologee/tirvandor/main/tirvandor-project/all_artwork/npcs/villain-corvus-blackwood.jpg){width:200px,float:right,margin:5px}


**The Boy:** Corvus was the youngest of four Blackwood children, twelve
years old when the soldiers came. His sisters Elara and Mira were kind
and beautiful. His brother Aldric was brave. His parents were the best
people he ever knew.

The night his world ended, a servant hid young Corvus in a wine barrel.
He listened to his family die. When silence came, he crawled out to find
ashes and bodies.

**The Man:** Forty-three years transformed the frightened boy into Lord
Shadows---master assassin, spymaster, revolutionary leader. He built the
Unbound from those the kingdoms wronged.

*"I'm not a villain. I'm an accountant, and the bill is due."*

**The Tragedy:** Corvus is right about almost everything. His family WAS
innocent. The Crown DID commit genocide. The system IS corrupt. His
cause IS just.

But his solution---triggering the Second Worldrend---would kill
millions. Somewhere deep inside, the twelve-year-old boy who just wanted
his parents back screams that this is wrong. That his mother would be
ashamed.

If the heroes reach that boy, they might save both Corvus and the world.
If they can't, they'll have to destroy a victim to stop a villain.
Either way, they'll never forget him.

### 64.8 Campaign Significance


The Shattered Oaths campaign reveals the dark foundations beneath
Thaldros' gilded surface. The kingdom presents itself as a beacon of
civilization. In truth, it was built on a lie---the genocide of innocent
people to cover a prince's crimes.

Whatever ending the heroes achieve, Tirvandor is changed. The question
is whether that change comes through reform or catastrophe, truth or
continued lies, justice or vengeance.

*"Sometimes heroes fail. Sometimes the world breaks despite your best
efforts. The question isn't whether we failed. It's what we did
after."*

## Chapter 65: The Revolutionary's Gambit (Blood & Coin™ Campaign)


### 65.1 Campaign Overview


**Tagline:** "You're not heroes. You're professionals."

Blood & Coin is a morally gray campaign set in western Thaldros during a
proxy war funded by the Aethorian Republic. Players begin as sellswords
in Crossroads, a lawless mercenary town, and rise through increasingly
complex moral dilemmas to become power players who shape the fate of
nations.

The campaign occurs simultaneously with Shattered Oaths---while Corvus
Blackwood's conspiracy unfolds in central Thaldros, Blood & Coin
follows his western operations and the larger political war.

**Central Question:** In a world where everyone lies, every choice has
costs, and survival demands compromise---what are you willing to become
to survive? And what lines will you never cross?

**Core Themes:**

-   Moral Ambiguity: No clear heroes or villains; every faction has
    valid arguments and hidden corruptions.

-   Consequences: Every choice creates allies and enemies, rippling
    throughout the campaign.

-   Professional Ethics: The mercenary's code---contracts are sacred,
    reputation is everything.

-   Revolution vs. Order: Monarchy, democracy, and apocalyptic
    transformation each claim to offer salvation.

-   Profit vs. Principle: Gold buys survival; principles cost
    everything.

### 65.2 The Premise


**The Setting:** Crossroads sits at the intersection of three trade
routes in western Thaldros, far from royal oversight. No official
government exists---the Iron Guild runs everything through contracts and
reputation. Violence is common but regulated. Murder requires a
contract. Theft is punishable by death (bad for business). Lying is
expected; getting caught is fatal.

**Three Laws of Crossroads:**

1\. Contracts are sacred---break your word, die

2\. Don't kill clients before they pay---bad for business

3\. Survive first, moralize later---idealism gets you killed

**The Western Conflict:** While Crossroads operates outside Crown
authority, war brews around it. The Aethorian Republic---across the
Sundering Sea---funds, arms, and advises separatist movements in
Thaldros' frontier territories. These rebels fight for Aethorian-style
democracy against Crown rule. This is not a continental invasion but a
civil war with foreign backing.

### 65.3 Act One: Blood for Coin


**The Arrival:** Protagonists arrive in Crossroads as aspiring
mercenaries, each with their own reasons---exile, desperation,
pragmatism---but all seeking work, coin, survival. Varak Ironfist, the
dwarven veteran who runs the Iron Guild, offers membership if they can
complete their first contracts.

**The First Lesson (Quest 1.1):** *Clients lie. Always.* Three contracts
reveal this truth:

The Rat Problem: A shopkeeper wants "rats" cleared---the rats turn out
to be thugs protecting his smuggling operation.

Debt Collection: A loan shark wants 125 gold collected from a carpenter
who borrowed money to save his dying daughter. The carpenter can't pay.
His seven-year-old daughter draws pictures while her father begs for
mercy. Choices include brutality, mercy, sacrifice, deception, or
vigilantism.

Caravan Guard: Simple cargo run becomes complicated when the cargo is
contraband weapons. When Crown officers stop the caravan, players must
choose between law, contract, and conscience.

**The Price of Loyalty (Quest 1.2):** Two clients arrive simultaneously
wanting mercenaries for the same target---but with opposite goals. Baron
Darius Thornhill wants his daughter Elara retrieved; he claims she was
kidnapped by a common merchant. Thomas Redwood tells a different story:
Elara chose to leave. They're in love. The Baron was forcing her into
an arranged marriage.

Investigation reveals the truth: Elara left willingly. She's an adult
making her own choice. Thomas is genuine. The Baron loves his daughter
but in a controlling way. No one is lying---they simply have
irreconcilable values.

Players must choose a client, knowing the other will hire different
mercenaries---and they'll likely fight over this woman's fate.
Varak's lesson: "Every choice makes enemies. There's no 'good'
answer in this business. Only choices and consequences."

**Blood Money (Quest 1.3):** The Merchant Consortium offers 500 gold to
eliminate "Red Wolf," a bandit leader terrorizing trade routes.
Investigation reveals the truth: Ten years ago, Lord Thornwood died in a
suspicious "hunting accident." His heir faced massive forged debts.
Courts ruled against her---judges had been bribed. The "Red Wolf" is
Elara Thornwood, returned to reclaim what was stolen. She only targets
Consortium goods. She gives what she takes to starving peasants. The
Consortium wants her dead before she can expose their conspiracy.

**The Black Ledger (Quest 1.4):** The Iron Guild reveals its true
purpose: gathering intelligence on Consortium corruption. Lord Pembroke
keeps a ledger documenting every bribe, forged deed, and "disappeared"
witness. The heist reveals evidence of systematic corruption---but also
that another thief, Whisper, is after the same prize. Potential ally or
rival.

**The Trial (Quest 1.5):** Marcus Blackwood, a refugee leader, is
arrested on trumped-up charges. The real reason: he uncovered evidence
linking the Consortium to land fraud. Secret: Marcus Blackwood is Corvus
Blackwood's younger brother---the "Lost Heir" hidden as an infant
when their family was destroyed. Players have three days to investigate,
gather allies, and defend an innocent man against corruption.

### 65.4 Act Two: Power Plays


**Six Months Later:** Reputation has spread across both kingdoms. War
escalates. Three factions simultaneously contact the protagonists.

**The Recruiters (Quest 2.1):** Three meetings, three offers, three
versions of salvation:

Commander Helena Dawnblade (Thaldros Crown) offers military commission,
wealth, authority. "Order is worth defending, even when order is
imperfect." What she doesn't mention: Scapegoat Protocol---when war
ends, mercenaries will be arrested, tried for war crimes, and executed.

Envoy Marcus Valen (Aethorian Republic) offers democratic ideals.
"Democracy is loud, chaotic, inefficient. But it's OURS." What he
doesn't mention: Senate leadership plans "temporary dictatorship"
after victory.

Corvus Blackwood (The Unbound) offers apocalyptic transformation. "With
the World-Splitter Components, I can end war, poverty, suffering. Create
a perfect world." What he doesn't mention: Activation will kill 30-40%
of the world's population. Survivors will lose free will.

**The First Mission (Quest 2.2):** Each faction demands proof of loyalty
through morally compromising missions. Thaldros: Destroy a supply convoy
carrying medicine for civilian refugees. Aethoria: Extract a war
criminal defector who has valuable intelligence. Unbound: Steal an
artifact from peaceful monks who'll die defending it.

**The Double Cross (Quest 2.3):** An informant within each faction
reveals devastating documents proving employer treachery. Thaldros is
setting up mercenaries as scapegoats. Aethoria's democracy was always a
tool for oligarchy. Corvus' "salvation" means genocide and mind
control. Confrontations force choices: Stay loyal despite betrayal?
Switch sides? Go independent?

**The Heist (Quest 2.4):** Everyone wants into the Royal Vault of Kaer
Thandros---military intelligence, World-Splitter Component #4, gold
beyond measure. Multiple heist teams converge. The crucial discovery:
correspondence between Thaldros high command and Aethorian military
leadership, dated three years ago---before the war started:

*"War serves both our interests. Thaldros consolidates power through
emergency measures. Aethoria senate suspends elections. We both win."*

The War Was Manufactured. Coordinated by both kingdoms for political
gain. Real casualties, fake justification.

**The Breaking Point (Quest 2.5):** Two months later, both armies stand
at the Border of Judgment. Five Possible Outcomes:

Thaldros Victory: Help Crown forces crush the rebellion. Democracy dies.
Players become heroes of tyranny.

Aethoria Victory: Help rebels defeat the monarchy. Freedom through
blood. But the kingdom fragments into chaos.

Unbound Apocalypse: Help Corvus complete the ritual. 35% of world
population dies. Survivors lose free will. Perfect order, zero freedom.

Peace Achieved: Expose the war conspiracy publicly. Force both kingdoms
to negotiate. The hardest path---but no one else dies.

Total War: Stalemate. Neither side wins. War continues indefinitely.

### 65.5 Act Three: The Long Peace (Peace Path Example)


**One Year Later:** The Treaty of Judgment Border holds---barely.
Players are official Peacekeepers, neutral mediators appointed by both
kingdoms.

**The Peacekeepers (Quest 3.1):** Three crises threaten to reignite war
simultaneously. Investigation reveals someone is coordinating all
attacks on the peace.

**The Underground (Quest 3.2):** A network of extremists from both
kingdoms opposes peace. Their leader, "The Prophet," was a decorated
soldier who lost everything in the manufactured war. "Peace is
surrender. Peace is accepting that everyone who died, died for
nothing."

**The Alliance (Quest 3.3):** From the frozen north comes the
Dreadhost---10,000 undead led by the Dread King, a lich who conquered
death 400 years ago. Both kingdoms must ally against this threat---the
first true test of their fragile peace. Decapitation strike required:
small team infiltrates enemy lines, kills the Dread King directly.

**The Unification (Quest 3.4):** The Dread King has a
phylactery---he'll reform unless it's destroyed. Players journey to
his Frozen Kingdom and destroy his crown-phylactery in the final battle.
After victory, both kingdoms owe everything to the Peacekeepers. They
can request wealth---or something greater: Unification. Thaldros and
Aethoria become the United Realm of Tirvandor.

**The Mediator's Rest (Quest 3.5):** One year after unification. Every
major survivor gathers. The question: What happens to the Peacekeepers?

### 65.6 The Four Campaign Endings


**Eternal Vigil:** Continue as Peacekeepers forever. Years pass.
Decades. Players mediate disputes, prevent conflicts, train new
generations. Eventually, one by one, they fall. Legacy: You gave
everything. The peace held because YOU held it.

**The Institution:** Train successors. Build an organization that
continues after you're gone. The Peacekeeper Order becomes institution.
Legacy: You built something that outlasts you.

**Retirement:** Walk away. Let the world handle itself. Legacy: You
proved that heroes can stop. That saving the world doesn't have to
consume you.

**Alternate Outcomes:** Revolutionary Victory (Aethoria), Imperial
Victory (Thaldros), Apocalyptic Victory (Unbound), and Endless War
(Stalemate) each create vastly different futures for Tirvandor.

### 65.7 Major Character Arcs


**Varak Ironfist:** The Iron Guild master begins as a pragmatic mentor
teaching survival through moral flexibility. But he was once idealistic.
Across the campaign, players may restore his faith---or confirm his
cynicism.

**Commander Helena Dawnblade:** Represents order's seduction and cost.
Honorable, competent, sincere---and will follow orders she knows are
wrong. Her arc forces confrontation between duty and conscience.

**Envoy Marcus Valen:** Represents idealism's limitations. Genuinely
believes in democracy---and has compromised those beliefs to "protect"
them. His arc explores whether ideals survive contact with power.

**Corvus Blackwood:** The visionary extremist connecting both campaigns.
In Blood & Coin, he presents as a scholarly recruiter. His true
nature---master assassin, grieving child grown into something
terrible---emerges gradually.

**Marcus Blackwood:** Corvus' younger brother represents what the
Blackwood line could have become without trauma. Justice sought through
systems rather than apocalypse. Perhaps the only person who can talk
Corvus down.

### 65.8 Campaign Significance


Blood & Coin represents a narrative where "hero" isn't a character
class but a choice made repeatedly under pressure. The protagonists
begin as professionals seeking survival and end as legends who shaped
history. But they didn't become heroes by following a predetermined
path---they became heroes by choosing, repeatedly, to do more than
survive.

The campaign's genius lies in making those choices genuinely difficult.
Every faction offers valid arguments. Every path has costs. Every
decision creates enemies. What exists is agency---the power to decide
what kind of person you are, and then becoming that person through
action.

*You're not heroes. You're professionals. But professionals can choose
to be heroes. That's the difference between surviving and living.*
